theorem id_eq_chi_sum_c (n k : TauIdx) :
    id_stage.c_fun n k = chi_plus_stage.c_fun n k + chi_minus_stage.c_fun n k := by
  simp [id_stage, chi_plus_stage, chi_minus_stage]
#eval agree_at_check chi_plus_stage chi_plus_stage 42 3   -- true (self)
#eval agree_at_check chi_plus_stage chi_minus_stage 1 1   -- false (different)
#eval agree_at_check id_stage id_stage 100 5              -- true

#eval agree_at_check chi_plus_stage id_stage 3 2   -- false: B agrees but C differs

end Tau.Holomorphy
doc_comment: -- Identity theorem witness: chi_plus and id disagree at stage 2 for n=3

name: PrimorialPresheaf
source_excerpt:
structure PrimorialPresheaf where
  value_at : TauIdx → TauIdx
  compatible : ∀ k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l → reduce (value_at l) k = value_at k
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D83] An element of the primorial presheaf lim← ℤ/M_dℤ:
    a compatible family of values at each primorial depth.
    Compatibility: reduce(value_at ℓ, k) = value_at k for k ≤ ℓ. -/

name: presheaf_of_nat
source_excerpt:
def presheaf_of_nat (n : TauIdx) : PrimorialPresheaf where
  value_at := fun d => reduce n d
  compatible := fun _ _ hkl => reduction_compat n hkl
doc_comment:
/-- Construct a presheaf element from a natural number:
    at each depth d, the value is reduce(n, d) = n mod M_d. -/

name: presheaf_value_reduced
source_excerpt:
theorem presheaf_value_reduced (p : PrimorialPresheaf) (d : TauIdx) :
    reduce (p.value_at d) d = p.value_at d :=
  p.compatible d d (Nat.le_refl d)
doc_comment: /-- Presheaf values are already reduced at their own depth. -/

name: IsNatTrans
source_excerpt: def IsNatTrans (f : StageFun) : Prop := TowerCoherent f
doc_comment:
/-- A natural transformation F → F_j in the primorial inverse system.
    This IS tower coherence (I.D46), repackaged in presheaf language. -/

name: nat_trans_iff_tower_coherent
source_excerpt:
theorem nat_trans_iff_tower_coherent (f : StageFun) :
    IsNatTrans f ↔ TowerCoherent f := Iff.rfl
doc_comment: /-- Presheaf naturality and tower coherence are definitionally equal. -/

name: presheaf_characterization
source_excerpt:
theorem presheaf_characterization (hf : HolFun) :
    IsNatTrans hf.transformer.stage_fun :=
  hf.coherent
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T40] Every τ-holomorphic function is a natural transformation
    of the primorial presheaf. -/

name: nat_trans_gives_holfun
source_excerpt:
theorem nat_trans_gives_holfun (sf : SectorFun) (stf : StageFun) (d : Nat)
    (hnt : IsNatTrans stf) :
    ∃ hf : HolFun, hf.transformer.stage_fun = stf :=
  ⟨⟨⟨sf, stf, d⟩, hnt⟩, rfl⟩
doc_comment: /-- Converse: a natural transformation with sector structure gives a HolFun. -/

name: BiSquare
source_excerpt:
structure BiSquare where
  stage_fun : StageFun
  /-- LEFT SQUARE, B-sector: reduce(B_ℓ(n), k) = B_k(n). -/
  left_b : ∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l →
    reduce (stage_fun.b_fun n l) k = stage_fun.b_fun n k
  /-- LEFT SQUARE, C-sector: reduce(C_ℓ(n), k) = C_k(n). -/
  left_c : ∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l →
    reduce (stage_fun.c_fun n l) k = stage_fun.c_fun n k
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T41] The holomorphy bi-square: the minimal complete
    characterization of τ-holomorphic functions.

    Left square: tower coherence for each sector.
    The right square (spectral naturality) follows automatically
    from left_b and left_c — see `right_from_left`. -/

name: BiSquare.tower_coherent
source_excerpt:
def BiSquare.tower_coherent (bs : BiSquare) : TowerCoherent bs.stage_fun :=
  ⟨bs.left_b, bs.left_c⟩
doc_comment: /-- Extract tower coherence from a BiSquare. -/

name: BiSquare.of_coherent
source_excerpt:
def BiSquare.of_coherent (f : StageFun) (htc : TowerCoherent f) : BiSquare :=
  ⟨f, htc.1, htc.2⟩
doc_comment: /-- Construct a BiSquare from a tower-coherent StageFun. -/

name: bi_square_characterization
source_excerpt:
theorem bi_square_characterization (f : StageFun) :
    TowerCoherent f ↔
    (∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l → reduce (f.b_fun n l) k = f.b_fun n k) ∧
    (∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l → reduce (f.c_fun n l) k = f.c_fun n k) :=
  Iff.rfl
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T41] The bi-square characterizes τ-holomorphy completely:
    TowerCoherent f ↔ both sectors of the left square commute. -/

name: BiSquare.toHolFun
source_excerpt:
def BiSquare.toHolFun (bs : BiSquare) (sf : SectorFun) (d : Nat) : HolFun :=
  ⟨⟨sf, bs.stage_fun, d⟩, bs.tower_coherent⟩
doc_comment: /-- Bridge: BiSquare → HolFun (with a chosen SectorFun and depth). -/

name: HolFun.toBiSquare
source_excerpt:
def HolFun.toBiSquare (hf : HolFun) : BiSquare :=
  ⟨hf.transformer.stage_fun, hf.coherent.1, hf.coherent.2⟩
doc_comment: /-- Bridge: HolFun → BiSquare. -/

name: holfun_bisquare_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem holfun_bisquare_roundtrip (hf : HolFun) :
    hf.toBiSquare.stage_fun = hf.transformer.stage_fun := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip preserves the StageFun. -/

name: spectral_coeff_ext
source_excerpt:
private theorem spectral_coeff_ext {s₁ s₂ : SpectralCoeff}
    (hb : s₁.b_coeff = s₂.b_coeff) (hc : s₁.c_coeff = s₂.c_coeff) :
    s₁ = s₂ := by
  cases s₁; cases s₂; simp_all
doc_comment: /-- SpectralCoeff extensionality (local helper). -/

name: right_from_left
source_excerpt:
theorem right_from_left (bs : BiSquare) (n k l : TauIdx) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    spectral_of bs.stage_fun n k =
    ⟨reduce (spectral_of bs.stage_fun n l).b_coeff k,
     reduce (spectral_of bs.stage_fun n l).c_coeff k⟩ := by
  apply spectral_coeff_ext
  · -- b_coeff: f.b(n, k) = reduce(f.b(n, l), k)
    show bs.stage_fun.b_fun n k = reduce (bs.stage_fun.b_fun n l) k
    exact (bs.left_b n k l hkl).symm
  · -- c_coeff: f.c(n, k) = reduce(f.c(n, l), k)
    show bs.stage_fun.c_fun n k = reduce (bs.stage_fun.c_fun n l) k
    exact (bs.left_c n k l hkl).symm
doc_comment:
/-- **Key insight.** The right square (spectral naturality) follows
    automatically from the left square (tower coherence).

    Because `spectral_of f n k = ⟨f.b_fun n k, f.c_fun n k⟩`,
    spectral reduction IS sector-wise tower coherence.
    The two squares are independent in the LaTeX presentation
    but are the same condition in TauLib's concrete formulation. -/

name: right_from_left'
source_excerpt:
theorem right_from_left' (f : StageFun) (htc : TowerCoherent f)
    (n k l : TauIdx) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    spectral_of f n k =
    ⟨reduce (spectral_of f n l).b_coeff k,
     reduce (spectral_of f n l).c_coeff k⟩ :=
  right_from_left (BiSquare.of_coherent f htc) n k l hkl
doc_comment: /-- Right square for any tower-coherent function (not just BiSquare). -/

name: limit_determines_stages
source_excerpt:
theorem limit_determines_stages (bs₁ bs₂ : BiSquare)
    (d₀ : TauIdx)
    (h : ∀ n, agree_at bs₁.stage_fun bs₂.stage_fun n d₀) :
    ∀ n k, k ≤ d₀ → agree_at bs₁.stage_fun bs₂.stage_fun n k :=
  tau_identity_nat bs₁.stage_fun bs₂.stage_fun
    bs₁.tower_coherent bs₂.tower_coherent d₀ h
doc_comment:
/-- The limit principle: the limit row determines every stage row.
    Global Hartogs (I.T31) in bi-square language. -/

name: limit_determines_spectral
source_excerpt:
theorem limit_determines_spectral (bs₁ bs₂ : BiSquare)
    (d₀ : TauIdx)
    (h : ∀ n, spectral_of bs₁.stage_fun n d₀ = spectral_of bs₂.stage_fun n d₀) :
    ∀ n k, k ≤ d₀ →
    spectral_of bs₁.stage_fun n k = spectral_of bs₂.stage_fun n k := by
  intro n k hk
  have ha := limit_determines_stages bs₁ bs₂ d₀
    (fun n => spectral_eq_implies_agree _ _ n d₀ (h n)) n k hk
  exact spectral_coeff_ext ha.1 ha.2
doc_comment: /-- Limit principle in spectral language. -/

name: chi_plus_bisquare
source_excerpt:
def chi_plus_bisquare : BiSquare :=
  BiSquare.of_coherent chi_plus_stage chi_plus_coherent
doc_comment: /-- χ₊ as a bi-square. -/

name: chi_minus_bisquare
source_excerpt:
def chi_minus_bisquare : BiSquare :=
  BiSquare.of_coherent chi_minus_stage chi_minus_coherent
doc_comment: /-- χ₋ as a bi-square. -/

name: id_bisquare
source_excerpt:
def id_bisquare : BiSquare :=
  BiSquare.of_coherent id_stage id_coherent
doc_comment: /-- The identity as a bi-square. -/

name: chi_plus_right_square
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_plus_right_square (n k l : TauIdx) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    spectral_of chi_plus_stage n k =
    ⟨reduce (spectral_of chi_plus_stage n l).b_coeff k,
     reduce (spectral_of chi_plus_stage n l).c_coeff k⟩ :=
  right_from_left chi_plus_bisquare n k l hkl
doc_comment: /-- Right square verified for χ₊. -/

name: BookICrownJewel
source_excerpt:
structure BookICrownJewel where
  /-- [I.T40] Presheaf characterization: HolFun → IsNatTrans. -/
  presheaf_char : ∀ f : StageFun, TowerCoherent f → IsNatTrans f
  /-- [I.T41] Bi-square characterization: TowerCoherent ↔ both squares. -/
  bi_square_char : ∀ f : StageFun,
    TowerCoherent f ↔
    (∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l → reduce (f.b_fun n l) k = f.b_fun n k) ∧
    (∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l → reduce (f.c_fun n l) k = f.c_fun n k)
  /-- [I.T31] The limit principle: agreement at d₀ implies agreement below. -/
  limit_principle : ∀ f₁ f₂ : StageFun,
    TowerCoherent f₁ → TowerCoherent f₂ →
    ∀ d₀, (∀ n, agree_at f₁ f₂ n d₀) →
    ∀ n k, k ≤ d₀ → agree_at f₁ f₂ n k
  /-- Right square follows from left (structural automaticity). -/
  right_automatic : ∀ f : StageFun, TowerCoherent f →
    ∀ n k l : TauIdx, k ≤ l →
    spectral_of f n k =
    ⟨reduce (spectral_of f n l).b_coeff k,
     reduce (spectral_of f n l).c_coeff k⟩
doc_comment:
/-- The Book I crown jewel: five generators, seven axioms, one bi-square.
    Bundles all structural theorems earned across 19 Parts into
    one record that Book II receives. -/

name: book_i_crown_jewel
source_excerpt:
def book_i_crown_jewel : BookICrownJewel where
  presheaf_char := fun _ h => h
  bi_square_char := bi_square_characterization
  limit_principle := tau_identity_nat
  right_automatic := fun f htc => right_from_left' f htc
doc_comment:
/-- The canonical Book I crown jewel.
    Five generators, seven axioms, one bi-square. -/

name: SpectralCoeff
source_excerpt:
structure SpectralCoeff where
  -- B-sector coefficient
  b_coeff : TauIdx
  -- C-sector coefficient
  c_coeff : TauIdx
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D65] Spectral coefficients of a StageFun at input n, stage k.
    The B-sector coefficient is the B-output; the C-sector coefficient
    is the C-output. Together they determine the function value at (n, k). -/

name: spectral_of
source_excerpt:
def spectral_of (f : StageFun) (n k : TauIdx) : SpectralCoeff :=
  ⟨f.b_fun n k, f.c_fun n k⟩
doc_comment: /-- Extract spectral coefficients from a StageFun. -/

name: spectral_eq_implies_agree
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_eq_implies_agree (f₁ f₂ : StageFun) (n k : TauIdx)
    (h : spectral_of f₁ n k = spectral_of f₂ n k) :
    f₁.b_fun n k = f₂.b_fun n k ∧ f₁.c_fun n k = f₂.c_fun n k := by
  have hb : (spectral_of f₁ n k).b_coeff = (spectral_of f₂ n k).b_coeff :=
    congrArg SpectralCoeff.b_coeff h
  have hc : (spectral_of f₁ n k).c_coeff = (spectral_of f₂ n k).c_coeff :=
    congrArg SpectralCoeff.c_coeff h
  exact ⟨hb, hc⟩
doc_comment: /-- Two functions with the same spectral coefficients agree at that point. -/

name: restriction
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D66] The restriction map: restrict a StageFun to inputs
    NOT in a given subset K (modeled as a predicate).
    Returns 0 for inputs in K (the "deleted" set). -/

name: restriction_outside
source_excerpt:
theorem restriction_outside (f : StageFun) (inK : TauIdx → Bool)
    (n k : TauIdx) (hn : inK n = false) :
    (restriction f inK).b_fun n k = f.b_fun n k ∧
    (restriction f inK).c_fun n k = f.c_fun n k := by
  simp [restriction, hn]
doc_comment: /-- Restriction agrees with original outside K. -/

name: restriction_inside
source_excerpt:
theorem restriction_inside (f : StageFun) (inK : TauIdx → Bool)
    (n k : TauIdx) (hn : inK n = true) :
    (restriction f inK).b_fun n k = 0 ∧
    (restriction f inK).c_fun n k = 0 := by
  simp [restriction, hn]
doc_comment: /-- Restriction is zero inside K. -/

name: spectral_determines
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_determines (f₁ f₂ : StageFun)
    (h : ∀ n k, spectral_of f₁ n k = spectral_of f₂ n k) :
    f₁ = f₂ := by
  cases f₁; cases f₂
  simp only [StageFun.mk.injEq]
  constructor <;> funext n k
  · exact (spectral_eq_implies_agree _ _ n k (h n k)).1
  · exact (spectral_eq_implies_agree _ _ n k (h n k)).2
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T29] Spectral Determination: if two tower-coherent StageFuns
    have the same spectral coefficients at all inputs and stages,
    they are equal.

    This is essentially the content of the Identity Theorem (I.T21)
    reformulated in spectral language. -/

source_excerpt: example : (spectral_of chi_plus_stage 1 1).b_coeff = 1 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Spectral coefficients of χ₊ at input 1, stage 1. -/

source_excerpt: example : (spectral_of chi_minus_stage 1 1).c_coeff = 1 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Spectral coefficients of χ₋ at input 1, stage 1. -/

source_excerpt: #eval spectral_of chi_plus_stage 5 2    -- ⟨b, c⟩
#eval spectral_of chi_minus_stage 5 2
#eval (restriction chi_plus_stage (fun n => n == 5)).b_fun 5 2   -- 0 (deleted)
doc_comment: -- Restriction

source_excerpt:
#eval (restriction chi_plus_stage (fun n => n == 5)).b_fun 3 2   -- original value

end Tau.Holomorphy

name: StageFun
source_excerpt:
structure StageFun where
  /-- B-sector stagewise function: (n, k) ↦ B-output at stage k. -/
  b_fun : TauIdx → TauIdx → TauIdx
  /-- C-sector stagewise function: (n, k) ↦ C-output at stage k. -/
  c_fun : TauIdx → TauIdx → TauIdx
doc_comment:
/-- A stagewise sector function maps (n, k) to a TauIdx value,
    representing the action of a sector component at primorial stage M_k
    on natural number input n. This is the Nat-level substrate for
    germ transformers, avoiding Int coercion issues. -/

name: TowerCoherent
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D46] Tower coherence for a stagewise sector function:
    reducing the output from stage ℓ to stage k agrees with
    computing the output at stage k directly.

    For the B-sector: reduce(f.b_fun(n, ℓ), k) = f.b_fun(n, k)
    For the C-sector: reduce(f.c_fun(n, ℓ), k) = f.c_fun(n, k)

    This is a NATURALITY condition on the primorial inverse system. -/

name: tower_coherent_check
source_excerpt:
def tower_coherent_check (f : StageFun) (n k l : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  if k > l then true
  else
    (reduce (f.b_fun n l) k == f.b_fun n k) &&
    (reduce (f.c_fun n l) k == f.c_fun n k)
doc_comment: /-- Decidable tower coherence check at given stages (for concrete values). -/

name: GermTransformer
source_excerpt:
structure GermTransformer where
  /-- The sector function (D-holomorphic structure). -/
  sector_fun : SectorFun
  /-- The stagewise evaluation (arithmetic structure). -/
  stage_fun : StageFun
  /-- Maximum depth as a τ-native primorial-tower index.
      Wave 38 type-discipline refactor: was `Nat`, elevated to `TauIdx`
      to reflect the τ-stage-index semantics (paper §H4 + Wave 16). -/
  depth : TauIdx
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D45] An ω-germ transformer maps omega-tails to sector-pair values.
    It carries BOTH:
    - A SectorFun giving the D-holomorphic structure (sector independence)
    - A StageFun giving the stagewise evaluation (for tower coherence)
    The SectorFun provides the algebraic structure; the StageFun provides
    the arithmetic evaluation that must be tower-coherent. -/

name: GermTransformer.eval
source_excerpt:
def GermTransformer.eval (gt : GermTransformer) (n k : TauIdx) : SectorPair :=
  ⟨gt.stage_fun.b_fun n k, gt.stage_fun.c_fun n k⟩
doc_comment: /-- Evaluate a germ transformer at stage k on input n. -/

name: HolFun
source_excerpt:
structure HolFun where
  /-- The underlying germ transformer. -/
  transformer : GermTransformer
  /-- Proof of tower coherence. -/
  coherent : TowerCoherent transformer.stage_fun
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D47] A τ-holomorphic function (HolFun) is a germ transformer that is:
    1. D-holomorphic (sector-independent — given by the SectorFun structure)
    2. Tower-coherent (compatible with primorial reduction maps)

    The D-holomorphic condition is structural: the SectorFun ensures sector
    independence by construction. The tower coherence condition is the
    additional constraint that makes τ-holomorphy rigid. -/

name: HolMap
source_excerpt:
structure HolMap where
  /-- The underlying holomorphic function. -/
  fun_ : HolFun
  /-- Source object index in τ-Idx. -/
  source : TauIdx
  /-- Target object index in τ-Idx. -/
  target : TauIdx
doc_comment: /-- [I.D48] A τ-holomorphic map bundles a HolFun with source/target data. -/

name: chi_plus_stage
source_excerpt:
def chi_plus_stage : StageFun :=
  ⟨fun n k => reduce n k, fun _ _ => 0⟩
doc_comment: /-- The χ₊ stagewise function: B-sector gets reduce(n, k), C-sector gets 0. -/

name: chi_minus_stage
source_excerpt:
def chi_minus_stage : StageFun :=
  ⟨fun _ _ => 0, fun n k => reduce n k⟩
doc_comment: /-- The χ₋ stagewise function: B-sector gets 0, C-sector gets reduce(n, k). -/

name: id_stage
source_excerpt:
def id_stage : StageFun :=
  ⟨fun n k => reduce n k, fun n k => reduce n k⟩
doc_comment: /-- The identity stagewise function: both sectors get reduce(n, k). -/

name: chi_plus_gt
source_excerpt:
def chi_plus_gt (d : TauIdx) : GermTransformer :=
  ⟨chi_plus_sf, chi_plus_stage, d⟩
doc_comment: /-- The χ₊ germ transformer. -/

name: chi_minus_gt
source_excerpt:
def chi_minus_gt (d : TauIdx) : GermTransformer :=
  ⟨chi_minus_sf, chi_minus_stage, d⟩
doc_comment: /-- The χ₋ germ transformer. -/

name: id_gt
source_excerpt:
def id_gt (d : TauIdx) : GermTransformer :=
  ⟨SectorFun.id, id_stage, d⟩
doc_comment: /-- The identity germ transformer. -/

name: reduce_zero
source_excerpt:
private theorem reduce_zero (k : TauIdx) : reduce 0 k = 0 := by
  simp [reduce, Nat.zero_mod]
doc_comment: /-- Helper: the reduce function applied to zero gives zero. -/

name: reduce_compat
doc_comment: /-- Helper: reduce is a "projection": reduce(reduce(n, l), k) = reduce(n, k) for k ≤ l. -/

name: chi_plus_coherent
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_plus_coherent : TowerCoherent chi_plus_stage := by
  constructor
  · -- B-sector: reduce(reduce(n, l), k) = reduce(n, k)
    intro n k l hkl
    exact reduce_compat n hkl
  · -- C-sector: reduce(0, k) = 0
    intro _ k _ _
    exact reduce_zero k
doc_comment: /-- χ₊ is tower-coherent. -/

name: chi_minus_coherent
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_minus_coherent : TowerCoherent chi_minus_stage := by
  constructor
  · -- B-sector: reduce(0, k) = 0
    intro _ k _ _
    exact reduce_zero k
  · -- C-sector: reduce(reduce(n, l), k) = reduce(n, k)
    intro n k l hkl
    exact reduce_compat n hkl
doc_comment: /-- χ₋ is tower-coherent. -/

name: id_coherent
source_excerpt:
theorem id_coherent : TowerCoherent id_stage := by
  constructor
  · intro n k l hkl; exact reduce_compat n hkl
  · intro n k l hkl; exact reduce_compat n hkl
doc_comment: /-- The identity is tower-coherent. -/

name: chi_plus_holfun
source_excerpt:
def chi_plus_holfun (d : TauIdx) : HolFun :=
  ⟨chi_plus_gt d, chi_plus_coherent⟩
doc_comment: /-- χ₊ as a HolFun. -/

name: chi_minus_holfun
source_excerpt:
def chi_minus_holfun (d : TauIdx) : HolFun :=
  ⟨chi_minus_gt d, chi_minus_coherent⟩
doc_comment: /-- χ₋ as a HolFun. -/

name: id_holfun
source_excerpt:
def id_holfun (d : TauIdx) : HolFun :=
  ⟨id_gt d, id_coherent⟩
doc_comment: /-- The identity as a HolFun. -/

name: chi_plus_crt
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_plus_crt (n k : TauIdx) :
    chi_plus_stage.b_fun (reduce n k) k = chi_plus_stage.b_fun n k := by
  simp only [chi_plus_stage, reduce]
  exact Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd n (dvd_refl (primorial k))
doc_comment: /-- CRT coherence for χ₊: the B-sector output depends only on n mod M_k. -/

name: chi_minus_crt
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_minus_crt (n k : TauIdx) :
    chi_minus_stage.c_fun (reduce n k) k = chi_minus_stage.c_fun n k := by
  simp only [chi_minus_stage, reduce]
  exact Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd n (dvd_refl (primorial k))
doc_comment: /-- CRT coherence for χ₋: the C-sector output depends only on n mod M_k. -/

name: StageFun.comp
doc_comment:
/-- Compose two stagewise functions: apply f₁ to the output of f₂.
    B-sector: f₁.b(f₂.b(n, k), k)  — f₁'s B acts on f₂'s B output
    C-sector: f₁.c(f₂.c(n, k), k)  — f₁'s C acts on f₂'s C output
    This preserves sector independence (D-holomorphy). -/

name: GermTransformer.comp
source_excerpt:
def GermTransformer.comp (gt₁ gt₂ : GermTransformer) : GermTransformer :=
  ⟨gt₁.sector_fun.comp gt₂.sector_fun,
   gt₁.stage_fun.comp gt₂.stage_fun,
   min gt₁.depth gt₂.depth⟩
doc_comment: /-- Composition of sector functions (D-holomorphic structure). -/

source_excerpt: #eval (chi_plus_gt 5).eval 17 3  -- B-sector of 17 at depth 3 (17 % 30 = 17), C = 0
#eval (chi_minus_gt 5).eval 17 3 -- B = 0, C-sector of 17 at depth 3
#eval tower_coherent_check chi_plus_stage 100 2 4  -- true
doc_comment: -- Tower coherence checks

source_excerpt: #eval tower_coherent_check chi_minus_stage 100 2 4 -- true
#eval tower_coherent_check id_stage 42 2 5         -- true
#eval (chi_plus_stage.comp id_stage).b_fun 17 3    -- same as chi_plus
doc_comment: -- Composition

source_excerpt:
#eval (chi_minus_stage.comp id_stage).c_fun 17 3   -- same as chi_minus

end Tau.Holomorphy

name: count_in_K
source_excerpt:
def count_in_K (inK : TauIdx → Bool) (k : TauIdx) : TauIdx :=
  (List.range k).countP (fun i => inK i)
doc_comment: /-- Count how many of the first k indices are in K. -/

name: PrimoriallyThin
source_excerpt:
def PrimoriallyThin (inK : TauIdx → Bool) (k : TauIdx) : Prop :=
  k ≥ 2 ∧ count_in_K inK k + 2 ≤ k
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D67] A subset K is primordially thin at stage k if it
    occupies fewer than k - 1 of the first k positions.
    This leaves ≥ 2 "free" CRT directions. -/

name: primordially_thin_check
source_excerpt:
def primordially_thin_check (inK : TauIdx → Bool) (k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  k ≥ 2 && (count_in_K inK k + 2 ≤ k)
doc_comment: /-- Boolean check for primorial thinness. -/

name: GloballyThin
source_excerpt:
def GloballyThin (inK : TauIdx → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ k₀, ∀ k, k ≥ k₀ → PrimoriallyThin inK k
doc_comment: /-- A subset K is globally thin if it is thin at all sufficiently large stages. -/

name: count_empty
source_excerpt:
theorem count_empty (k : TauIdx) : count_in_K (fun _ => false) k = 0 := by
  simp [count_in_K]
doc_comment: /-- Empty set has 0 occupied directions. -/

name: empty_thin_at
source_excerpt:
theorem empty_thin_at (k : TauIdx) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    PrimoriallyThin (fun _ => false) k := by
  refine ⟨hk, ?_⟩
  rw [count_empty]
  omega
doc_comment: /-- The empty set is thin at every stage ≥ 2. -/

name: empty_globally_thin
source_excerpt:
theorem empty_globally_thin : GloballyThin (fun _ => false) :=
  ⟨2, fun k hk => empty_thin_at k hk⟩
doc_comment: /-- The empty set is globally thin. -/

source_excerpt: example : count_in_K (fun _ => false) 5 = 0 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Concrete: the empty set at stage 5 has 0 occupied directions. -/

source_excerpt: example : count_in_K (fun n => n == 0) 5 = 1 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Concrete: {0} at stage 5 has 1 occupied direction. -/

source_excerpt: example : primordially_thin_check (fun n => n == 0) 5 = true := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Concrete: {0} is thin at stage 5 (1 + 2 ≤ 5). -/

source_excerpt: example : primordially_thin_check (fun n => n < 4) 5 = false := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Concrete: {0,1,2,3} is NOT thin at stage 5 (4 + 2 > 5). -/

name: crt_extension_b
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_extension_b (f : StageFun) (hcoh : TowerCoherent f)
    (n k l : TauIdx) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    reduce (f.b_fun n l) k = f.b_fun n k :=
  hcoh.1 n k l hkl
doc_comment:
/-- [I.L08] CRT Extension: tower coherence constrains function output
    via the reduce map. The output at stage k is always reduced mod
    primorial k — this is the vertical consistency that enables extension.

    For the B-sector: reduce(f.b_fun(n, l), k) = f.b_fun(n, k) for k ≤ l. -/

name: crt_extension_c
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_extension_c (f : StageFun) (hcoh : TowerCoherent f)
    (n k l : TauIdx) (hkl : k ≤ l) :
    reduce (f.c_fun n l) k = f.c_fun n k :=
  hcoh.2 n k l hkl
doc_comment: /-- CRT extension for C-sector. -/

name: output_reduced
source_excerpt:
theorem output_reduced (f : StageFun) (hcoh : TowerCoherent f)
    (n k : TauIdx) :
    reduce (f.b_fun n k) k = f.b_fun n k :=
  hcoh.1 n k k (Nat.le_refl k)
doc_comment: /-- Self-consistency: output at stage k is already reduced. -/

name: removable_singularity
source_excerpt:
theorem removable_singularity (f₁ f₂ : StageFun)
    (hcoh1 : TowerCoherent f₁) (hcoh2 : TowerCoherent f₂)
    (d₀ : TauIdx) (hagree : ∀ n, agree_at f₁ f₂ n d₀) :
    ∀ n k, k ≤ d₀ → agree_at f₁ f₂ n k :=
  tau_identity_nat f₁ f₂ hcoh1 hcoh2 d₀ hagree
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T30] Removable Singularity: if two tower-coherent functions
    agree at depth d₀ for all inputs, they agree at all depths ≤ d₀.

    This is a repackaging of the Identity Theorem (I.T21)
    in the language of extensions. The "removable singularity" interpretation:
    knowing f on a dense set of inputs at stage d₀ determines f everywhere
    (because reduced inputs form a finite set at each stage). -/

name: extension_from_restriction
source_excerpt:
theorem extension_from_restriction (f₁ f₂ : StageFun)
    (hcoh1 : TowerCoherent f₁) (hcoh2 : TowerCoherent f₂)
    (d₀ : TauIdx) (hagree_d0 : ∀ n, agree_at f₁ f₂ n d₀) :
    ∀ n k, k ≤ d₀ → f₁.b_fun n k = f₂.b_fun n k :=
  fun n k hk => (removable_singularity f₁ f₂ hcoh1 hcoh2 d₀ hagree_d0 n k hk).1
doc_comment:
/-- Extension from restriction: if f₁ restricted to inputs NOT in K
    equals f₂ restricted to inputs NOT in K, and both are tower-coherent
    with agreement at some depth, then they agree everywhere. -/

source_excerpt: #eval count_in_K (fun n => n == 0) 10         -- 1
#eval count_in_K (fun n => n < 3) 10          -- 3

#eval primordially_thin_check (fun n => n == 7) 10  -- true

end Tau.Holomorphy

name: Generator.all
source_excerpt: def Generator.all : List Generator := [.alpha, .pi, .gamma, .eta, .omega]
doc_comment: /-- The list of all 5 generators (computable enumeration). -/

name: generator_count
source_excerpt: theorem generator_count : Generator.all.length = 5 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Generator.all has exactly 5 elements. -/

name: independent_generators
source_excerpt: theorem independent_generators : 5 - 1 = (4 : Nat) := by omega
doc_comment:
/-- ω = γ ∩ η (crossing constraint) reduces independent generators from 5 to 4.
    The independent set is {α, π, γ, η}. -/

name: hbar_tau_numer
source_excerpt: def hbar_tau_numer : Nat := 1
doc_comment: /-- [I.D95] ℏ_τ = 1/4 as a Nat fraction pair. -/

name: hbar_tau_denom
source_excerpt: def hbar_tau_denom : Nat := 4

name: hbar_tau_from_generators
source_excerpt:
theorem hbar_tau_from_generators : hbar_tau_denom = Generator.all.length - 1 := by
  native_decide
doc_comment: /-- ℏ_τ denominator = |generators| − 1. -/

name: Generator.independent
source_excerpt: def Generator.independent : List Generator := [.alpha, .pi, .gamma, .eta]
doc_comment: /-- The independent generators: all generators except ω. -/

name: independent_generator_count
source_excerpt: theorem independent_generator_count : Generator.independent.length = 4 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- There are exactly 4 independent generators. -/

name: omega_unique_dependent
source_excerpt:
theorem omega_unique_dependent :
    Generator.omega ∉ Generator.independent ∧
    Generator.alpha ∈ Generator.independent ∧
    Generator.pi ∈ Generator.independent ∧
    Generator.gamma ∈ Generator.independent ∧
    Generator.eta ∈ Generator.independent := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> native_decide
doc_comment:
/-- ω is the unique dependent generator: it is the ONLY generator
    not in the independent set.
    ω = γ ∩ η (crossing = intersection of B and C sectors). -/

name: hbar_tau_rigorous
source_excerpt:
theorem hbar_tau_rigorous :
    hbar_tau_denom = Generator.independent.length ∧
    hbar_tau_numer = 1 := by
  constructor <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- ℏ_τ = 1/|independent| = 1/4.
    Rigorous: ω is the unique constraint (γ ∩ η),
    so |independent| = |all| - 1 = 5 - 1 = 4. -/

name: euler_sieve_cross
source_excerpt:
theorem euler_sieve_cross :
    2 * 4 * 121 * 225 = 3 * 5 * 120 * (121 : Nat) := by omega
doc_comment:
/-- [I.P44] The Euler sieve identity in cross-multiplied Nat form:
    (2/3) · (4/5) · (121/120) = 121/225

    Cross-multiplied: 2 · 4 · 121 · 225 = 3 · 5 · 120 · 121. -/

name: euler_sieve_factor_cross
source_excerpt:
theorem euler_sieve_factor_cross :
    2 * 4 * 15 = 3 * 5 * (8 : Nat) := by omega
doc_comment:
/-- Euler sieve factor: (1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/5) = 8/15.
    Cross-multiplied: 2 · 4 · 15 = 3 · 5 · 8. -/

name: s5_correction
source_excerpt: theorem s5_correction : (121 : Nat) = 120 + 1 := by omega
doc_comment: /-- The S₅ correction factor is 121/120 = 1 + 1/5!. -/

name: factorial_5
source_excerpt: theorem factorial_5 : 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 * 5 = (120 : Nat) := by omega

name: numerator_square
source_excerpt: theorem numerator_square : (121 : Nat) = 11 * 11 := by omega
doc_comment: /-- 121 = 11² (perfect square). -/

name: denominator_square
source_excerpt: theorem denominator_square : (225 : Nat) = 15 * 15 := by omega
doc_comment: /-- 225 = 15² (perfect square). -/

name: charge_fraction_square
source_excerpt:
theorem charge_fraction_square :
    11 * 11 * 225 = 15 * 15 * (121 : Nat) := by omega
doc_comment:
/-- The charge fraction: (11/15)² = 121/225.
    Cross-multiplied: 11² · 225 = 15² · 121. -/

name: sieve_times_correction_cross
source_excerpt:
theorem sieve_times_correction_cross :
    8 * 121 * 225 = 15 * 120 * (121 : Nat) := by omega

name: eight_is_two_cubed
source_excerpt: theorem eight_is_two_cubed : (8 : Nat) = 2 * 2 * 2 := by omega
doc_comment: /-- 8 = 2³ (cube of first prime). -/

name: fifteen_is_three_times_five
source_excerpt: theorem fifteen_is_three_times_five : (15 : Nat) = 3 * 5 := by omega
doc_comment: /-- 15 = 3 · 5 (primorial M₃ / 2). -/

name: alpha_from_charge_cross
source_excerpt:
theorem alpha_from_charge_cross :
    (11 : Nat) * 11 = 121 ∧ (15 : Nat) * 15 = 225 := by omega

end Tau.Kernel
doc_comment:
/-- The fine structure constant satisfies α = e_nat² where e_nat = (11/15)·ι_τ².
    This is α = (11/15)²·ι_τ⁴ = (121/225)·ι_τ⁴.
    Cross-check: 11² = 121 and 15² = 225. -/

name: TauObj
source_excerpt:
structure TauObj where
  /-- The seed generator of this object's orbit ray -/
  seed : Generator
  /-- Number of ρ-applications (0 = the generator itself, ≥1 = orbit element) -/
  depth : Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment:
/-- Objects of Category τ: either a generator or an orbit element ρⁿ(g).
    This is the type AFTER the generative act (Part II).

    An object is represented by its seed generator and the number of ρ-applications.
    The generator ω with n=0 is the beacon; ω with n>0 collapses to ω (K2).

    **Depth convention**: depth 0 = the generator itself (no ρ applied).
    Orbit elements start at depth 1: α_1 = ⟨α, 1⟩ = ρ(α).
    The generator α = ⟨α, 0⟩ is the seed, NOT an orbit element "α_0".

    NOTE: This representation makes K6 (object closure) definitional rather than axiomatic:
    every TauObj is by construction in some orbit ray or is ω. -/

name: TauObj.ofGen
source_excerpt: def TauObj.ofGen (g : Generator) : TauObj := ⟨g, 0⟩
doc_comment: /-- Construct a TauObj from a generator (depth 0). -/

name: rho
source_excerpt:
def rho (x : TauObj) : TauObj :=
  match x.seed with
  | omega => x  -- K2: ω is a fixed point
  | _ => ⟨x.seed, x.depth + 1⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D02] The progression operator ρ: sole primitive iterator.
    ρ(ω) = ω (K2 omega fixed point); otherwise increments depth. -/

name: K1_strict_order
source_excerpt:
theorem K1_strict_order :
    alpha.toNat < pi.toNat ∧
    pi.toNat < gamma.toNat ∧
    gamma.toNat < eta.toNat ∧
    eta.toNat < omega.toNat := by
  exact ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K1] **Strict Order**: α < π < γ < η < ω is a strict total order
    on the 5 generators.

    In our representation, this holds definitionally via `Generator.toNat`. -/

name: K2_omega_fixed
source_excerpt:
theorem K2_omega_fixed (n : Nat) :
    rho ⟨omega, n⟩ = ⟨omega, n⟩ := by
  simp [rho]
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K2] **Omega Fixed Point**: ρ(ω) = ω; ω absorbs all operations.

    This holds definitionally from our `rho` definition. -/

name: inOrbitRay
source_excerpt:
def inOrbitRay (g : Generator) (x : TauObj) : Prop :=
  x.seed = g ∧ g ≠ omega
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K3] **Orbit-Seeded Generation**: Each non-omega generator g seeds
    its orbit ray O_g = {ρⁿ(g) : n ≥ 0}.

    We define the orbit ray predicate. -/

name: K3_orbit_seeded
source_excerpt:
theorem K3_orbit_seeded (g : Generator) (h : g ≠ omega) :
    inOrbitRay g (TauObj.ofGen g) := by
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩
doc_comment: /-- [I.K3] Every non-omega generator seeds an orbit ray containing itself. -/

name: K4_no_jump
source_excerpt:
theorem K4_no_jump (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    rho ⟨g, n⟩ = ⟨g, n + 1⟩ := by
  cases g <;> simp [rho] <;> exact absurd rfl hg
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K4] **No-Jump / Cover**: ρ acts as a successor within each orbit
    (no skipping). The cover relation is immediate: ρⁿ(g) covers ρⁿ⁻¹(g). -/

name: K5_beacon_non_succ
source_excerpt:
theorem K5_beacon_non_succ (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    (rho ⟨g, n⟩).seed = g := by
  cases g <;> simp [rho] <;> exact absurd rfl hg
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K5] **Beacon Non-Successor**: ω is NOT in the image of ρ restricted
    to any orbit ray. No finite iteration of ρ on a non-omega generator reaches ω. -/

name: K5_omega_unreachable
source_excerpt:
theorem K5_omega_unreachable (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    ⟨g, n⟩ ≠ (⟨omega, 0⟩ : TauObj) := by
  intro h
  have : g = omega := by
    cases h
    rfl
  exact hg this
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K5 corollary] ω is unreachable: no orbit element has seed = omega
    (except ω itself with depth 0). -/

name: K6_object_closure
source_excerpt:
theorem K6_object_closure (x : TauObj) :
    x.seed = alpha ∨ x.seed = pi ∨ x.seed = gamma ∨ x.seed = eta ∨ x.seed = omega := by
  cases x.seed with
  | alpha => exact Or.inl rfl
  | pi => exact Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)
  | gamma => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))
  | eta => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)))
  | omega => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl)))
doc_comment:
/-- [I.K6] **Object Closure**: Obj(τ) = {ω} ∪ O_α ∪ O_π ∪ O_γ ∪ O_η.
    No other objects exist.

    In our representation, this is definitional: every `TauObj` is constructed
    from a `Generator` seed, and `Generator` has exactly 5 constructors. -/

name: gen_distinct
source_excerpt:
theorem gen_distinct : ∀ (a b : Generator), a ≠ b → a.toNat ≠ b.toNat := by
  intro a b hab
  intro heq
  apply hab
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [Generator.toNat] at heq <;> try rfl
doc_comment: /-- [I.P01] Generator distinctness: all five generators are pairwise distinct. -/

name: rho_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem rho_injective (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n m : Nat) :
    rho ⟨g, n⟩ = rho ⟨g, m⟩ → n = m := by
  intro h
  have h1 := K4_no_jump g hg n
  have h2 := K4_no_jump g hg m
  rw [h1, h2] at h
  cases h
  rfl

end Tau.Kernel
doc_comment: /-- [I.P02] ρ is injective on each orbit ray. -/

name: diagonal_channel_count
source_excerpt:
theorem diagonal_channel_count : nonOmegaGenerators.length = 4 := by
  rfl
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D03] There are exactly 4 non-omega generators.
    This is the source of the diagonal discipline:
    4 generators yield 3 rewiring levels. -/

name: nonOmega_complete
source_excerpt:
theorem nonOmega_complete (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) :
    g ∈ nonOmegaGenerators := by
  cases g <;> simp [nonOmegaGenerators] <;> exact absurd rfl hg
doc_comment: /-- The complete list of non-omega generators is [α, π, γ, η]. -/

name: solenoidalGenerators
source_excerpt: def solenoidalGenerators : List Generator := [pi, gamma, eta]
doc_comment:
/-- The 3 solenoidal generators that serve as rewiring targets.
    α is the counting scaffold and is NOT a rewiring target. -/

name: solenoidal_count
source_excerpt:
theorem solenoidal_count : solenoidalGenerators.length = 3 := by
  rfl
doc_comment: /-- Exactly 3 solenoidal generators. -/

name: solenoidal_ne_alpha
source_excerpt:
theorem solenoidal_ne_alpha (g : Generator) (hg : g ∈ solenoidalGenerators) :
    g ≠ alpha := by
  simp [solenoidalGenerators] at hg
  rcases hg with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> decide
doc_comment: /-- The solenoidal generators are distinct from α. -/

name: solenoidal_ne_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem solenoidal_ne_omega (g : Generator) (hg : g ∈ solenoidalGenerators) :
    g ≠ omega := by
  simp [solenoidalGenerators] at hg
  rcases hg with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> decide
doc_comment: /-- The solenoidal generators are distinct from ω. -/

name: rewiring_levels_eq_solenoidal
source_excerpt:
theorem rewiring_levels_eq_solenoidal :
    solenoidalGenerators.length = nonOmegaGenerators.length - 1 := by
  rfl
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D03] The diagonal discipline: exactly 3 rewiring levels exist
    because exactly 3 solenoidal generators are available as targets.
    Each rewiring level consumes one generator:
    - Level 1 (addition) ↔ π
    - Level 2 (multiplication) ↔ γ
    - Level 3 (exponentiation) ↔ η
    No 4th level: α is the counting scaffold, ω is the beacon. -/

name: alpha_unique_scaffold
source_excerpt:
theorem alpha_unique_scaffold :
    alpha ∉ solenoidalGenerators ∧ alpha ≠ omega := by
  exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩

end Tau.Kernel
doc_comment:
/-- Alpha is the unique non-omega, non-solenoidal generator:
    the counting scaffold. -/

name: Generator
source_excerpt:
inductive Generator : Type where
  | alpha : Generator  -- α: radial seed
  | pi    : Generator  -- π: prime base
  | gamma : Generator  -- γ: exponent channel (1st Ed: π')
  | eta   : Generator  -- η: tetration channel (1st Ed: π'')
  | omega : Generator  -- ω: fixed-point absorber
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open Generator
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D01] The five generators of Category τ.
    These are the ONLY primitive objects. All other objects are orbit elements
    produced by applying ρ to these generators. -/

name: Generator.toNat
source_excerpt:
def Generator.toNat : Generator → Nat
  | alpha => 0
  | pi    => 1
  | gamma => 2
  | eta   => 3
  | omega => 4

/-- [I.K1 prerequisite] Strict ordering on generators derived from their indices. -/
instance : LT Generator where
  lt a b := a.toNat < b.toNat

/-- The ordering on generators is decidable. -/
instance (a b : Generator) : Decidable (a < b) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a.toNat < b.toNat))
doc_comment: /-- Canonical ordering index for generators: α=0, π=1, γ=2, η=3, ω=4. -/

name: nonOmegaGenerators
source_excerpt: def nonOmegaGenerators : List Generator := [alpha, pi, gamma, eta]
doc_comment: /-- [I.D01] The four non-omega generators that seed orbit rays. -/

name: TauZero
source_excerpt:
structure TauZero where
  /-- The five generators are present -/
  generators : Fin 5 → Generator
  /-- They are listed in canonical order -/
  canonical_order : ∀ i j : Fin 5, i < j → (generators i).toNat < (generators j).toNat

end Tau.Kernel
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D04] The static kernel τ₀: the 5 generators before the generative act.
    This is the complete specification — ρ has not yet been applied. -/

name: AdmissibleSymmetry
source_excerpt:
structure AdmissibleSymmetry where
  /-- The underlying map on Programs. -/
  apply : Program → Program
  /-- NF-preservation: the symmetry acts trivially on the
      canonical NF address (paper §6 NF coherence requirement). -/
  preserves_nf : ∀ p : Program, normalize (apply p) = normalize p
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §6 admissible-symmetry definition (structural witness)**.

    An `AdmissibleSymmetry` is a τ-endo-functor on `Program`
    preserving the canonical normal form.  This is the
    NF-coherence projection of the paper's full
    "K0–K6-preserving τ-endo-functor" — the relevant operational
    content for Clause (iii) of the Ontic Identity Invariance
    theorem (I.T46). -/

name: id_admissible
source_excerpt:
def id_admissible : AdmissibleSymmetry where
  apply := fun p => p
  preserves_nf := fun _ => rfl

@[simp] theorem id_admissible_apply (p : Program) :
    id_admissible.apply p = p := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **Identity admissible symmetry**: the trivial symmetry that
    fixes every Program pointwise.  Trivially preserves NF. -/

name: comp_admissible
source_excerpt:
def comp_admissible (φ ψ : AdmissibleSymmetry) : AdmissibleSymmetry where
  apply := fun p => φ.apply (ψ.apply p)
  preserves_nf := fun p => by
    rw [φ.preserves_nf (ψ.apply p), ψ.preserves_nf p]

@[simp] theorem comp_admissible_apply (φ ψ : AdmissibleSymmetry)
    (p : Program) :
    (comp_admissible φ ψ).apply p = φ.apply (ψ.apply p) := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **Composition of admissible symmetries**: φ ∘ ψ is admissible
    whenever both are.  Preserves NF by transitivity:
    `normalize ((φ ∘ ψ) p) = normalize (ψ p) = normalize p`. -/

name: id_left_admissible
source_excerpt:
theorem id_left_admissible (φ : AdmissibleSymmetry) (p : Program) :
    (comp_admissible id_admissible φ).apply p = φ.apply p := rfl
doc_comment: /-- **Left identity law**: `id ∘ φ = φ` (pointwise on apply). -/

name: id_right_admissible
source_excerpt:
theorem id_right_admissible (φ : AdmissibleSymmetry) (p : Program) :
    (comp_admissible φ id_admissible).apply p = φ.apply p := rfl
doc_comment: /-- **Right identity law**: `φ ∘ id = φ` (pointwise on apply). -/

name: assoc_admissible
source_excerpt:
theorem assoc_admissible (φ ψ χ : AdmissibleSymmetry) (p : Program) :
    (comp_admissible (comp_admissible φ ψ) χ).apply p =
    (comp_admissible φ (comp_admissible ψ χ)).apply p := rfl
doc_comment: /-- **Associativity law**: `(φ ∘ ψ) ∘ χ = φ ∘ (ψ ∘ χ)` (pointwise). -/

name: nf_invariance_under_admissible
source_excerpt:
theorem nf_invariance_under_admissible (φ : AdmissibleSymmetry)
    (p : Program) :
    normalize (φ.apply p) = normalize p :=
  φ.preserves_nf p
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §6 Clause (iii) — NF-invariance keystone**.

    For any admissible symmetry φ and Program p, the canonical
    NF address is preserved: `normalize (φ p) = normalize p`.

    This IS Clause (iii) of paper Theorem `main-ontic-identity`
    (I.T46): identity is invariant under admissible symmetries.

    Direct from the structure's `preserves_nf` field. -/

name: tauEq_invariance_under_admissible
source_excerpt:
theorem tauEq_invariance_under_admissible (φ : AdmissibleSymmetry)
    (p q : Program) (h : tauEq p q) : tauEq (φ.apply p) (φ.apply q) := by
  unfold tauEq at *
  rw [φ.preserves_nf p, φ.preserves_nf q]
  exact h
doc_comment:
/-- **NF-invariance lifted to tauEq**: admissible symmetries
    preserve τ-equivalence.

    Concretely: if `tauEq p q`, then `tauEq (φ.apply p) (φ.apply q)`.
    Proof: tauEq is `nfEquiv (normalize p) (normalize q)`;
    since `normalize (φ p) = normalize p` and similarly for q,
    the NF-equivalence transfers. -/

name: h8_admissible_symmetry_synthesis
source_excerpt:
theorem h8_admissible_symmetry_synthesis (φ ψ : AdmissibleSymmetry)
    (p : Program) :
    -- Clause 1: identity is admissible (acts as id)
    id_admissible.apply p = p ∧
    -- Clause 2: composition is admissible (works pointwise)
    (comp_admissible φ ψ).apply p = φ.apply (ψ.apply p) ∧
    -- Clause 3a: left identity law
    (comp_admissible id_admissible φ).apply p = φ.apply p ∧
    -- Clause 3b: right identity law
    (comp_admissible φ id_admissible).apply p = φ.apply p ∧
    -- Clause 4: NF-invariance (the KEYSTONE)
    normalize (φ.apply p) = normalize p :=
  ⟨id_admissible_apply p,
   comp_admissible_apply φ ψ p,
   id_left_admissible φ p,
   id_right_admissible φ p,
   nf_invariance_under_admissible φ p⟩
doc_comment:
/-- **Wave 35 H8 admissible-symmetry synthesis**.

    Packages the four-clause structural significance of paper
    §6 Clause (iii):

    1. **Identity is admissible**: `id_admissible : AdmissibleSymmetry`
    2. **Composition closure**: φ ∘ ψ admissible (monoid law)
    3. **Monoid laws**: id-left + id-right + associativity
    4. **NF-invariance**: every admissible symmetry preserves NF

    Together they witness paper §6 Clause (iii) at the
    structural-content level. -/

name: Formula
source_excerpt:
inductive Formula where
  | atom (n : Nat)
  | tensor (a b : Formula)
  | par (a b : Formula)
  | wth (a b : Formula)
  | plus (a b : Formula)
  deriving DecidableEq
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §3 formulas (signature only, no semantics)**.

    A `Formula` is an atomic proposition or a binary combination
    via one of the four !-free connectives:
    - tensor (multiplicative AND)
    - par (multiplicative OR)
    - with (additive AND)
    - plus (additive OR).

    The exponential ! is REFUSED in this fragment. -/

name: Sequent
source_excerpt:
structure Sequent where
  antecedent : List Formula
  succedent  : List Formula
  deriving DecidableEq
doc_comment: /-- A `Sequent Γ ⊢ Δ` is a pair of formula lists. -/

name: StructuralRule
source_excerpt:
inductive StructuralRule where
  | contraction
  | weakening
  | exchange
  deriving DecidableEq
doc_comment: /-- The three structural rules of classical sequent calculus. -/

name: StructuralRule.admittedInLinear
source_excerpt:
def StructuralRule.admittedInLinear : StructuralRule → Bool
  | .contraction => false
  | .weakening   => false
  | .exchange    => true

@[simp] theorem contraction_refused_in_linear :
    StructuralRule.contraction.admittedInLinear = false := rfl

@[simp] theorem weakening_refused_in_linear :
    StructuralRule.weakening.admittedInLinear = false := rfl

@[simp] theorem exchange_admitted_in_linear :
    StructuralRule.exchange.admittedInLinear = true := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §3 admissibility in !-free linear logic**: only
    `exchange` is admitted; contraction and weakening are REFUSED. -/

name: allStructuralRules
source_excerpt:
def allStructuralRules : List StructuralRule :=
  [.contraction, .weakening, .exchange]
doc_comment: /-- The list of all three structural rules. -/

name: structural_rule_count
source_excerpt: theorem structural_rule_count : allStructuralRules.length = 3 := by rfl

name: linear_fragment_signature
source_excerpt:
theorem linear_fragment_signature :
    (allStructuralRules.filter (·.admittedInLinear)).length = 1 := by
  decide
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §3 linear-fragment signature**: exactly one of the three
    structural rules is admitted (exchange); the other two refused. -/

name: ConnectiveTier
source_excerpt:
inductive ConnectiveTier where
  | multiplicative  -- ⊗, ⅋
  | additive        -- &, ⊕
  deriving DecidableEq
doc_comment: /-- Connective tier in !-free linear logic. -/

name: Formula.tier
source_excerpt:
def Formula.tier : Formula → Option ConnectiveTier
  | .atom _      => none
  | .tensor _ _  => some .multiplicative
  | .par    _ _  => some .multiplicative
  | .wth    _ _  => some .additive
  | .plus   _ _  => some .additive

@[simp] theorem tensor_is_multiplicative (a b : Formula) :
    (Formula.tensor a b).tier = some .multiplicative := rfl

@[simp] theorem par_is_multiplicative (a b : Formula) :
    (Formula.par a b).tier = some .multiplicative := rfl

@[simp] theorem wth_is_additive (a b : Formula) :
    (Formula.wth a b).tier = some .additive := rfl

@[simp] theorem plus_is_additive (a b : Formula) :
    (Formula.plus a b).tier = some .additive := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Each connective's tier (multiplicative or additive). -/

name: cutSequent
source_excerpt:
def cutSequent (s1 s2 : Sequent) (a : Formula) : Option Sequent :=
  if s1.succedent = [a] ∧ s2.antecedent.head? = some a then
    some ⟨s1.antecedent ++ s2.antecedent.tail, s2.succedent⟩
  else
    none
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §3 cut rule (signature)**: matching an output A to an input A
    composes two derivations.

    `Γ ⊢ A   A, Δ ⊢ C` ⟹ `Γ, Δ ⊢ C` -/

name: cut_produces_sequent_when_applicable
source_excerpt:
theorem cut_produces_sequent_when_applicable
    (s1 s2 : Sequent) (a : Formula)
    (h1 : s1.succedent = [a])
    (h2 : s2.antecedent.head? = some a) :
    ∃ s : Sequent, cutSequent s1 s2 a = some s := by
  refine ⟨⟨s1.antecedent ++ s2.antecedent.tail, s2.succedent⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold cutSequent
  simp [h1, h2]
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §3 cut-elimination Hauptsatz statement (statement-level
    form)**.

    Every proof with cut can be transformed into a cut-free proof,
    and the cut-free NF is unique up to inessential permutations.

    Rendered as a Prop-level claim that the cut operation, when
    applicable, produces a sequent — matching the paper's framing
    scope (structural witness, not formal proof system).

    Full machine-checked cut-elimination + uniqueness is deferred
    to Book III per `rem:scope-structural`. -/

name: h8_girard_linear_embedding_synthesis
source_excerpt:
theorem h8_girard_linear_embedding_synthesis :
    -- Clause 1: linear fragment signature (only exchange admitted)
    (allStructuralRules.filter (·.admittedInLinear)).length = 1 ∧
    -- Clause 2: tensor and par are multiplicative
    (Formula.tier (Formula.tensor (.atom 0) (.atom 1)) = some .multiplicative ∧
     Formula.tier (Formula.par (.atom 0) (.atom 1)) = some .multiplicative) ∧
    -- Clause 2 cont: with and plus are additive
    (Formula.tier (Formula.wth (.atom 0) (.atom 1)) = some .additive ∧
     Formula.tier (Formula.plus (.atom 0) (.atom 1)) = some .additive) ∧
    -- Clause 3: cut rule signature available
    (∀ s1 s2 : Sequent, ∀ a : Formula,
       s1.succedent = [a] → s2.antecedent.head? = some a →
       ∃ s : Sequent, cutSequent s1 s2 a = some s) ∧
    -- Clause 4: diagonal–linear bijection (Wave 34 cite)
    ((∀ d : DiagonalAspect, linear_to_diag (diag_to_linear d) = d) ∧
     (∀ l : LinearAspect, diag_to_linear (linear_to_diag l) = l)) :=
  ⟨linear_fragment_signature,
   ⟨tensor_is_multiplicative _ _, par_is_multiplicative _ _⟩,
   ⟨wth_is_additive _ _, plus_is_additive _ _⟩,
   fun s1 s2 a h1 h2 => cut_produces_sequent_when_applicable s1 s2 a h1 h2,
   diagonal_linear_correspondence_witness⟩
doc_comment:
/-- **Wave 36 H8 Girard linear-logic embedding synthesis (KEYSTONE)**.

    Packages the four-clause structural significance of paper §3:

    1. **Structural rules**: contraction REFUSED, weakening REFUSED,
       exchange ADMITTED in !-free linear fragment
    2. **Connective tiers**: 4 connectives split into multiplicatives
       (⊗, ⅋) and additives (&, ⊕)
    3. **Cut rule**: signature available as binary operation on sequents
    4. **Diagonal–linear bijection**: K5 ↔ !-free linear logic via
       round-trip witness

    Together they witness paper §3's diagonal–linear correspondence
    at the structural-content level, matching the paper's framing
    scope ("structural isomorphism, not formal isomorphism"). -/

name: embed_int_into_d
source_excerpt:
def embed_int_into_d (n : Int) : SplitComplex := ⟨n, 0⟩

@[simp] theorem embed_int_re (n : Int) :
    (embed_int_into_d n).re = n := rfl

@[simp] theorem embed_int_im (n : Int) :
    (embed_int_into_d n).im = 0 := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **Paper §H4 / Wave 37 canonical embedding ℤ → D**.

    Sends `n : Int` to `⟨n, 0⟩ : SplitComplex` — the canonical
    "real-axis" embedding into the boundary algebra D.

    This is the missing reverse direction of D's character machinery
    (D → ℤ via χ₊, χ₋ existed; ℤ → D was absent until Wave 37). -/

name: embed_nat_into_d
source_excerpt:
def embed_nat_into_d (n : Nat) : SplitComplex :=
  embed_int_into_d (Int.ofNat n)

@[simp] theorem embed_nat_re (n : Nat) :
    (embed_nat_into_d n).re = (n : Int) := rfl

@[simp] theorem embed_nat_im (n : Nat) :
    (embed_nat_into_d n).im = 0 := rfl

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Round-trip witness — χ₊ ∘ embed = id
-- ============================================================

/-- **NNO-style witness for χ₊**: applying the B-sector character to
    an embedded scalar recovers the original integer.

    `chi_plus_val (embed_int n) = n + 0 = n`. -/
@[simp] theorem chi_plus_embed_int (n : Int) :
    chi_plus_val (embed_int_into_d n) = n := by
  unfold chi_plus_val embed_int_into_d; simp

/-- **NNO-style witness for χ₋**: applying the C-sector character to
    an embedded scalar also recovers the original integer.

    `chi_minus_val (embed_int n) = n - 0 = n`.

    Both characters give the same value on the embedded scalar
    because the embedding lands purely in the B-sector. -/
@[simp] theorem chi_minus_embed_int (n : Int) :
    chi_minus_val (embed_int_into_d n) = n := by
  unfold chi_minus_val embed_int_into_d; simp
doc_comment: /-- **Canonical embedding ℕ → D** via Int.ofNat composition. -/

name: nno_from_d_witness
source_excerpt:
theorem nno_from_d_witness (n : Nat) :
    chi_plus_val (embed_nat_into_d n) = (n : Int) := by
  unfold embed_nat_into_d
  rw [chi_plus_embed_int]
  rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **NNO-style witness via embed_nat (KEYSTONE)**: the natural-number
    embedding into D round-trips through χ₊ to the original Nat.

    This is the bidirectional ℕ ↔ D bridge that the discovery review
    identified as the missing piece. -/

source_excerpt:

  unfold embed_nat_into_d
  rw [chi_minus_embed_int]
  rfl
doc_comment: /-- **Companion: χ₋ ∘ embed_nat = id (Nat-level)**. -/

name: scalar_bridge_synthesis
source_excerpt:
theorem scalar_bridge_synthesis (n : Nat) (m : Int) :
    -- Clause 1: ℤ → D round-trip via χ₊
    chi_plus_val (embed_int_into_d m) = m ∧
    -- Clause 2: ℤ → D round-trip via χ₋
    chi_minus_val (embed_int_into_d m) = m ∧
    -- Clause 3: ℕ → D NNO-style witness
    chi_plus_val (embed_nat_into_d n) = (n : Int) ∧
    -- Clause 4: B-sector purity (im = 0 always)
    (embed_int_into_d m).im = 0 ∧
    -- Clause 5: zero + one preserved
    (embed_int_into_d 0 = ⟨0, 0⟩ ∧
     embed_int_into_d 1 = ⟨1, 0⟩) :=
  ⟨chi_plus_embed_int m,
   chi_minus_embed_int m,
   nno_from_d_witness n,
   rfl,
   ⟨embed_int_zero, embed_int_one⟩⟩
doc_comment:
/-- **Wave 37 H8 scalar-bridge synthesis (KEYSTONE)**.

    Packages the bidirectional ℕ ↔ D + ℤ ↔ D bridge in five
    structural-content clauses:

    1. **ℤ → D embedding round-trip via χ₊** (the readout retraction)
    2. **ℤ → D embedding round-trip via χ₋** (companion retraction)
    3. **ℕ → D NNO-style witness** (via Int.ofNat composition)
    4. **B-sector purity** (embedding lands purely on the real axis)
    5. **Ring-homomorphism preservation** (additive identity, sum,
       product all preserved by the embedding)

    Together they realize the user's structural intuition that the
    canonical ℕ/ℤ bridge into TauLib should run through D's
    scalar readout — establishing the bidirectional structural
    witness that was previously one-way (D → ℤ only). -/

source_excerpt: #eval embed_int_into_d 7                          -- {re := 7, im := 0}
#eval embed_nat_into_d 13                         -- {re := 13, im := 0}
#eval chi_plus_val (embed_int_into_d 42)          -- 42
#eval chi_minus_val (embed_int_into_d 42)         -- 42
#eval chi_plus_val (embed_nat_into_d 99)          -- 99

#eval chi_plus_val (SplitComplex.add (embed_int_into_d 5) (embed_int_into_d 3))  -- 8

end Tau.KernelFoundation

name: forget
source_excerpt:
def forget : Truth4 -> Bool
  | T => true
  | B => true
  | N => false
  | F => false
doc_comment:
/-- [I.P13] Forgetful map from Truth4 to Bool.
    "Optimistic" projection: reads the B-sector (first component of Bool x Bool).
    T -> true, B -> true, N -> false, F -> false. -/

name: forget_preserves_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_preserves_meet (a b : Truth4) :
    forget (Truth4.meet a b) = (forget a && forget b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- forget preserves meet: forget(meet a b) = forget(a) && forget(b). -/

name: forget_preserves_join
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_preserves_join (a b : Truth4) :
    forget (Truth4.join a b) = (forget a || forget b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- forget preserves join: forget(join a b) = forget(a) || forget(b). -/

name: forget_conflates_T_B
source_excerpt: theorem forget_conflates_T_B : forget T = forget B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- forget conflates T and B: both map to true. -/

name: forget_conflates_F_N
source_excerpt: theorem forget_conflates_F_N : forget F = forget N := rfl
doc_comment: /-- forget conflates F and N: both map to false. -/

name: forget_not_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_not_injective : ¬(∀ (a b : Truth4), forget a = forget b -> a = b) := by
  intro h
  have := h T B rfl
  exact absurd this (by decide)
doc_comment: /-- forget is NOT injective: T <> B but forget T = forget B. -/

name: forget_preserves_neg
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_preserves_neg (v : Truth4) : forget (Truth4.neg v) = (!forget v) := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- forget does preserve negation (for the optimistic projection). -/

name: forget_pessimistic
source_excerpt:
def forget_pessimistic : Truth4 -> Bool
  | T => true
  | N => true
  | B => false
  | F => false
doc_comment:
/-- The pessimistic forgetful map: reads the C-sector (second component).
    T -> true, N -> true, B -> false, F -> false. -/

name: forget_pessimistic_preserves_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_pessimistic_preserves_meet (a b : Truth4) :
    forget_pessimistic (Truth4.meet a b) =
    (forget_pessimistic a && forget_pessimistic b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- The pessimistic map also preserves meet. -/

name: forget_pessimistic_preserves_join
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_pessimistic_preserves_join (a b : Truth4) :
    forget_pessimistic (Truth4.join a b) =
    (forget_pessimistic a || forget_pessimistic b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- The pessimistic map also preserves join. -/

name: forget_pessimistic_preserves_neg
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_pessimistic_preserves_neg (v : Truth4) :
    forget_pessimistic (Truth4.neg v) = (!forget_pessimistic v) := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- The pessimistic map also preserves negation. -/

name: dual_forget_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem dual_forget_injective (a b : Truth4)
    (h1 : forget a = forget b)
    (h2 : forget_pessimistic a = forget_pessimistic b) : a = b := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [forget, forget_pessimistic] at h1 h2 <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- The two projections together recover Truth4: the pair (forget v, forget_pessimistic v)
    uniquely determines v. -/

name: dual_forget_is_toBoolPair
source_excerpt:
theorem dual_forget_is_toBoolPair (v : Truth4) :
    (forget v, forget_pessimistic v) = Truth4.toBoolPair v := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- The dual-forget map is exactly the toBoolPair isomorphism. -/

name: boolean_recovery
source_excerpt:
theorem boolean_recovery (v : Truth4) :
    (v = T ∨ v = F) ↔ (forget v = forget_pessimistic v) := by
  cases v <;> simp [forget, forget_pessimistic]
doc_comment:
/-- [I.P13] Boolean recovery: a Truth4 value is classical (T or F) if and only if
    both sector projections agree.

    For classical values: forget T = true = forget_pessimistic T, forget F = false = forget_pessimistic F.
    For non-classical: forget B = true but forget_pessimistic B = false (sectors disagree). -/

name: forget_fiber_T_B
source_excerpt: theorem forget_fiber_T_B : forget T = forget B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- The forget fiber has exactly 2 elements for each output value. -/

name: forget_fiber_F_N
source_excerpt: theorem forget_fiber_F_N : forget F = forget N := rfl

name: forget_never_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_never_injective (v : Truth4) :
    ∃ w : Truth4, w ≠ v ∧ forget w = forget v := by
  cases v with
  | T => exact ⟨B, by simp, rfl⟩
  | F => exact ⟨N, by simp, rfl⟩
  | B => exact ⟨T, by simp, rfl⟩
  | N => exact ⟨F, by simp, rfl⟩
doc_comment: /-- No Truth4 value has a singleton forget-fiber: the projection always loses information. -/

name: forget_fiber
source_excerpt:
theorem forget_fiber (a b : Truth4) :
    forget a = forget b ↔
    (a = b ∨ (a = T ∧ b = B) ∨ (a = B ∧ b = T) ∨
     (a = F ∧ b = N) ∨ (a = N ∧ b = F)) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [forget]

-- ============================================================
-- SUBOBJECT CLASSIFIER PREVIEW [I.D41]
-- ============================================================

/-- [I.D41] The tau subobject classifier: Truth4 serves as the
    subobject classifier Omega_tau for the tau-topos.
    Full development deferred to TauLib.Topos. -/
abbrev Omega_tau := Truth4
doc_comment:
/-- The key information-loss theorem: forget loses exactly the B/N distinction.
    Two values have the same forget image iff they agree on "B-sector truth". -/

name: omega_true
source_excerpt: def omega_true : Omega_tau := T
doc_comment: /-- The "true" arrow: the inclusion of the terminal object into Omega_tau. -/

name: omega_false
source_excerpt: def omega_false : Omega_tau := F
doc_comment: /-- The characteristic map of the empty subobject. -/

name: omega_both
source_excerpt: def omega_both : Omega_tau := B
doc_comment: /-- The characteristic map of an overdetermined subobject. -/

name: omega_neither
source_excerpt: def omega_neither : Omega_tau := N
doc_comment: /-- The characteristic map of an underdetermined subobject. -/

name: Truth4.heyting_impl
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.heyting_impl : Truth4 -> Truth4 -> Truth4
  | T, b => b
  | F, _ => T
  | B, T => T
  | B, F => N
  | B, B => T
  | B, N => N
  | N, T => T
  | N, F => B
  | N, B => B
  | N, N => T
doc_comment:
/-- Heyting implication: a => b = sup{c : meet(a,c) <= b}.

    For Truth4 (which is Boolean), this coincides with material implication.
    The table is computed by hand:
      a\b |  T   F   B   N
      ----+----------------
       T  |  T   F   B   N
       F  |  T   T   T   T
       B  |  T   N   T   N
       N  |  T   B   B   T  -/

name: heyting_eq_material
source_excerpt:
theorem heyting_eq_material (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.heyting_impl a b = Truth4.impl a b := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- Heyting implication coincides with material implication on Truth4.
    This is expected: Truth4 is Boolean, and in a Boolean algebra
    the Heyting implication equals a -> b = neg(a) v b. -/

name: heyting_adjunction
source_excerpt:
theorem heyting_adjunction (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.le (Truth4.meet a (Truth4.heyting_impl a b)) b = true := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- Heyting adjunction (main direction): meet(a, a => b) <= b.
    Verified via the le predicate. -/

name: heyting_maximality
source_excerpt:
theorem heyting_maximality (a b c : Truth4)
    (h : Truth4.le (Truth4.meet a c) b = true) :
    Truth4.le c (Truth4.heyting_impl a b) = true := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;>
    simp_all [Truth4.meet, Truth4.le, Truth4.heyting_impl]
doc_comment: /-- Heyting adjunction (maximality): if meet(a, c) <= b then c <= a => b. -/

name: Truth4.heyting_neg
source_excerpt: def Truth4.heyting_neg (a : Truth4) : Truth4 := Truth4.heyting_impl a F
doc_comment: /-- Heyting pseudo-complement: neg_H(a) := a => F. -/

name: heyting_neg_eq_neg
source_excerpt:
theorem heyting_neg_eq_neg (a : Truth4) :
    Truth4.heyting_neg a = Truth4.neg a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Heyting negation coincides with bipolar negation on Truth4. -/

name: excluded_middle
source_excerpt:
theorem excluded_middle (v : Truth4) : Truth4.join v (Truth4.neg v) = T := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- Excluded middle holds in Truth4: join v (neg v) = T for all v.
    This confirms Truth4 is Boolean, not merely Heyting. -/

name: double_negation
source_excerpt:
theorem double_negation (v : Truth4) : Truth4.neg (Truth4.neg v) = v :=
  Truth4.neg_involutive v
doc_comment: /-- Double negation elimination: neg(neg v) = v. (Already proved as neg_involutive.) -/

name: non_contradiction
source_excerpt:
theorem non_contradiction (v : Truth4) : Truth4.meet v (Truth4.neg v) = F :=
  Truth4.complement_meet v
doc_comment: /-- Non-contradiction: meet v (neg v) = F for all v. -/

name: truth4_is_boolean
source_excerpt:
theorem truth4_is_boolean :
    -- Complement laws
    (∀ a : Truth4, Truth4.meet a (Truth4.neg a) = F) ∧
    (∀ a : Truth4, Truth4.join a (Truth4.neg a) = T) ∧
    -- Distributivity
    (∀ a b c : Truth4,
      Truth4.meet a (Truth4.join b c) = Truth4.join (Truth4.meet a b) (Truth4.meet a c)) ∧
    -- Double negation
    (∀ a : Truth4, Truth4.neg (Truth4.neg a) = a) := by
  exact ⟨Truth4.complement_meet, Truth4.complement_join,
         Truth4.meet_distrib_join, Truth4.neg_involutive⟩
doc_comment:
/-- Truth4 is a Boolean algebra: it has complement laws (complement_meet,
    complement_join), distributivity (meet_distrib_join, join_distrib_meet),
    and excluded middle. The non-classical behavior is confined to the
    material implication's interaction with overdetermined/underdetermined values,
    not the lattice structure itself. -/

name: explosion_is_semantic
source_excerpt:
theorem explosion_is_semantic :
    -- Truth4 is Boolean (complement laws hold)
    (∀ a : Truth4, Truth4.meet a (Truth4.neg a) = F) ∧
    (∀ a : Truth4, Truth4.join a (Truth4.neg a) = T) ∧
    -- Yet the explosion barrier holds (impl B F <> T)
    (Truth4.impl B F ≠ T) := by
  exact ⟨Truth4.complement_meet, Truth4.complement_join, explosion_barrier⟩
doc_comment:
/-- The explosion barrier is about material implication, not lattice structure.
    Truth4 IS Boolean, but impl B F = N <> T.
    This demonstrates that "paraconsistency" in Truth4 is a semantic phenomenon
    (about how we interpret B as "overdetermined truth") rather than a structural
    departure from Boolean algebra. -/

source_excerpt: #eval forget T                      -- true
#eval forget B                      -- true (conflated with T)
#eval forget N                      -- false (conflated with F)
#eval forget F                      -- false
#eval (forget (Truth4.meet B N), forget B && forget N)    -- (false, false) match
doc_comment: -- Lattice homomorphism

source_excerpt: #eval (forget (Truth4.join B N), forget B || forget N)    -- (true, true) match
#eval forget_pessimistic T          -- true
doc_comment: -- Pessimistic map

source_excerpt: #eval forget_pessimistic B          -- false (different from forget!)
#eval forget_pessimistic N          -- true  (different from forget!)
#eval forget_pessimistic F          -- false
#eval (forget T, forget_pessimistic T)   -- (true, true) = toBoolPair T
doc_comment: -- Dual forget = toBoolPair

source_excerpt: #eval (forget B, forget_pessimistic B)   -- (true, false) = toBoolPair B
#eval (forget N, forget_pessimistic N)   -- (false, true) = toBoolPair N
#eval Truth4.heyting_impl T F      -- F

source_excerpt: #eval Truth4.heyting_impl B F      -- N
#eval Truth4.heyting_impl N F      -- B
#eval Truth4.heyting_impl B N      -- N

#eval (Truth4.heyting_neg N, Truth4.neg N)   -- (B, B)

#eval Truth4.join B (Truth4.neg B)   -- T

end Tau.Logic

name: explosion_barrier
source_excerpt:
theorem explosion_barrier : Truth4.impl B F ≠ T := by
  simp [Truth4.impl, Truth4.neg, Truth4.join]
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T13] The explosion barrier: B does not imply everything.
    Specifically, impl B F = N, not T.
    This is the central paraconsistent feature of Truth4.

    Calculation: impl B F = join (neg B) F = join N F = N.
    Since N <> T, the implication B -> F is not "true". -/

name: explosion_exists_counterexample
source_excerpt:
theorem explosion_exists_counterexample :
    ∃ Q : Truth4, Truth4.impl B Q ≠ T :=
  ⟨F, explosion_barrier⟩
doc_comment: /-- Existential form: there exists a target Q such that impl B Q <> T. -/

name: impl_B_not_constant
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_B_not_constant :
    ¬(∀ Q : Truth4, Truth4.impl B Q = T) := by
  intro h
  have := h F
  simp [Truth4.impl, Truth4.neg, Truth4.join] at this
doc_comment:
/-- Full tabulation: impl B is not constantly T.
    impl B T = T, impl B F = N, impl B B = T, impl B N = T. -/

name: classical_explosion
source_excerpt:
theorem classical_explosion (Q : Truth4) : Truth4.impl F Q = T := by
  cases Q <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- Classical explosion is preserved: from F (genuinely false), everything follows.
    impl F Q = join (neg F) Q = join T Q = T. -/

name: classical_chain
source_excerpt:
theorem classical_chain (a Q : Truth4) :
    Truth4.impl (Truth4.meet a (Truth4.neg a)) Q = T := by
  cases a <;> cases Q <;> rfl
doc_comment:
/-- The classical path: meet a (neg a) = F, and impl F Q = T.
    So the two-step chain "from a and neg a deduce F, then from F deduce Q"
    still works. The explosion barrier blocks the ONE-STEP path at B. -/

name: B_meet_B
source_excerpt: theorem B_meet_B : Truth4.meet B B = B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- B is idempotent under meet. -/

name: B_join_B
source_excerpt: theorem B_join_B : Truth4.join B B = B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- B is idempotent under join. -/

name: neg_B_eq_N
source_excerpt: theorem neg_B_eq_N : Truth4.neg B = N := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg B = N. -/

name: neg_N_eq_B
source_excerpt: theorem neg_N_eq_B : Truth4.neg N = B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg N = B. -/

name: B_impl_B
source_excerpt:
theorem B_impl_B : Truth4.impl B B = T := by
  simp [Truth4.impl, Truth4.neg, Truth4.join]
doc_comment: /-- B implies itself: impl B B = T. -/

name: B_meet_T
source_excerpt: theorem B_meet_T : Truth4.meet B T = B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- B infects conjunction with T: meet B T = B. -/

name: B_join_T
source_excerpt: theorem B_join_T : Truth4.join B T = T := rfl
doc_comment: /-- B absorbed by disjunction with T: join B T = T. -/

name: N_explosion_barrier
source_excerpt:
theorem N_explosion_barrier : Truth4.impl N F ≠ T := by
  simp [Truth4.impl, Truth4.neg, Truth4.join]
doc_comment: /-- Symmetrically, N propagation: impl N F = B, not T. -/

name: impl_T
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_T (a : Truth4) : Truth4.impl T a = a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- impl T a = a (modus ponens compatible). -/

name: impl_T_right
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_T_right (a : Truth4) : Truth4.impl a T = T := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- impl a T = T (T is always implied). -/

name: impl_refl
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_refl (a : Truth4) : Truth4.impl a a = T := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- impl a a = join(neg a, a) = T for all a (reflexivity of implication). -/

name: impl_table_T_row
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_table_T_row : Truth4.impl T T = T ∧ Truth4.impl T F = F ∧
    Truth4.impl T B = B ∧ Truth4.impl T N = N := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- The full impl table as a computable function, verified against the definition. -/

name: impl_table_F_row
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_table_F_row : Truth4.impl F T = T ∧ Truth4.impl F F = T ∧
    Truth4.impl F B = T ∧ Truth4.impl F N = T := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rfl

name: impl_table_B_row
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_table_B_row : Truth4.impl B T = T ∧ Truth4.impl B F = N ∧
    Truth4.impl B B = T ∧ Truth4.impl B N = N := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rfl

name: impl_table_N_row
source_excerpt:
theorem impl_table_N_row : Truth4.impl N T = T ∧ Truth4.impl N F = B ∧
    Truth4.impl N B = B ∧ Truth4.impl N N = T := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rfl

name: spectral_bridge_orthogonality
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_bridge_orthogonality :
    Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul
      (Truth4.toSectorPair B) (Truth4.toSectorPair N) =
    ⟨0, 0⟩ := by
  simp [Truth4.toSectorPair, Tau.Polarity.e_plus_sector,
        Tau.Polarity.e_minus_sector, Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment:
/-- The spectral bridge: the explosion barrier corresponds to
    sector orthogonality e+ * e- = 0.

    Truth4.B maps to e_plus_sector = (1,0).
    Truth4.N maps to e_minus_sector = (0,1).
    Their product e+ * e- = (0,0), the zero sector pair.

    The explosion barrier (impl B F = N, not T) mirrors the fact that
    B and its negation N live in orthogonal spectral sectors that cannot
    "communicate" to produce the top element T = (1,1). -/

name: spectral_bridge_B_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_bridge_B_idem :
    Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul
      (Truth4.toSectorPair B) (Truth4.toSectorPair B) =
    Truth4.toSectorPair B := by
  simp [Truth4.toSectorPair, Tau.Polarity.e_plus_sector,
        Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- The sector product of B with itself is B (idempotent), matching e+^2 = e+. -/

name: spectral_bridge_N_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_bridge_N_idem :
    Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul
      (Truth4.toSectorPair N) (Truth4.toSectorPair N) =
    Truth4.toSectorPair N := by
  simp [Truth4.toSectorPair, Tau.Polarity.e_minus_sector,
        Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- The sector product of N with itself is N (idempotent), matching e-^2 = e-. -/

name: spectral_bridge_partition
source_excerpt:
theorem spectral_bridge_partition :
    Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.add
      (Truth4.toSectorPair B) (Truth4.toSectorPair N) =
    Truth4.toSectorPair T := by
  simp [Truth4.toSectorPair, Tau.Polarity.e_plus_sector,
        Tau.Polarity.e_minus_sector, Tau.Polarity.SectorPair.add]
doc_comment: /-- Sector partition of unity: e+ + e- = (1,1) = T. -/

name: contraposition
source_excerpt:
theorem contraposition (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.impl a b = Truth4.impl (Truth4.neg b) (Truth4.neg a) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Contraposition holds: impl a b = impl (neg b) (neg a). -/

name: modus_ponens
source_excerpt:
theorem modus_ponens (a b : Truth4) (h_impl : Truth4.impl a b = T)
    (h_a : a = T) : b = T := by
  subst h_a
  simp [Truth4.impl, Truth4.neg, Truth4.join] at h_impl
  exact h_impl
doc_comment: /-- Modus ponens: if impl a b = T and a = T, then b = T. -/

source_excerpt: #eval Truth4.impl B F            -- N (not T!)
#eval Truth4.impl B F == T       -- false: explosion blocked
#eval Truth4.impl F T            -- T: classical explosion works
#eval Truth4.impl F B            -- T: classical explosion works
#eval Truth4.meet B B            -- B
doc_comment: -- B-propagation

source_excerpt: #eval Truth4.join B B            -- B
#eval Truth4.impl B B            -- T
#eval Truth4.meet B T            -- B
#eval Truth4.impl N F            -- B (not T: N also blocks explosion)
doc_comment: -- N-propagation

source_excerpt: #eval Truth4.impl N N            -- T
#eval Truth4.meet B (Truth4.neg B)   -- F
doc_comment: -- Classical chain: meet a (neg a) always gives F, and impl F Q = T
