name: Truth4
source_excerpt:
inductive Truth4 where
  | T : Truth4
  | F : Truth4
  | B : Truth4
  | N : Truth4
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

open Truth4
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D21] The four truth values from bipolar evaluation.
    - T: both sectors confirm (overdetermined-true)
    - F: both sectors deny (underdetermined-false)
    - B: B-sector confirms, C-sector denies (overdetermined / "both")
    - N: neither sector confirms (underdetermined / "neither") -/

name: Truth4.le
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.le : Truth4 -> Truth4 -> Bool
  | F, _ => true
  | _, T => true
  | B, B => true
  | N, N => true
  | _, _ => false
doc_comment:
/-- Lattice ordering on Truth4.
    Diamond: F is bottom, T is top, B and N are incomparable middle elements. -/

name: Truth4.meet
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.meet : Truth4 -> Truth4 -> Truth4
  | T, b => b
  | a, T => a
  | F, _ => F
  | _, F => F
  | B, B => B
  | N, N => N
  | B, N => F
  | N, B => F
doc_comment: /-- Meet (conjunction): greatest lower bound in the diamond lattice. -/

name: Truth4.join
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.join : Truth4 -> Truth4 -> Truth4
  | F, b => b
  | a, F => a
  | T, _ => T
  | _, T => T
  | B, B => B
  | N, N => N
  | B, N => T
  | N, B => T
doc_comment: /-- Join (disjunction): least upper bound in the diamond lattice. -/

name: Truth4.neg
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.neg : Truth4 -> Truth4
  | T => F
  | F => T
  | B => N
  | N => B
doc_comment:
/-- Negation: bipolar polarity swap. T <-> F, B <-> N.
    Corresponds to the polarity involution sigma on the split-complex algebra. -/

name: Truth4.impl
source_excerpt: def Truth4.impl (a b : Truth4) : Truth4 := Truth4.join (Truth4.neg a) b
doc_comment:
/-- Material implication: a -> b := join(neg a, b).
    Note: this does NOT validate all classical tautologies at B and N. -/

name: Truth4.toBoolPair
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.toBoolPair : Truth4 -> Bool × Bool
  | T => (true, true)
  | F => (false, false)
  | B => (true, false)
  | N => (false, true)
doc_comment: /-- Encode Truth4 as a pair of Booleans (B-sector, C-sector). -/

name: Truth4.fromBoolPair
source_excerpt:
def Truth4.fromBoolPair : Bool × Bool -> Truth4
  | (true, true) => T
  | (false, false) => F
  | (true, false) => B
  | (false, true) => N
doc_comment: /-- Decode a Boolean pair back to Truth4. -/

name: Truth4.meet_comm
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_comm (a b : Truth4) : Truth4.meet a b = Truth4.meet b a := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Meet is commutative. -/

name: Truth4.join_comm
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_comm (a b : Truth4) : Truth4.join a b = Truth4.join b a := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Join is commutative. -/

name: Truth4.meet_assoc
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_assoc (a b c : Truth4) :
    Truth4.meet (Truth4.meet a b) c = Truth4.meet a (Truth4.meet b c) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Meet is associative. -/

name: Truth4.join_assoc
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_assoc (a b c : Truth4) :
    Truth4.join (Truth4.join a b) c = Truth4.join a (Truth4.join b c) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Join is associative. -/

name: Truth4.meet_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_idem (a : Truth4) : Truth4.meet a a = a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Meet is idempotent. -/

name: Truth4.join_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_idem (a : Truth4) : Truth4.join a a = a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Join is idempotent. -/

name: Truth4.absorption_meet_join
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.absorption_meet_join (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.meet a (Truth4.join a b) = a := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Absorption law: meet a (join a b) = a. -/

name: Truth4.absorption_join_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.absorption_join_meet (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.join a (Truth4.meet a b) = a := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Absorption law: join a (meet a b) = a. -/

name: Truth4.meet_distrib_join
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_distrib_join (a b c : Truth4) :
    Truth4.meet a (Truth4.join b c) = Truth4.join (Truth4.meet a b) (Truth4.meet a c) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Meet distributes over join. -/

name: Truth4.join_distrib_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_distrib_meet (a b c : Truth4) :
    Truth4.join a (Truth4.meet b c) = Truth4.meet (Truth4.join a b) (Truth4.join a c) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Join distributes over meet. -/

name: Truth4.meet_F
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_F (a : Truth4) : Truth4.meet F a = F := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- F is the bottom element for meet. -/

name: Truth4.join_T
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_T (a : Truth4) : Truth4.join T a = T := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- T is the top element for join. -/

name: Truth4.meet_T
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.meet_T (a : Truth4) : Truth4.meet T a = a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- T is the identity for meet. -/

name: Truth4.join_F
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.join_F (a : Truth4) : Truth4.join F a = a := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- F is the identity for join. -/

name: Truth4.neg_involutive
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.neg_involutive (v : Truth4) : Truth4.neg (Truth4.neg v) = v := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Negation is involutive: neg (neg v) = v. -/

name: Truth4.neg_T
source_excerpt: theorem Truth4.neg_T : Truth4.neg T = F := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg T = F. -/

name: Truth4.neg_F
source_excerpt: theorem Truth4.neg_F : Truth4.neg F = T := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg F = T. -/

name: Truth4.neg_B
source_excerpt: theorem Truth4.neg_B : Truth4.neg B = N := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg B = N. -/

name: Truth4.neg_N
source_excerpt: theorem Truth4.neg_N : Truth4.neg N = B := rfl
doc_comment: /-- neg N = B. -/

name: Truth4.complement_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.complement_meet (a : Truth4) : Truth4.meet a (Truth4.neg a) = F := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Complement law: meet a (neg a) = F for all a. -/

name: Truth4.complement_join
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.complement_join (a : Truth4) : Truth4.join a (Truth4.neg a) = T := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Complement law: join a (neg a) = T for all a. -/

name: Truth4.de_morgan_meet
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.de_morgan_meet (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.neg (Truth4.meet a b) = Truth4.join (Truth4.neg a) (Truth4.neg b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- De Morgan: neg (meet a b) = join (neg a) (neg b). -/

name: Truth4.de_morgan_join
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.de_morgan_join (a b : Truth4) :
    Truth4.neg (Truth4.join a b) = Truth4.meet (Truth4.neg a) (Truth4.neg b) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- De Morgan: neg (join a b) = meet (neg a) (neg b). -/

name: Truth4.toBoolPair_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.toBoolPair_injective (a b : Truth4)
    (h : Truth4.toBoolPair a = Truth4.toBoolPair b) : a = b := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [Truth4.toBoolPair] at h <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- toBoolPair is injective: distinct truth values map to distinct pairs. -/

name: Truth4.fromBoolPair_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.fromBoolPair_roundtrip (v : Truth4) :
    Truth4.fromBoolPair (Truth4.toBoolPair v) = v := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: fromBoolPair (toBoolPair v) = v. -/

name: Truth4.toBoolPair_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.toBoolPair_roundtrip (p : Bool × Bool) :
    Truth4.toBoolPair (Truth4.fromBoolPair p) = p := by
  rcases p with ⟨b1, b2⟩
  cases b1 <;> cases b2 <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: toBoolPair (fromBoolPair p) = p for valid pairs. -/

name: Truth4.toSectorPair
doc_comment:
/-- Map Truth4 to sector pairs: T = (1,1), F = (0,0), B = (1,0), N = (0,1).
    Links Truth4 to the split-complex idempotent structure from BipolarAlgebra. -/

name: Truth4.B_is_e_plus
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.B_is_e_plus :
    Truth4.toSectorPair B = Tau.Polarity.e_plus_sector := rfl
doc_comment: /-- B maps to the B-sector idempotent e+. -/

name: Truth4.N_is_e_minus
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.N_is_e_minus :
    Truth4.toSectorPair N = Tau.Polarity.e_minus_sector := rfl
doc_comment: /-- N maps to the C-sector idempotent e-. -/

name: Truth4.B_meet_N_spectral
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.B_meet_N_spectral :
    Truth4.meet B N = F := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Spectral bridge: meet of B and N gives F, mirroring e+ * e- = 0. -/

name: Truth4.le_refl
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.le_refl (a : Truth4) : Truth4.le a a = true := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- le is reflexive. -/

name: Truth4.le_F
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.le_F (a : Truth4) : Truth4.le F a = true := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- F is the bottom element. -/

name: Truth4.le_T
source_excerpt:
theorem Truth4.le_T (a : Truth4) : Truth4.le a T = true := by
  cases a <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- T is the top element. -/

source_excerpt: theorem Truth4.N_not_le_B : Truth4.le N B = false := rfl

name: ResonanceComponent
source_excerpt:
inductive ResonanceComponent where
  | L  -- Meta-level contraction / free token reuse
  | E  -- Equality-as-congruence (substitution = identification)
  | P  -- Ontic self-products / diagonal materialization
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- [I.D89] The three components of diagonal resonance. -/

name: DiagonalResonance
source_excerpt:
structure DiagonalResonance where
  contraction_present : Bool     -- (L) free meta-level contraction
  equality_congruence : Bool     -- (E) equality-as-congruence with full substitution
  self_products : Bool           -- (P) ontic self-products with diagonal materialization
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- [I.D89] A foundation's diagonal resonance profile: which components are present. -/

name: DiagonalResonance.isFullResonance
source_excerpt:
def DiagonalResonance.isFullResonance (dr : DiagonalResonance) : Bool :=
  dr.contraction_present && dr.equality_congruence && dr.self_products
doc_comment: /-- A foundation has full diagonal resonance when all three components are present. -/

name: allResonanceComponents
source_excerpt: def allResonanceComponents : List ResonanceComponent := [.L, .E, .P]
doc_comment: /-- All resonance components enumerated. -/

name: resonance_component_count
source_excerpt: theorem resonance_component_count : allResonanceComponents.length = 3 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- There are exactly 3 resonance components. -/

name: tau_resonance
source_excerpt:
def tau_resonance : DiagonalResonance where
  contraction_present := false   -- K5 refuses contraction
  equality_congruence := false   -- NF-confluence: identity decidable, not substitutive
  self_products := false         -- Star-autonomous: no free self-products
doc_comment: /-- τ's diagonal resonance profile: K5 blocks (L) and (P), NF-confluence controls (E). -/

name: tau_no_full_resonance
source_excerpt: theorem tau_no_full_resonance : tau_resonance.isFullResonance = false := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- τ does NOT exhibit full diagonal resonance. -/

name: IdentitySlippage
source_excerpt:
structure IdentitySlippage where
  resonance : DiagonalResonance
  is_full : resonance.isFullResonance = true
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D90] Identity slippage: a foundation exhibits identity slippage if
    diagonal resonance prevents distinct ontic objects from being preserved
    as distinct under global projection. -/

name: tau_no_slippage
source_excerpt:
theorem tau_no_slippage : ¬ ∃ (s : IdentitySlippage), s.resonance = tau_resonance := by
  intro ⟨s, h⟩
  have := s.is_full
  rw [h] at this
  simp [DiagonalResonance.isFullResonance, tau_resonance] at this
doc_comment: /-- τ cannot exhibit identity slippage because it lacks full resonance. -/

name: ShadowIdentityType
source_excerpt:
inductive ShadowIdentityType where
  | equivalenceWitness    -- From (E): congruence-based identification
  | substitutionBridge    -- From (E+L): variable reuse under substitution
  | diagonalProjection    -- From (P): self-product materializes sameness witness
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- [I.D91] Shadow identity: an implicit identification channel type. -/

name: shadowRequires
source_excerpt:
def shadowRequires : ShadowIdentityType → List ResonanceComponent
  | .equivalenceWitness  => [.E]
  | .substitutionBridge  => [.E, .L]
  | .diagonalProjection  => [.P]
doc_comment: /-- A shadow identity requires the relevant resonance components. -/

name: ShadowIdentity
source_excerpt:
structure ShadowIdentity where
  kind : ShadowIdentityType
  resonance : DiagonalResonance
  -- The required components must be present
  component_present : match kind with
    | .equivalenceWitness => resonance.equality_congruence = true
    | .substitutionBridge => resonance.equality_congruence = true ∧ resonance.contraction_present = true
    | .diagonalProjection => resonance.self_products = true
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D91] Shadow identity witness: a channel that acts like identity without being
    ontically constructed. -/

name: tau_no_shadow_equivalence
source_excerpt:
theorem tau_no_shadow_equivalence :
    ¬ ∃ (s : ShadowIdentity), s.resonance = tau_resonance ∧ s.kind = .equivalenceWitness := by
  intro ⟨s, hr, hk⟩
  have := s.component_present
  rw [hr, hk] at this
  simp [tau_resonance] at this
doc_comment: /-- τ admits no shadow identities of equivalenceWitness type. -/

name: tau_no_shadow_substitution
source_excerpt:
theorem tau_no_shadow_substitution :
    ¬ ∃ (s : ShadowIdentity), s.resonance = tau_resonance ∧ s.kind = .substitutionBridge := by
  intro ⟨s, hr, hk⟩
  have := s.component_present
  rw [hr, hk] at this
  simp [tau_resonance] at this
doc_comment: /-- τ admits no shadow identities of substitutionBridge type. -/

name: tau_no_shadow_diagonal
source_excerpt:
theorem tau_no_shadow_diagonal :
    ¬ ∃ (s : ShadowIdentity), s.resonance = tau_resonance ∧ s.kind = .diagonalProjection := by
  intro ⟨s, hr, hk⟩
  have := s.component_present
  rw [hr, hk] at this
  simp [tau_resonance] at this
doc_comment: /-- τ admits no shadow identities of diagonalProjection type. -/

name: LinearAspect
source_excerpt:
inductive LinearAspect where
  | noFreeContraction     -- Resources cannot be freely duplicated
  | resourceTracking      -- Each resource is consumed exactly once
  | finiteResourceBudget  -- The total resource pool is finite
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- The three aspects of linear logic that correspond to K5's discipline. -/

name: DiagonalAspect
source_excerpt:
inductive DiagonalAspect where
  | noUnearnedDiagonals  -- K5.1: no unearned diagonal maps
  | channelConsumption   -- K5.2: each rewiring consumes a channel
  | saturation           -- K5.3: the iterator ladder saturates at 3 levels
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open LinearAspect DiagonalAspect
doc_comment: /-- The three aspects of K5's diagonal discipline. -/

name: diag_to_linear
source_excerpt:
def diag_to_linear : DiagonalAspect → LinearAspect
  | .noUnearnedDiagonals => .noFreeContraction
  | .channelConsumption  => .resourceTracking
  | .saturation          => .finiteResourceBudget
doc_comment: /-- The diagonal-to-linear map: each K5 aspect corresponds to a linear aspect. -/

name: linear_to_diag
source_excerpt:
def linear_to_diag : LinearAspect → DiagonalAspect
  | .noFreeContraction    => .noUnearnedDiagonals
  | .resourceTracking     => .channelConsumption
  | .finiteResourceBudget => .saturation
doc_comment: /-- The inverse map: each linear aspect corresponds to a K5 aspect. -/

name: diag_linear_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem diag_linear_roundtrip (d : DiagonalAspect) :
    linear_to_diag (diag_to_linear d) = d := by
  cases d <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: diagonal -> linear -> diagonal is the identity. -/

name: linear_diag_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem linear_diag_roundtrip (l : LinearAspect) :
    diag_to_linear (linear_to_diag l) = l := by
  cases l <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: linear -> diagonal -> linear is the identity. -/

name: diag_to_linear_injective

name: isRhoPure
source_excerpt:
def isRhoPure : Tau.Denotation.Program → Bool
  | [] => true
  | .rho_inst :: rest => isRhoPure rest
  | .sigma_inst _ _ :: _ => false
doc_comment:
/-- A program is in normal form (cut-free) when it has no redundant
    sigma instructions. The simplest characterization: a program is
    "rho-pure" when it contains only rho instructions.
    In general, cut-freedom corresponds to NF-confluence: the
    rho count is invariant under rewriting. -/

name: empty_is_rho_pure
source_excerpt: theorem empty_is_rho_pure : isRhoPure [] = true := rfl
doc_comment: /-- The empty program is rho-pure (the identity proof). -/

name: rho_pure_compose
source_excerpt:
theorem rho_pure_compose (p q : Tau.Denotation.Program)
    (hp : isRhoPure p = true) (hq : isRhoPure q = true) :
    isRhoPure (Tau.Denotation.Program.compose p q) = true := by
  induction p with
  | nil => simp [Tau.Denotation.Program.compose]; exact hq
  | cons i rest ih =>
    simp only [Tau.Denotation.Program.compose, List.cons_append]
    cases i with
    | rho_inst =>
      simp only [isRhoPure] at hp ⊢
      exact ih hp
    | sigma_inst s t =>
      simp [isRhoPure] at hp
doc_comment:
/-- Concatenation of rho-pure programs is rho-pure.
    This is the linear analogue: cut on two cut-free proofs
    gives a cut-free proof (in the rho-only fragment). -/

name: cut_elimination_additive
source_excerpt:
theorem cut_elimination_additive (p q : Tau.Denotation.Program) :
    Tau.Denotation.countRho (Tau.Denotation.Program.compose p q) =
    Tau.Denotation.countRho p + Tau.Denotation.countRho q :=
  Tau.Denotation.rho_count_compose p q
doc_comment:
/-- NF-confluence as a linear property: the rho count (resource consumption)
    is additive under composition (cut). This is the computational content
    of cut-elimination. -/

name: identity_zero_resource
source_excerpt:
theorem identity_zero_resource :
    Tau.Denotation.countRho [] = 0 :=
  Tau.Denotation.rho_count_nil
doc_comment: /-- The identity program consumes zero resources. -/

name: ResourceState
source_excerpt:
inductive ResourceState where
  | present         -- T: resource confirmed by both sectors
  | absent          -- F: resource denied by both sectors
  | overdetermined  -- B: resource claimed present AND absent (contraction artifact)
  | underdetermined -- N: resource status unknown (weakening artifact)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open ResourceState
doc_comment:
/-- The four resource states corresponding to Truth4 values.
    - present: the resource is available (both sectors confirm)
    - absent: the resource is consumed (both sectors deny)
    - overdetermined: the resource is claimed by conflicting sources
    - underdetermined: the resource status is unknown -/

name: truth4_to_resource
source_excerpt:
def truth4_to_resource : Tau.Logic.Truth4 → ResourceState
  | .T => .present
  | .F => .absent
  | .B => .overdetermined
  | .N => .underdetermined
doc_comment: /-- Map Truth4 values to resource states. -/

name: resource_to_truth4
source_excerpt:
def resource_to_truth4 : ResourceState → Tau.Logic.Truth4
  | .present         => .T
  | .absent          => .F
  | .overdetermined  => .B
  | .underdetermined => .N
doc_comment: /-- Map resource states back to Truth4 values. -/

name: truth4_resource_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem truth4_resource_roundtrip (v : Tau.Logic.Truth4) :
    resource_to_truth4 (truth4_to_resource v) = v := by
  cases v <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: truth4 -> resource -> truth4 is the identity. -/

name: resource_truth4_roundtrip
source_excerpt:
theorem resource_truth4_roundtrip (r : ResourceState) :
    truth4_to_resource (resource_to_truth4 r) = r := by
  cases r <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Round-trip: resource -> truth4 -> resource is the identity. -/

name: truth4_to_resource_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem truth4_to_resource_injective (a b : Tau.Logic.Truth4)
    (h : truth4_to_resource a = truth4_to_resource b) : a = b := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [truth4_to_resource] at h <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Injectivity of truth4_to_resource. -/

name: resource_to_truth4_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem resource_to_truth4_injective (a b : ResourceState)
    (h : resource_to_truth4 a = resource_to_truth4 b) : a = b := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [resource_to_truth4] at h <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- Injectivity of resource_to_truth4. -/

name: overdetermined_is_contraction_artifact
source_excerpt:
theorem overdetermined_is_contraction_artifact :
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.B = .overdetermined := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- B (overdetermined) is the contraction artifact: a resource claimed
    both present and absent — this arises when a resource is used twice
    (contracted) from conflicting sources. -/

name: underdetermined_is_weakening_artifact
source_excerpt:
theorem underdetermined_is_weakening_artifact :
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.N = .underdetermined := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- N (underdetermined) is the weakening artifact: a resource whose
    status is unknown — this arises when a resource is discarded
    (weakened away) before its status is determined. -/

name: present_is_T
source_excerpt:
theorem present_is_T :
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.T = .present := rfl
doc_comment: /-- The present state maps to T. -/

name: absent_is_F
source_excerpt:
theorem absent_is_F :
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.F = .absent := rfl
doc_comment: /-- The absent state maps to F. -/

name: allResourceStates
source_excerpt:
def allResourceStates : List ResourceState :=
  [.present, .absent, .overdetermined, .underdetermined]
doc_comment: /-- All resource states enumerated. -/

name: resource_state_count
source_excerpt: theorem resource_state_count : allResourceStates.length = 4 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- There are exactly 4 resource states. -/

name: contraction_produces_overdetermined
source_excerpt:
theorem contraction_produces_overdetermined :
    k5_status .contraction = .refused ∧
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.B = .overdetermined :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
doc_comment:
/-- Contraction produces overdetermined states. The refused rule
    (.contraction) corresponds to the pathological resource state
    (.overdetermined = B). -/

name: weakening_produces_underdetermined
source_excerpt:
theorem weakening_produces_underdetermined :
    k5_status .weakening = .refused ∧
    truth4_to_resource Tau.Logic.Truth4.N = .underdetermined :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
doc_comment:
/-- Weakening produces underdetermined states. The refused rule
    (.weakening) corresponds to the pathological resource state
    (.underdetermined = N). -/

name: DiagonalLinearCorrespondence
source_excerpt:
structure DiagonalLinearCorrespondence where
  /-- The aspect bijection has 3 components -/
  aspect_count : allDiagonalAspects.length = 3
  /-- The resource interpretation has 4 states matching Truth4 -/
  resource_count : allResourceStates.length = 4
  /-- The aspect bijection is a genuine bijection (round-trip) -/
  aspect_roundtrip_diag : ∀ d, linear_to_diag (diag_to_linear d) = d
  /-- The aspect bijection is a genuine bijection (round-trip) -/
  aspect_roundtrip_linear : ∀ l, diag_to_linear (linear_to_diag l) = l
  /-- The resource interpretation is a genuine bijection (round-trip) -/
  resource_roundtrip_t4 : ∀ v, resource_to_truth4 (truth4_to_resource v) = v
  /-- The resource interpretation is a genuine bijection (round-trip) -/
  resource_roundtrip_rs : ∀ r, truth4_to_resource (resource_to_truth4 r) = r
  /-- Structural rules: exactly 2 refused -/
  rules_refused : refusedRules.length = 2
  /-- Structural rules: exactly 1 preserved -/
  rules_preserved : preservedRules.length = 1
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T37] The Diagonal-Linear Correspondence Theorem.

    The correspondence has three components:
    1. Aspect bijection: 3 diagonal aspects ↔ 3 linear aspects
    2. Resource interpretation: 4 Truth4 values ↔ 4 resource states
    3. Structural classification: 2 refused + 1 preserved = 3 rules

    Together, these establish that K5's diagonal discipline IS the
    !-free fragment of linear logic, restricted to τ's finite universe. -/

name: diagonal_linear_correspondence
source_excerpt:
theorem diagonal_linear_correspondence : DiagonalLinearCorrespondence where
  aspect_count := diagonal_aspect_count
  resource_count := resource_state_count
  aspect_roundtrip_diag := diag_linear_roundtrip
  aspect_roundtrip_linear := linear_diag_roundtrip
  resource_roundtrip_t4 := truth4_resource_roundtrip
  resource_roundtrip_rs := resource_truth4_roundtrip
  rules_refused := refused_count
  rules_preserved := preserved_count
doc_comment: /-- The correspondence theorem: all components are satisfied. -/

    Proof that divisibility is decidable: -/

name: isPrime
source_excerpt:
def isPrime (n : Nat) : Bool :=
  n > 1 && (List.range n).all (fun d => d < 2 || n % d != 0)
doc_comment:
/-- The "is prime" predicate is decidable: a number is prime iff
    it is greater than 1 and its only divisors are 1 and itself.
    Since this is a bounded quantifier over Nat, it is decidable. -/

name: decidable_em
source_excerpt:
theorem decidable_em {P : Prop} [inst : Decidable P] : P ∨ ¬P :=
  match inst with
  | .isTrue h  => Or.inl h
  | .isFalse h => Or.inr h
doc_comment:
/-- Decidable excluded middle for decidable propositions:
    for any decidable P, we have P ∨ ¬P without Classical.em. -/

name: dvd_em
source_excerpt:
theorem dvd_em (a b : Nat) : (a ∣ b) ∨ ¬(a ∣ b) :=
  decidable_em
doc_comment:
/-- Divisibility on Nat is decidable, so Classical.em is not needed
    for excluded-middle on divisibility predicates. -/

  dvd_dec : ∀ a b : Nat, Decidable (a ∣ b)

    predicates, which are decidable. Therefore both sites are
    eliminable: Classical.em can be replaced by decidable_em. -/

name: em_eliminable

  dvd_dec := dvd_decidable
  dvd_em_constructive := dvd_em

name: BlockingMechanism

  | nf_confluence             -- Blocks (E): unique normal forms, decidable identity
  | star_autonomous_structure -- Blocks (P): no free self-products/diagonals

name: blocking_targets_injective

theorem blocking_targets_injective (m1 m2 : BlockingMechanism)
    (h : blocking_targets m1 = blocking_targets m2) : m1 = m2 := by
  cases m1 <;> cases m2 <;> simp [blocking_targets] at h <;> rfl

name: blocking_targets_surjective

  cases c
  · exact ⟨.k5_diagonal_discipline, rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨.nf_confluence, rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨.star_autonomous_structure, rfl⟩
doc_comment: /-- The blocking map is surjective: every component has a blocker. -/

  have hblock := r.resonance_blocks
  rw [hr] at hblock
  have := hblock h
  rw [this] at hc
  exact absurd hc (by decide)

source_excerpt:
structure CCCSide where
  /-- Free diagonals are available -/
  freeDiagonals : Bool
  /-- The Lawvere barrier applies -/
  lawvereBarrier : Bool
  /-- Consistency: free diagonals imply the barrier -/
  barrier_from_diag : freeDiagonals = true → lawvereBarrier = true
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D81] The CCC side of the dichotomy: cartesian-closed categories
    have free diagonal maps Δ : A → A × A, which enable the Lawvere
    fixed-point argument. Self-hosting is obstructed. -/

name: StarAutonomousSide
source_excerpt:
structure StarAutonomousSide where
  /-- Free diagonals are NOT available -/
  noFreeDiagonals : Bool
  /-- The Lawvere barrier does NOT apply -/
  noLawvereBarrier : Bool
  /-- Consistency: no free diagonals imply no barrier -/
  no_barrier_from_no_diag : noFreeDiagonals = true → noLawvereBarrier = true
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D81] The star-autonomous side of the dichotomy: star-autonomous
    categories replace the cartesian product × with the tensor ⊗.
    The diagonal Δ : A → A ⊗ A is not freely available — it must be
    earned. The Lawvere barrier does not apply. -/

name: ccc_side
source_excerpt:
def ccc_side : CCCSide where
  freeDiagonals := true
  lawvereBarrier := true
  barrier_from_diag := fun _ => rfl
doc_comment: /-- The CCC side: free diagonals, Lawvere barrier applies. -/

source_excerpt:

doc_comment: /-- The star-autonomous side: no free diagonals, no Lawvere barrier. -/

name: K5StructuralExclusion

structure K5StructuralExclusion where

  contraction_refused : k5_status .contraction = .refused
  /-- The diagonal-to-linear map sends noUnearnedDiagonals to noFreeContraction -/
  diagonal_is_linear : diag_to_linear .noUnearnedDiagonals = .noFreeContraction
  /-- τ is on the star-autonomous side -/
  tau_star_autonomous : StarAutonomousSide
  /-- On the star-autonomous side, the Lawvere barrier does not apply -/
  no_barrier : tau_star_autonomous.noLawvereBarrier = true
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T39] K5 Structural Exclusion Theorem.

    K5's diagonal discipline (DiagonalAspect.noUnearnedDiagonals) places τ
    on the star-autonomous side of the CCC-linear dichotomy. Specifically:
    1. K5 refuses free diagonals (contraction is refused — from Substrate.lean)
    2. Refusing free diagonals places τ on the star-autonomous side
    3. On the star-autonomous side, the Lawvere barrier does not apply
    4. Therefore: the standard obstruction to self-hosting is excluded -/

source_excerpt:

  no_barrier := rfl

/-- [I.D82] The enrichment frontier status classifies each transition
    of the enrichment ladder by its novelty relative to existing work. -/

name: e0_e1_status
source_excerpt: def e0_e1_status : EnrichmentFrontierStatus := .achieved
doc_comment:
/-- E₀ → E₁ status: achieved. Internalizing types in a categorical
    framework has multiple precedents (Altenkirch-Kaposi 2016,
    Bocquet-Kaposi-Sattler 2023, Moerdijk-Palmgren 2002). -/

name: e1_e2_status
source_excerpt: def e1_e2_status : EnrichmentFrontierStatus := .partiallyAchieved
doc_comment:
/-- E₁ → E₂ status: partially achieved. Internal proof-theoretic
    reasoning (Joyal) and resource-sensitive DTT (Abel 2023) exist
    separately; their combination is novel. -/

name: e2_e3_status
source_excerpt: def e2_e3_status : EnrichmentFrontierStatus := .unprecedented
doc_comment:
/-- E₂ → E₃ status: unprecedented. No formal system of CIC-level
    strength achieves full self-hosting. Willard (2001) achieves it
    below PA; Girard TX achieves fragments only. -/

name: allFrontierStatuses
source_excerpt:
def allFrontierStatuses : List EnrichmentFrontierStatus :=
  [.achieved, .partiallyAchieved, .unprecedented]
doc_comment: /-- All enrichment frontier statuses enumerated. -/

name: frontier_status_count
source_excerpt: theorem frontier_status_count : allFrontierStatuses.length = 3 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- There are exactly 3 frontier statuses. -/

name: e_transitions_distinct

theorem e_transitions_distinct :
    e0_e1_status ≠ e1_e2_status ∧
    e1_e2_status ≠ e2_e3_status ∧
    e0_e1_status ≠ e2_e3_status := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
doc_comment: /-- The three E-transitions have distinct statuses. -/

name: frontierRank
source_excerpt:
def frontierRank : EnrichmentFrontierStatus → Nat
  | .achieved          => 0
  | .partiallyAchieved => 1
  | .unprecedented     => 2
doc_comment:
/-- The enrichment frontier is strictly ordered: each transition
    is harder than the previous one. We encode this by assigning
    a difficulty rank (0, 1, 2) and verifying strict monotonicity. -/

name: e0_e1_easier_than_e1_e2
source_excerpt:
theorem e0_e1_easier_than_e1_e2 :
    frontierRank e0_e1_status < frontierRank e1_e2_status := by decide
doc_comment: /-- E₀→E₁ is easier than E₁→E₂. -/

name: e1_e2_easier_than_e2_e3
source_excerpt:
theorem e1_e2_easier_than_e2_e3 :
    frontierRank e1_e2_status < frontierRank e2_e3_status := by decide
doc_comment: /-- E₁→E₂ is easier than E₂→E₃. -/

name: max_frontier_rank

theorem max_frontier_rank :
    frontierRank e2_e3_status = 2 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- The maximum difficulty is 2 (unprecedented). -/

name: StructuralRule
source_excerpt:
inductive StructuralRule where
  | contraction   -- Γ, A, A ⊢ B  →  Γ, A ⊢ B  (use a resource twice)
  | weakening     -- Γ ⊢ B  →  Γ, A ⊢ B  (discard a resource)
  | exchange      -- Γ, A, B, Δ ⊢ C  →  Γ, B, A, Δ ⊢ C  (reorder)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open StructuralRule
doc_comment: /-- The three structural rules of classical sequent calculus. -/

name: ObjectLevelStatus
source_excerpt:
inductive ObjectLevelStatus where
  | refused    -- Rule is refused at the object level
  | preserved  -- Rule is preserved at the object level
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open ObjectLevelStatus
doc_comment: /-- The object-level status of a structural rule under K5's diagonal discipline. -/

name: k5_status
source_excerpt:
def k5_status : StructuralRule → ObjectLevelStatus
  | .contraction => .refused
  | .weakening   => .refused
  | .exchange    => .preserved
doc_comment:
/-- K5's classification: contraction and weakening are refused,
    exchange is preserved. -/

name: contraction_refused
source_excerpt: theorem contraction_refused : k5_status .contraction = .refused := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Contraction is refused at the object level. -/

name: weakening_refused
source_excerpt: theorem weakening_refused : k5_status .weakening = .refused := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Weakening is refused at the object level. -/

name: exchange_preserved
source_excerpt: theorem exchange_preserved : k5_status .exchange = .preserved := rfl
doc_comment: /-- Exchange is preserved at the object level. -/

name: allRules
source_excerpt: def allRules : List StructuralRule := [.contraction, .weakening, .exchange]
doc_comment: /-- The complete list of structural rules. -/

name: allRules_length
source_excerpt: theorem allRules_length : allRules.length = 3 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- There are exactly 3 structural rules. -/

name: refusedRules
source_excerpt:
def refusedRules : List StructuralRule :=
  allRules.filter (fun r => k5_status r == .refused)
doc_comment: /-- The rules refused by K5 at the object level. -/

name: preservedRules
source_excerpt:
def preservedRules : List StructuralRule :=
  allRules.filter (fun r => k5_status r == .preserved)
doc_comment: /-- The rules preserved by K5 at the object level. -/

name: refused_count
source_excerpt: theorem refused_count : refusedRules.length = 2 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Exactly 2 rules are refused. -/

name: preserved_count
source_excerpt: theorem preserved_count : preservedRules.length = 1 := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Exactly 1 rule is preserved. -/

name: refused_are
source_excerpt: theorem refused_are : refusedRules = [.contraction, .weakening] := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- The refused rules are contraction and weakening. -/

name: preserved_is
source_excerpt: theorem preserved_is : preservedRules = [.exchange] := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- The preserved rule is exchange. -/

name: count_partition
source_excerpt:
theorem count_partition :
    refusedRules.length + preservedRules.length = allRules.length := by native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Count consistency: refused + preserved = total. -/

name: diagonal_discipline_refuses_contraction
source_excerpt:
theorem diagonal_discipline_refuses_contraction :
    solenoidalGenerators.length < nonOmegaGenerators.length := by
  native_decide
doc_comment:
/-- The 3 solenoidal generators correspond to 3 controlled rewiring levels.
    Free contraction would require unbounded rewiring. Since K6 bounds
    the universe at 4 non-omega generators, free contraction is structurally
    impossible: there are fewer rewiring targets (3) than total channels (4),
    so at least one channel (α) is NEVER a rewiring target and serves as
    the scaffold. -/

name: diagonal_discipline_refuses_weakening
source_excerpt:
theorem diagonal_discipline_refuses_weakening :
    ∀ g : Generator, g ≠ omega → g ∈ nonOmegaGenerators :=
  nonOmega_complete
doc_comment:
/-- Every generator in `nonOmegaGenerators` is reachable by construction.
    No generator can be discarded — each participates in the orbit structure.
    The list is complete: every non-omega generator appears. -/

name: scaffold_invariant
source_excerpt: theorem scaffold_invariant : alpha ∉ solenoidalGenerators := by decide
doc_comment:
/-- The scaffold invariant: α is not a solenoidal generator.
    It is the unique channel that is never consumed by rewiring. -/

name: rewiring_budget
source_excerpt:
theorem rewiring_budget :
    solenoidalGenerators.length = nonOmegaGenerators.length - 1 :=
  rewiring_levels_eq_solenoidal
doc_comment:
/-- The rewiring budget is exactly 3 = 4 - 1.
    This means 3 levels of rewiring (addition, multiplication, exponentiation)
    and no room for a 4th. -/
