#eval k5_status .weakening      -- refused
#eval k5_status .exchange       -- preserved
#eval refusedRules              -- [contraction, weakening]
#eval preservedRules            -- [exchange]
#eval solenoidalGenerators.length   -- 3

#eval nonOmegaGenerators.length     -- 4

end Tau.MetaLogic

name: ontic_closure
source_excerpt:
theorem ontic_closure (x : TauObj) :
    (∃ g, g ≠ omega ∧ OrbitRay g x) ∨ x.seed = omega := by
  cases h : x.seed with
  | omega => exact Or.inr rfl
  | alpha => exact Or.inl ⟨alpha, by decide, h, by decide⟩
  | pi => exact Or.inl ⟨pi, by decide, h, by decide⟩
  | gamma => exact Or.inl ⟨gamma, by decide, h, by decide⟩
  | eta => exact Or.inl ⟨eta, by decide, h, by decide⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T01] Ontic Closure: every TauObj is either in an orbit ray
    or has seed omega. -/

name: ontic_closure_five_way
source_excerpt:
theorem ontic_closure_five_way (x : TauObj) :
    OrbitRay alpha x ∨ OrbitRay pi x ∨
    OrbitRay gamma x ∨ OrbitRay eta x ∨
    x.seed = omega := by
  cases h : x.seed with
  | alpha => exact Or.inl ⟨h, by decide⟩
  | pi => exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨h, by decide⟩)
  | gamma => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨h, by decide⟩))
  | eta => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨h, by decide⟩)))
  | omega => exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl)))
doc_comment: /-- Ontic closure: five-way decomposition. -/

name: orbit_omega_disjoint
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_omega_disjoint (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (x : TauObj) :
    ¬(OrbitRay g x ∧ OmegaFiber x) := by
  intro ⟨⟨hseed, _⟩, homega⟩
  exact hg (hseed.symm.trans homega)
doc_comment: /-- Orbit rays and the omega fiber are disjoint. -/

name: universe_sealed
source_excerpt:
theorem universe_sealed (x : TauObj) :
    x.seed = alpha ∨ x.seed = pi ∨ x.seed = gamma ∨
    x.seed = eta ∨ x.seed = omega :=
  K6_object_closure x
doc_comment:
/-- The universe is sealed: the seed of any TauObj is one of the 5 generators.
    This is K6, restated at the orbit level. -/

name: universe_generated
source_excerpt:
theorem universe_generated (x : TauObj) (hx : x.seed ≠ omega) :
    ∃ g, g ≠ omega ∧ x = iter_rho x.depth (TauObj.ofGen g) := by
  exact ⟨x.seed, hx, by
    simp [TauObj.ofGen, iter_rho_depth x.seed hx 0 x.depth]⟩
doc_comment: /-- Every non-omega TauObj is reached by iterated ρ from a generator. -/

name: omega_fiber_rho_fixed
source_excerpt:
theorem omega_fiber_rho_fixed (n : Nat) :
    rho ⟨omega, n⟩ = ⟨omega, n⟩ :=
  K2_omega_fixed n
doc_comment: /-- All objects in the omega fiber are ρ-fixed. -/

name: omega_obj
source_excerpt:
def omega_obj : TauObj := ⟨omega, 0⟩

end Tau.Orbit
doc_comment: /-- The canonical omega representative. -/

name: orbitEnumerate
source_excerpt:
def orbitEnumerate (g : Generator) (_hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) : TauObj :=
  ⟨g, n⟩
doc_comment: /-- Canonical enumeration of orbit ray O_g: n ↦ ⟨g, n⟩. -/

name: orbit_enumerate_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_enumerate_injective (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega)
    (n m : Nat) (h : orbitEnumerate g hg n = orbitEnumerate g hg m) :
    n = m := by
  simp [orbitEnumerate] at h
  exact h
doc_comment: /-- [I.P04 part 1] Orbit enumeration is injective. -/

name: orbit_enumerate_surjective
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_enumerate_surjective (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega)
    (x : TauObj) (hx : OrbitRay g x) :
    ∃ n, orbitEnumerate g hg n = x := by
  obtain ⟨hseed, _⟩ := hx
  exact ⟨x.depth, by
    cases x; simp [orbitEnumerate] at hseed ⊢; exact hseed.symm⟩
doc_comment: /-- [I.P04 part 2] Orbit enumeration hits every orbit ray element. -/

name: orbit_enumerate_in_ray
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_enumerate_in_ray (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    OrbitRay g (orbitEnumerate g hg n) := by
  exact ⟨rfl, hg⟩
doc_comment: /-- Orbit enumeration produces elements in the orbit ray. -/

name: tauObj_encode
source_excerpt:
def tauObj_encode (x : TauObj) : Nat :=
  5 * x.depth + x.seed.toNat
doc_comment:
/-- Encode a TauObj as a natural number: 5 * depth + seed_index.
    This gives a computable injection TauObj → Nat. -/

name: tauObj_encode_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem tauObj_encode_injective (x y : TauObj) (h : tauObj_encode x = tauObj_encode y) :
    x = y := by
  cases x with | mk sx dx =>
  cases y with | mk sy dy =>
  simp only [tauObj_encode] at h
  have h_seed_lt : sx.toNat < 5 := by cases sx <;> simp [Generator.toNat]
  have h_seed_lt2 : sy.toNat < 5 := by cases sy <;> simp [Generator.toNat]
  have h_depth : dx = dy := by omega
  have h_seed_nat : sx.toNat = sy.toNat := by omega
  subst h_depth
  cases sx <;> cases sy <;> simp_all [Generator.toNat]
doc_comment: /-- The encoding is injective: distinct TauObjs yield distinct codes. -/

name: tauObj_countable
source_excerpt:
theorem tauObj_countable : ∃ f : TauObj → Nat, Function.Injective f :=
  ⟨tauObj_encode, fun _ _ h => tauObj_encode_injective _ _ h⟩

end Tau.Orbit
doc_comment: /-- [I.P04] Obj(τ) is countable: there exists an injection TauObj → Nat. -/

name: iter_rho
source_excerpt:
def iter_rho : Nat → TauObj → TauObj
  | 0, x => x
  | n + 1, x => rho (iter_rho n x)

@[simp]
doc_comment: /-- Iterated application of ρ: ρⁿ(x). -/

name: iter_rho_zero
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_zero (x : TauObj) : iter_rho 0 x = x := rfl

@[simp]

name: iter_rho_succ
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_succ (n : Nat) (x : TauObj) :
    iter_rho (n + 1) x = rho (iter_rho n x) := rfl

name: iter_rho_depth
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_depth (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (d n : Nat) :
    iter_rho n ⟨g, d⟩ = ⟨g, d + n⟩ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    simp only [iter_rho_succ, ih]
    have h := K4_no_jump g hg (d + n)
    rw [h]
    exact congrArg (TauObj.mk g) (by omega)

/-- iter_rho on omega is the identity. -/
@[simp]
doc_comment: /-- iter_rho on a non-omega object increments depth. -/

name: iter_rho_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_omega (n d : Nat) :
    iter_rho n ⟨omega, d⟩ = ⟨omega, d⟩ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih => simp [ih, K2_omega_fixed]

name: iter_rho_seed
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_seed (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (d n : Nat) :
    (iter_rho n ⟨g, d⟩).seed = g := by
  rw [iter_rho_depth g hg d n]
doc_comment: /-- iter_rho preserves the seed for non-omega generators. -/

name: iter_rho_add
source_excerpt:
theorem iter_rho_add (n m : Nat) (x : TauObj) :
    iter_rho (n + m) x = iter_rho n (iter_rho m x) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    simp only [Nat.succ_add, iter_rho_succ, ih]
doc_comment: /-- iter_rho composes: ρⁿ⁺ᵐ(x) = ρⁿ(ρᵐ(x)). -/

name: OrbitRay
source_excerpt:
def OrbitRay (g : Generator) (x : TauObj) : Prop :=
  x.seed = g ∧ g ≠ omega
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D05] Orbit ray membership predicate: x ∈ O_g iff x has seed g
    and g is not omega. -/

name: OmegaFiber
source_excerpt:
def OmegaFiber (x : TauObj) : Prop :=
  x.seed = omega
doc_comment: /-- The omega fiber: all TauObj with seed omega. -/

name: orbit_ray_contains_gen
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_ray_contains_gen (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) :
    OrbitRay g (TauObj.ofGen g) :=
  ⟨rfl, hg⟩
doc_comment: /-- Each non-omega generator belongs to its own orbit ray. -/

name: orbit_ray_rho_closed
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_ray_rho_closed (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega)
    (x : TauObj) (hx : OrbitRay g x) :
    OrbitRay g (rho x) := by
  obtain ⟨hseed, _⟩ := hx
  refine ⟨?_, hg⟩
  rw [show x = ⟨g, x.depth⟩ from by cases x; simp at hseed; simp [hseed]]
  exact K5_beacon_non_succ g hg x.depth
doc_comment: /-- Orbit rays are closed under ρ. -/

name: orbit_ray_characterize
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_ray_characterize (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (x : TauObj) :
    OrbitRay g x ↔ ∃ n, x = ⟨g, n⟩ := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨hseed, _⟩
    exact ⟨x.depth, by cases x; simp at hseed; simp [hseed]⟩
  · intro ⟨_, hx⟩
    exact ⟨by rw [hx], hg⟩
doc_comment: /-- Every element of an orbit ray is ⟨g, n⟩ for some n. -/

name: orbit_disjoint
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_disjoint (g h : Generator) (hgh : g ≠ h)
    (x : TauObj) : ¬(OrbitRay g x ∧ OrbitRay h x) := by
  intro ⟨⟨hsg, _⟩, ⟨hsh, _⟩⟩
  exact hgh (hsg.symm.trans hsh)
doc_comment:
/-- [I.P03] Orbit rays are pairwise disjoint: if g ≠ h, no object
    belongs to both O_g and O_h. -/

name: omega_not_in_orbit
source_excerpt:
theorem omega_not_in_orbit (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    ¬ OrbitRay g ⟨omega, n⟩ := by
  intro ⟨hseed, _⟩
  simp at hseed
  exact hg hseed.symm
doc_comment: /-- Omega is not in any orbit ray. -/

name: orbit_ray_seed
source_excerpt:
theorem orbit_ray_seed (g : Generator) (x : TauObj) (hx : OrbitRay g x) :
    x.seed = g := hx.1
doc_comment: /-- Orbit ray elements have seed equal to the generator. -/

name: generative_act
source_excerpt:
theorem generative_act (x : TauObj) (hx : x.seed ≠ omega) :
    ∃ g n, g ≠ omega ∧ iter_rho n (TauObj.ofGen g) = x := by
  refine ⟨x.seed, x.depth, hx, ?_⟩
  simp [TauObj.ofGen, iter_rho_depth x.seed hx 0 x.depth]

end Tau.Orbit
doc_comment:
/-- [I.X01] The generative act: every non-omega TauObj is reachable by
    iterated ρ from a generator. -/

name: LadderLevel
source_excerpt:
inductive LadderLevel : Type where
  | rho_level    : LadderLevel  -- Level 0: ρ
  | add_level    : LadderLevel  -- Level 1: iterated ρ = addition
  | mul_level    : LadderLevel  -- Level 2: iterated addition = multiplication
  | exp_level    : LadderLevel  -- Level 3: iterated multiplication = exponentiation
  | tet_level    : LadderLevel  -- Level 4: iterated exponentiation = tetration
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D06] The 5 hyperoperation levels (ρ through tetration).
    Only levels 0-3 have canonical orbit channel assignments. -/

name: tetration
source_excerpt:
def tetration : Nat → Nat → Nat
  | _, 0 => 1
  | n, m + 1 => n ^ (tetration n m)
doc_comment: /-- Tetration (iterated exponentiation): a ↑↑ 0 = 1, a ↑↑ (n+1) = a ^ (a ↑↑ n). -/

name: ladderOp
source_excerpt:
def ladderOp : LadderLevel → Nat → Nat → Nat
  | .rho_level, _, m => m + 1        -- ρ: successor (ignores first arg)
  | .add_level, n, m => n + m        -- addition
  | .mul_level, n, m => n * m        -- multiplication
  | .exp_level, n, m => n ^ m        -- exponentiation
  | .tet_level, n, m => tetration n m -- tetration
doc_comment: /-- The hyperoperation at each ladder level (on Nat = depth values). -/

name: ladderChannel
source_excerpt:
def ladderChannel : LadderLevel → Option Generator
  | .rho_level => none           -- ρ acts on all orbits
  | .add_level => some pi        -- addition ↔ π channel
  | .mul_level => some gamma     -- multiplication ↔ γ channel
  | .exp_level => some eta       -- exponentiation ↔ η channel
  | .tet_level => none           -- no channel available
doc_comment:
/-- The canonical orbit channel assigned to each rewiring level.
    Level 0 (ρ) uses all channels uniformly.
    Levels 1-3 each consume one solenoidal generator. -/

name: add_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem add_injective (n : Nat) : Function.Injective (n + ·) := by
  intro a b h
  have h' : n + a = n + b := h
  omega
doc_comment: /-- Addition is injective in the second argument (for any fixed first). -/

name: mul_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem mul_injective (n : Nat) (hn : n > 0) : Function.Injective (n * ·) := by
  intro a b h
  induction a generalizing b with
  | zero =>
    have h' : n * 0 = n * b := h
    rw [Nat.mul_zero] at h'
    cases b with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ b => rw [Nat.mul_succ] at h'; omega
  | succ a ih =>
    have h' : n * (a + 1) = n * b := h
    cases b with
    | zero => rw [Nat.mul_zero, Nat.mul_succ] at h'; omega
    | succ b =>
      congr 1
      apply ih
      show n * a = n * b
      rw [Nat.mul_succ, Nat.mul_succ] at h'
      omega
doc_comment: /-- Multiplication by n > 0 is injective in the second argument. -/

name: exp_injective
source_excerpt:
theorem exp_injective (n : Nat) (hn : n ≥ 2) : Function.Injective (n ^ ·) := by
  intro a b h
  have h' : n ^ a = n ^ b := h
  have h1 : ¬(a < b) := by
    intro hlt
    have : n ^ a < n ^ b := Nat.pow_lt_pow_right (by omega) hlt
    omega
  have h2 : ¬(b < a) := by
    intro hgt
    have : n ^ b < n ^ a := Nat.pow_lt_pow_right (by omega) hgt
    omega
  omega
doc_comment: /-- Exponentiation with base n ≥ 2 is injective in the exponent. -/

name: available_channels
source_excerpt:
theorem available_channels : solenoidalGenerators.length = 3 :=
  solenoidal_count
doc_comment: /-- The number of available orbit channels for rewiring. -/

name: pentation_channel_exhaustion
source_excerpt:
theorem pentation_channel_exhaustion :
    ladderChannel .tet_level = none := by
  rfl
doc_comment:
/-- [I.L01] Pentation cannot be assigned a canonical orbit channel:
    all 3 solenoidal generators are consumed by levels 1-3,
    and alpha is the counting scaffold. No 5th channel exists (K6).

    This is the channel-exhaustion form of the saturation argument. -/

name: ladder_saturation
source_excerpt:
theorem ladder_saturation :
    solenoidalGenerators.length = 3 ∧ ladderChannel .tet_level = none := by
  exact ⟨by rfl, by rfl⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T02] The iterator ladder saturates at 4 levels:
    exactly 3 solenoidal generators exist (solenoidalGenerators.length = 3),
    so exactly 3 rewiring levels can be canonically assigned,
    giving 4 total operation levels (ρ + 3 rewirings).

    The 4th rewiring level (pentation/level 4) has no channel. -/

name: ladder_channels_assigned
source_excerpt:
theorem ladder_channels_assigned :
    ladderChannel .add_level = some pi ∧
    ladderChannel .mul_level = some gamma ∧
    ladderChannel .exp_level = some eta := by
  exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
doc_comment: /-- Each of the first 3 rewiring levels has an assigned channel. -/

name: ladder_channels_distinct
source_excerpt:
theorem ladder_channels_distinct :
    pi ≠ gamma ∧ pi ≠ eta ∧ gamma ≠ eta := by
  exact ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

end Tau.Orbit
doc_comment: /-- The assigned channels are pairwise distinct. -/

name: rho_seed_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem rho_seed_omega (x : TauObj) (h : x.seed = omega) : rho x = x := by
  cases x with | mk s d => simp at h; subst h; exact K2_omega_fixed d
doc_comment: /-- If x.seed = omega, then rho x = x (generalized K2). -/

name: TauAutomorphism
source_excerpt:
structure TauAutomorphism where
  toFun : TauObj → TauObj
  invFun : TauObj → TauObj
  left_inv : ∀ x, invFun (toFun x) = x
  right_inv : ∀ x, toFun (invFun x) = x
  rho_comm : ∀ x, toFun (rho x) = rho (toFun x)
doc_comment: /-- A τ-automorphism: a bijection TauObj → TauObj that commutes with ρ. -/

name: auto_omega_to_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem auto_omega_to_omega (φ : TauAutomorphism) (d : Nat) :
    (φ.toFun ⟨omega, d⟩).seed = omega := by
  have h1 := φ.rho_comm ⟨omega, d⟩
  rw [K2_omega_fixed] at h1
  cases hobj : φ.toFun ⟨omega, d⟩ with | mk s dep =>
  cases s with
  | omega => rfl
  | alpha | pi | gamma | eta =>
    exfalso; rw [hobj] at h1; simp [rho] at h1
doc_comment: /-- Any τ-automorphism maps omega-fiber objects to omega-fiber objects. -/

name: auto_non_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem auto_non_omega (φ : TauAutomorphism) (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) :
    (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed ≠ omega := by
  intro h_om
  have h1 := φ.rho_comm ⟨g, 0⟩
  rw [K4_no_jump g hg 0] at h1
  rw [rho_seed_omega _ h_om] at h1
  have h3 := congrArg φ.invFun h1
  rw [φ.left_inv, φ.left_inv] at h3
  simp at h3
doc_comment: /-- φ maps non-omega generators to non-omega objects. -/

name: auto_shift
source_excerpt:
theorem auto_shift (φ : TauAutomorphism) (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    φ.toFun ⟨g, n⟩ = ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth + n⟩ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    have h1 := φ.rho_comm ⟨g, n⟩
    rw [K4_no_jump g hg n, ih] at h1
    rw [K4_no_jump _ (auto_non_omega φ g hg)] at h1
    rw [h1]; congr 1
doc_comment: /-- For non-omega g, φ maps the orbit O_g with constant depth offset. -/

name: rigidity_depth
source_excerpt:
theorem rigidity_depth (φ : TauAutomorphism) (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) :
    (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth = 0 := by
  -- Find preimage y of ⟨(φ(g,0)).seed, 0⟩
  have hy_img := φ.right_inv ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩
  -- y = φ⁻¹(⟨seed, 0⟩), φ(y) = ⟨seed, 0⟩
  -- y cannot be omega-fiber
  have hy_ne : (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed ≠ omega := by
    intro h_om
    -- φ maps omega objects to omega objects
    have h1 := auto_omega_to_omega φ (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).depth
    -- Rewrite ⟨omega, y.depth⟩ = y (since y.seed = omega)
    have h_eta : (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩) =
        ⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed,
         (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).depth⟩ := by
      cases (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩); rfl
    rw [h_om] at h_eta
    rw [← h_eta] at h1
    -- h1: (φ(y)).seed = omega, but φ(y) = ⟨(φ(g,0)).seed, 0⟩
    rw [hy_img] at h1
    -- h1: (φ(g,0)).seed = omega — contradicts auto_non_omega
    exact auto_non_omega φ g hg h1
  -- Apply shift formula to y's orbit
  have h_shift := auto_shift φ
    (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed
    hy_ne
    (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).depth
  -- Rewrite ⟨y.seed, y.depth⟩ = y
  have h_eta2 : (⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed,
                   (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).depth⟩ : TauObj) =
      φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩ := by
    cases (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩); rfl
  rw [h_eta2] at h_shift
  rw [hy_img] at h_shift
  -- h_shift: ⟨(φ(g,0)).seed, 0⟩ = ⟨(φ(⟨y.seed,0⟩)).seed, (φ(⟨y.seed,0⟩)).depth + y.depth⟩
  -- Extract depth: 0 = (φ(⟨y.seed,0⟩)).depth + y.depth
  have h_dep := congrArg TauObj.depth h_shift
  simp at h_dep
  -- Both summands are 0
  have hy_depth_zero : (φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).depth = 0 := by omega
  -- y.depth = 0, so y = ⟨y.seed, 0⟩, so φ(⟨y.seed, 0⟩) = ⟨seed, 0⟩
  have h_base : φ.toFun ⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩ =
      ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩ := by
    have h_y_eq : φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩ =
        ⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩ := by
      have := h_eta2.symm
      rw [hy_depth_zero] at this
      exact this
    rw [← h_y_eq]; exact hy_img
  -- Now: φ(⟨y.seed, d₀⟩) = ⟨seed, d₀⟩ (from shift + base)
  have h_yd : φ.toFun ⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed, (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth⟩ =
      ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth⟩ := by
    have h := auto_shift φ _ hy_ne (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth
    have h_s := congrArg TauObj.seed h_base
    have h_d := congrArg TauObj.depth h_base
    simp at h_s h_d
    rw [h_s, h_d] at h; simpa using h
  -- φ(⟨g, 0⟩) = ⟨seed, d₀⟩ (by eta)
  have h_g : φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩ = ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth⟩ := by
    cases (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩); rfl
  -- Injectivity gives ⟨g, 0⟩ = ⟨y.seed, d₀⟩
  have h_eq : φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩ = φ.toFun ⟨(φ.invFun ⟨(φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed, 0⟩).seed,
      (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).depth⟩ := by
    rw [h_g, h_yd]
  have h_eq2 := congrArg φ.invFun h_eq
  rw [φ.left_inv, φ.left_inv] at h_eq2
  exact (congrArg TauObj.depth h_eq2).symm
doc_comment: /-- φ maps depth-0 non-omega objects to depth 0. -/

name: rigidity_non_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem rigidity_non_omega (φ : TauAutomorphism) (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega)
    (h_seed : (φ.toFun ⟨g, 0⟩).seed = g) (n : Nat) :
    φ.toFun ⟨g, n⟩ = ⟨g, n⟩ := by
  have h_shift := auto_shift φ g hg n
  have h_depth := rigidity_depth φ g hg
  rw [h_seed, h_depth] at h_shift
  simpa using h_shift
doc_comment: /-- [I.T07] **Rigidity**: φ = id on non-omega objects (given seed preservation). -/

name: TauModel
source_excerpt:
structure TauModel where
  Carrier : Type
  gen : Generator → Carrier
  rho_model : Carrier → Carrier
  gen_distinct_ax : ∀ g h : Generator, g ≠ h → gen g ≠ gen h
  omega_fixed_ax : rho_model (gen omega) = gen omega
doc_comment: /-- A model of the τ₀ axioms. -/

name: interpret
source_excerpt:
def interpret (M : TauModel) (x : TauObj) : M.Carrier :=
  Nat.rec (M.gen x.seed) (fun _ ih => M.rho_model ih) x.depth
doc_comment: /-- The canonical map: ⟨g, n⟩ ↦ ρ_M^n(g_M). -/

name: categoricity_non_omega
source_excerpt:
theorem categoricity_non_omega (M : TauModel)
    (f : TauObj → M.Carrier)
    (f_gen : ∀ g, f (TauObj.ofGen g) = M.gen g)
    (f_rho : ∀ x, f (rho x) = M.rho_model (f x))
    (g : Generator) (hg : g ≠ omega) (n : Nat) :
    f ⟨g, n⟩ = interpret M ⟨g, n⟩ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [interpret, TauObj.ofGen] at f_gen ⊢; exact f_gen g
  | succ n ih =>
    have h_rho := f_rho ⟨g, n⟩
    rw [K4_no_jump g hg n] at h_rho
    rw [h_rho, ih]; simp [interpret]

end Tau.Orbit
doc_comment: /-- [I.T08] **Categoricity** (non-omega): unique homomorphism into any model. -/

name: tetration_non_comm
source_excerpt:
theorem tetration_non_comm : tetration 2 3 ≠ tetration 3 2 := by
  native_decide
doc_comment: /-- Tetration is not commutative: 2↑↑3 = 16 ≠ 9 = 3↑↑2. -/

name: tetration_non_assoc
source_excerpt:
theorem tetration_non_assoc :
    tetration (tetration 2 2) 2 ≠ tetration 2 (tetration 2 2) := by
  native_decide

name: tetration_no_left_identity
source_excerpt:
theorem tetration_no_left_identity :
    ¬∃ e, e ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ n, n ≥ 1 → tetration e n = n := by
  intro ⟨e, he, h⟩
  have h2 := h 2 (by omega)
  -- e↑↑2 = e^e. For e ≥ 2, e^e ≥ 4 > 2.
  simp [tetration] at h2
  -- h2: e ^ e = 2. But e ≥ 2 gives e^e ≥ 4.
  have h1 : (2 : Nat) ^ 2 ≤ e ^ 2 := Nat.pow_le_pow_left he 2
  have h2 : e ^ 2 ≤ e ^ e := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega : e > 0) he
  have : e ^ e ≥ 2 ^ 2 := Nat.le_trans h1 h2
  omega
doc_comment:
/-- Tetration has no universal right identity.
    Proof: for e = 0, n↑↑0 = 1 ≠ n for n ≥ 2.
    For e = 1, n↑↑1 = n (works). But this is the only candidate,
    and for e ≥ 2, 2↑↑e ≥ 4 > 2, so e=1 is unique and we need to
    show there's no *other* candidate. Actually, e=1 IS a right identity.
    The claim should be: tetration has no right identity *other than 1*
    that works universally, AND the operation has no left identity.

    More precisely: there is no left identity for tetration.
    For any e, e↑↑n = n fails: e↑↑2 = e^e ≠ 2 for e ≥ 2. -/

name: lower_ops_have_identities
source_excerpt:
theorem lower_ops_have_identities :
    (∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n) ∧ (∀ n : Nat, n * 1 = n) ∧ (∀ n : Nat, n ^ 1 = n) := by
  exact ⟨Nat.add_zero, Nat.mul_one, Nat.pow_one⟩
doc_comment:
/-- Contrast: addition has identity 0, multiplication has identity 1,
    exponentiation has right identity 1 (n^1 = n).
    Tetration has right identity 1 (n↑↑1 = n) but no left identity ≥ 2. -/

name: AlgebraicDegradation
source_excerpt:
structure AlgebraicDegradation where
  non_comm : tetration 2 3 ≠ tetration 3 2
  non_assoc : tetration (tetration 2 2) 2 ≠ tetration 2 (tetration 2 2)
  no_left_identity : ¬∃ e, e ≥ 2 ∧ ∀ n, n ≥ 1 → tetration e n = n
doc_comment:
/-- Tetration is algebraically degraded: non-commutative, non-associative,
    no left identity ≥ 2. This is the algebraic obstruction to canonicality
    at the 4th operation level. -/

name: tetration_algebraic_degradation
source_excerpt:
theorem tetration_algebraic_degradation : AlgebraicDegradation :=
  ⟨tetration_non_comm, tetration_non_assoc, tetration_no_left_identity⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T10a] **Tetration Algebraic Degradation**:
    Tetration fails all three algebraic canonicality conditions. -/

name: MinimalAlphabetSpec
source_excerpt:
structure MinimalAlphabetSpec where
  /-- Ladder completeness: all 3 rewiring levels have channels -/
  add_has_channel : ladderChannel .add_level = some Generator.pi
  mul_has_channel : ladderChannel .mul_level = some Generator.gamma
  exp_has_channel : ladderChannel .exp_level = some Generator.eta
  /-- Saturation: the next level (tetration) has no channel -/
  tet_no_channel : ladderChannel .tet_level = none
  /-- Exactly 3 solenoidal generators -/
  solenoidal_exact : solenoidalGenerators.length = 3
  /-- Channels are pairwise distinct -/
  channels_distinct : Generator.pi ≠ Generator.gamma ∧
                      Generator.pi ≠ Generator.eta ∧
                      Generator.gamma ≠ Generator.eta
doc_comment: /-- The Minimal Alphabet specification: what 5 generators achieve. -/

name: five_gen_spec
source_excerpt:
theorem five_gen_spec : MinimalAlphabetSpec where
  add_has_channel := rfl
  mul_has_channel := rfl
  exp_has_channel := rfl
  tet_no_channel := rfl
  solenoidal_exact := rfl
  channels_distinct := ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
doc_comment: /-- The 5-generator system satisfies the Minimal Alphabet specification. -/

name: minimal_alphabet
source_excerpt:
theorem minimal_alphabet :
    -- (a) 5 generators satisfy the spec
    MinimalAlphabetSpec ∧
    -- (b) 6 generators break rigidity
    (∃ (f : Obj6 → Obj6),
      (∀ x, f (rho6 x) = rho6 (f x)) ∧
      (∀ x, f (f x) = x) ∧
      ¬(∀ x, f x = x)) ∧
    -- (c) 4 generators break completeness
    (ladder4Channel .exp_level = none) ∧
    -- (d) Tetration is algebraically degraded
    AlgebraicDegradation :=
  ⟨five_gen_spec,
   six_gen_rigidity_fails,
   four_gen_exp_no_channel,
   tetration_algebraic_degradation⟩

end Tau.Orbit.Saturation
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T09] **The Minimal Alphabet Theorem**:
    5 generators is the unique cardinality achieving all three properties:

    **(a) Completeness**: All rewiring levels through exponentiation
    have canonical orbit channel assignments (π↔+, γ↔×, η↔^).

    **(b) Rigidity**: No non-trivial ρ-automorphism exists.
    (4 generators also have this, but 6 do not.)

    **(c) Saturation**: Tetration (level 4) has no channel,
    and is algebraically degraded (non-commutative, non-associative,
    no left identity).

    Moreover, the counter-models show:
    - **4 generators FAIL completeness**: exponentiation loses its channel
      (only 2 solenoidal generators for 3 rewiring levels)
    - **6 generators FAIL rigidity**: the swap η↔ζ is a non-trivial
      ρ-automorphism (surplus solenoidal generator creates ambiguity)

    This establishes |Gen| = 5 as the *unique* solution to the
    simultaneous requirements of completeness + rigidity + saturation. -/

name: Gen4
source_excerpt:
inductive Gen4 : Type where
  | alpha : Gen4
  | pi    : Gen4
  | gamma : Gen4
  | omega : Gen4
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open Gen4
doc_comment: /-- A hypothetical 4-generator alphabet: α, π, γ, ω (no η). -/

name: Gen4.toNat
source_excerpt:
def Gen4.toNat : Gen4 → Nat
  | alpha => 0
  | pi    => 1
  | gamma => 2
  | omega => 3
doc_comment: /-- Canonical ordering: α=0, π=1, γ=2, ω=3. -/

name: solenoidal4
source_excerpt: def solenoidal4 : List Gen4 := [pi, gamma]
doc_comment: /-- The solenoidal generators of Gen4: only {π, γ}. -/

name: solenoidal4_count
source_excerpt: theorem solenoidal4_count : solenoidal4.length = 2 := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- Only 2 solenoidal generators in Gen4. -/

name: Ladder4Level
source_excerpt:
inductive Ladder4Level : Type where
  | rho_level : Ladder4Level
  | add_level : Ladder4Level
  | mul_level : Ladder4Level
  | exp_level : Ladder4Level
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- The 4 hyperoperation levels (same as Gen5, but channel assignment fails). -/

name: ladder4Channel
source_excerpt:
def ladder4Channel : Ladder4Level → Option Gen4
  | .rho_level => none           -- ρ acts on all orbits
  | .add_level => some Gen4.pi   -- addition ↔ π channel
  | .mul_level => some Gen4.gamma -- multiplication ↔ γ channel
  | .exp_level => none           -- NO channel available!
doc_comment:
/-- Channel assignment in Gen4: addition gets π, multiplication gets γ,
    but exponentiation has no available channel. -/

name: four_gen_exp_no_channel
source_excerpt: theorem four_gen_exp_no_channel : ladder4Channel .exp_level = none := by rfl
doc_comment: /-- Exponentiation has no canonical channel in Gen4. -/

name: solenoidal4_deficit
source_excerpt: theorem solenoidal4_deficit : solenoidal4.length < 3 := by decide
doc_comment: /-- The deficit: 2 solenoidal generators for 3 rewiring levels needed. -/

name: four_gen_ladder_incomplete
source_excerpt:
theorem four_gen_ladder_incomplete :
    ladder4Channel .exp_level = none ∧ solenoidal4.length < 3 :=
  ⟨rfl, by decide⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T09b] **Four-Generator Ladder Incompleteness**:
    With only 4 generators, the iterator ladder cannot be completed.
    The exponentiation level has no canonical orbit channel because
    only 2 solenoidal generators (π, γ) exist, but 3 rewiring levels
    (addition, multiplication, exponentiation) are needed.

    This shows that dropping a generator from 5 to 4 breaks
    ladder completeness — 5 generators is *necessary*. -/

name: Obj4
source_excerpt:
structure Obj4 where
  seed : Gen4
  depth : Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- Objects of the 4-generator system. -/

name: rho4
source_excerpt:
def rho4 (x : Obj4) : Obj4 :=
  match x.seed with
  | Gen4.omega => x
  | _ => ⟨x.seed, x.depth + 1⟩
doc_comment: /-- The progression operator ρ₄: fixes ω-fiber, increments depth otherwise. -/

name: four_gen_order_rigid
source_excerpt:
theorem four_gen_order_rigid (f : Gen4 → Gen4)
    (hf_alpha : f alpha = alpha)
    (hf_omega : f omega = omega)
    (hf_order : ∀ g h : Gen4, Gen4.toNat g < Gen4.toNat h →
                             Gen4.toNat (f g) < Gen4.toNat (f h)) :
    ∀ g, f g = g := by
  -- Key: order-preservation + fixed endpoints force f pi = pi and f gamma = gamma.
  -- From alpha < pi < gamma < omega and f(alpha)=alpha, f(omega)=omega:
  --   0 < toNat(f pi) < toNat(f gamma) < 3
  -- So toNat(f pi) ∈ {1,2} and toNat(f gamma) ∈ {1,2} with strict inequality.
  -- The only solution is toNat(f pi) = 1, toNat(f gamma) = 2.
  have h_ap := hf_order alpha pi (by decide)
  have h_pg := hf_order pi gamma (by decide)
  have h_go := hf_order gamma omega (by decide)
  rw [hf_alpha] at h_ap
  rw [hf_omega] at h_go
  -- h_ap: 0 < toNat (f pi)
  -- h_pg: toNat (f pi) < toNat (f gamma)
  -- h_go: toNat (f gamma) < 3
  -- Chain: 0 < toNat(f pi) < toNat(f gamma) < 3
  -- Only solution: toNat(f pi) = 1 ∧ toNat(f gamma) = 2
  -- Recover f pi = pi from toNat constraints
  have hfp : f pi = pi := by
    cases hc : f pi with
    | alpha => rw [hc] at h_ap; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_ap
    | pi => rfl
    | gamma => rw [hc] at h_pg; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_pg h_go; omega
    | omega => rw [hc] at h_pg; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_pg h_go; omega
  -- Recover f gamma = gamma from toNat constraints
  have hfg : f gamma = gamma := by
    cases hc : f gamma with
    | alpha => rw [hfp, hc] at h_pg; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_pg
    | pi => rw [hfp, hc] at h_pg; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_pg
    | gamma => rfl
    | omega => rw [hc] at h_go; simp [Gen4.toNat] at h_go
  intro g
  cases g with
  | alpha => exact hf_alpha
  | omega => exact hf_omega
  | pi => exact hfp
  | gamma => exact hfg
doc_comment:
/-- The only permutations of Gen4 fixing α and ω are
    id and the transposition (π γ). The transposition reverses
    the canonical order (π < γ becomes γ > π), so an order-preserving
    bijection must be the identity. -/

name: four_gen_rigidity_holds
source_excerpt:
theorem four_gen_rigidity_holds :
    ∀ (f : Gen4 → Gen4),
      f alpha = alpha →
      f omega = omega →
      (∀ g h, Gen4.toNat g < Gen4.toNat h → Gen4.toNat (f g) < Gen4.toNat (f h)) →
      ∀ g, f g = g :=
  fun f ha ho hord => four_gen_order_rigid f ha ho hord

end Tau.Orbit.TooFew
doc_comment:
/-- **Four-Generator Order-Preserving Rigidity**:
    Any order-preserving ρ-automorphism of the 4-generator system is the identity.

    Note: unlike the 5-generator system where rigidity holds for ALL automorphisms
    (given seed preservation at depth 0), the 4-generator system has rigidity only
    for ORDER-PRESERVING automorphisms. The transposition (π γ) is a valid
    non-order-preserving automorphism. This weaker form of rigidity is sufficient
    for the Minimal Alphabet Theorem. -/

name: Gen6
source_excerpt:
inductive Gen6 : Type where
  | alpha : Gen6
  | pi    : Gen6
  | gamma : Gen6
  | eta   : Gen6
  | zeta  : Gen6   -- the extra generator
  | omega : Gen6
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open Gen6
doc_comment: /-- A hypothetical 6-generator alphabet: α, π, γ, η, ζ, ω. -/

name: Gen6.toNat
source_excerpt:
def Gen6.toNat : Gen6 → Nat
  | alpha => 0
  | pi    => 1
  | gamma => 2
  | eta   => 3
  | zeta  => 4
  | omega => 5
doc_comment: /-- Canonical ordering: α=0, π=1, γ=2, η=3, ζ=4, ω=5. -/

name: Obj6
source_excerpt:
structure Obj6 where
  seed : Gen6
  depth : Nat
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment: /-- Objects of the 6-generator system: (seed, depth) pairs. -/

name: rho6
source_excerpt:
def rho6 (x : Obj6) : Obj6 :=
  match x.seed with
  | Gen6.omega => x
  | _ => ⟨x.seed, x.depth + 1⟩
doc_comment: /-- The progression operator ρ₆: fixes ω-fiber, increments depth otherwise. -/

name: K1_six
source_excerpt:
theorem K1_six : Gen6.toNat alpha < Gen6.toNat pi ∧
    Gen6.toNat pi < Gen6.toNat gamma ∧
    Gen6.toNat gamma < Gen6.toNat eta ∧
    Gen6.toNat eta < Gen6.toNat zeta ∧
    Gen6.toNat zeta < Gen6.toNat omega := by
  decide
doc_comment: /-- K1₆: The generators are strictly ordered. -/

name: K2_six
source_excerpt:
theorem K2_six (d : Nat) : rho6 ⟨omega, d⟩ = ⟨omega, d⟩ := by
  rfl
doc_comment: /-- K2₆: ω is the unique fixed point of ρ₆. -/

name: K4_six
source_excerpt:
theorem K4_six (g : Gen6) (hg : g ≠ omega) (d : Nat) :
    rho6 ⟨g, d⟩ = ⟨g, d + 1⟩ := by
  cases g <;> simp [rho6] <;> exact absurd rfl hg
doc_comment: /-- K4₆: ρ₆ increments depth for non-ω generators. -/

name: swap_ez
source_excerpt:
def swap_ez : Gen6 → Gen6
  | eta   => zeta
  | zeta  => eta
  | g     => g
doc_comment: /-- Swap η and ζ, fix everything else. -/

name: swap6
source_excerpt: def swap6 (x : Obj6) : Obj6 := ⟨swap_ez x.seed, x.depth⟩
doc_comment: /-- Lift the generator swap to objects. -/

name: swap_ez_invol
source_excerpt:
theorem swap_ez_invol (g : Gen6) : swap_ez (swap_ez g) = g := by
  cases g <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- swap_ez is an involution on generators. -/

name: swap6_involution
source_excerpt:
theorem swap6_involution (x : Obj6) : swap6 (swap6 x) = x := by
  cases x with | mk s d =>
  simp [swap6, swap_ez_invol]
doc_comment: /-- swap6 is an involution on objects. -/

name: swap6_rho_comm
source_excerpt:
theorem swap6_rho_comm (x : Obj6) : swap6 (rho6 x) = rho6 (swap6 x) := by
  cases x with | mk s d =>
  cases s <;> rfl
doc_comment: /-- swap6 commutes with ρ₆. -/

name: swap6_ne_id
source_excerpt:
theorem swap6_ne_id : swap6 ⟨eta, 0⟩ ≠ ⟨eta, 0⟩ := by
  decide
doc_comment: /-- swap6 is NOT the identity: it moves ⟨η, 0⟩. -/

name: six_gen_rigidity_fails
source_excerpt:
theorem six_gen_rigidity_fails :
    ∃ (f : Obj6 → Obj6),
      (∀ x, f (rho6 x) = rho6 (f x)) ∧
      (∀ x, f (f x) = x) ∧
      ¬(∀ x, f x = x) :=
  ⟨swap6, swap6_rho_comm, swap6_involution, fun h => swap6_ne_id (h _)⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T09a] **Six-Generator Rigidity Failure**:
    A 6-generator tau-like system admits a non-trivial ρ-automorphism.

    The witness is the swap η ↔ ζ, which:
    (1) commutes with ρ₆ (preserves all dynamical structure)
    (2) is an involution (self-inverse, hence bijective)
    (3) is not the identity (moves ⟨η, 0⟩ to ⟨ζ, 0⟩)

    This shows that adding a 6th generator breaks the rigidity
    property Aut(τ) = {id} that holds for exactly 5 generators. -/

name: solenoidal6
source_excerpt: def solenoidal6 : List Gen6 := [pi, gamma, eta, zeta]
doc_comment:
/-- In Gen6, the solenoidal generators are {π, γ, η, ζ} — four of them.
    This is one more than the 3 rewiring levels need, creating the
    η ↔ ζ ambiguity that enables the swap automorphism. -/

name: solenoidal6_count
source_excerpt: theorem solenoidal6_count : solenoidal6.length = 4 := by rfl

name: solenoidal6_surplus
source_excerpt:
theorem solenoidal6_surplus : solenoidal6.length > 3 := by decide

end Tau.Orbit.TooMany
doc_comment: /-- The surplus: 4 solenoidal generators for only 3 rewiring levels. -/

name: bdry_add
source_excerpt: def bdry_add (x y k : TauIdx) : TauIdx := (x + y) % primorial k
doc_comment: /-- Boundary ring element at stage k: a pair of Z/M_kZ values (for add/mul). -/

name: bdry_mul
source_excerpt: def bdry_mul (x y k : TauIdx) : TauIdx := (x * y) % primorial k

name: bdry_neg
source_excerpt: def bdry_neg (x k : TauIdx) : TauIdx := (primorial k - x % primorial k) % primorial k

name: SplitComplex
source_excerpt:
structure SplitComplex where
  re : Int
  im : Int
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

instance : Inhabited SplitComplex := ⟨⟨0, 0⟩⟩
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D27] Split-complex number: a + bj where j² = +1.
    Represented as a pair of integers. -/

name: SplitComplex.zero
source_excerpt: def SplitComplex.zero : SplitComplex := ⟨0, 0⟩
doc_comment: /-- Split-complex zero. -/

name: SplitComplex.one
source_excerpt: def SplitComplex.one : SplitComplex := ⟨1, 0⟩
doc_comment: /-- Split-complex one. -/

name: SplitComplex.j
source_excerpt: def SplitComplex.j : SplitComplex := ⟨0, 1⟩
doc_comment: /-- The split-complex unit j. -/

name: SplitComplex.add
source_excerpt:
def SplitComplex.add (a b : SplitComplex) : SplitComplex :=
  ⟨a.re + b.re, a.im + b.im⟩
doc_comment: /-- Split-complex addition. -/

name: SplitComplex.neg
source_excerpt:
def SplitComplex.neg (a : SplitComplex) : SplitComplex :=
  ⟨-a.re, -a.im⟩
doc_comment: /-- Split-complex negation. -/

name: SplitComplex.mul
source_excerpt:
def SplitComplex.mul (a b : SplitComplex) : SplitComplex :=
  ⟨a.re * b.re + a.im * b.im, a.re * b.im + a.im * b.re⟩
doc_comment:
/-- Split-complex multiplication: (a + bj)(c + dj) = (ac + bd) + (ad + bc)j.
    Uses j² = +1. -/

name: SplitComplex.sub
source_excerpt:
def SplitComplex.sub (a b : SplitComplex) : SplitComplex :=
  a.add b.neg
doc_comment: /-- Split-complex subtraction. -/

name: j_squared
source_excerpt:
theorem j_squared : SplitComplex.mul SplitComplex.j SplitComplex.j = SplitComplex.one := by
  simp [SplitComplex.j, SplitComplex.mul, SplitComplex.one]
doc_comment: /-- j² = 1: the defining property of split-complex numbers. -/

name: SectorPair
source_excerpt:
structure SectorPair where
  b_sector : Int  -- = re + im
  c_sector : Int  -- = re - im
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment:
/-- [I.D27] Sector pair: the isomorphic representation (u, v) = (re + im, re - im).
    In sector coordinates, multiplication is componentwise. -/

name: to_sectors
source_excerpt:
def to_sectors (z : SplitComplex) : SectorPair :=
  ⟨z.re + z.im, z.re - z.im⟩
doc_comment: /-- Convert split-complex to sector representation. -/

name: SectorPair.add
source_excerpt:
def SectorPair.add (a b : SectorPair) : SectorPair :=
  ⟨a.b_sector + b.b_sector, a.c_sector + b.c_sector⟩
doc_comment: /-- Sector addition (componentwise). -/

name: SectorPair.mul
source_excerpt:
def SectorPair.mul (a b : SectorPair) : SectorPair :=
  ⟨a.b_sector * b.b_sector, a.c_sector * b.c_sector⟩
doc_comment: /-- Sector multiplication (componentwise). -/

name: sectors_add
source_excerpt:
theorem sectors_add (a b : SplitComplex) :
    to_sectors (SplitComplex.add a b) =
    SectorPair.add (to_sectors a) (to_sectors b) := by
  simp [to_sectors, SplitComplex.add, SectorPair.add]
  omega
doc_comment: /-- Homomorphism check: to_sectors preserves addition. -/

name: sectors_mul
source_excerpt:
theorem sectors_mul (a b : SplitComplex) :
    to_sectors (SplitComplex.mul a b) =
    SectorPair.mul (to_sectors a) (to_sectors b) := by
  simp only [to_sectors, SplitComplex.mul, SectorPair.mul, SectorPair.mk.injEq]
  constructor <;> ring
doc_comment: /-- Homomorphism check: to_sectors preserves multiplication. -/

name: e_plus_sector
source_excerpt: def e_plus_sector : SectorPair := ⟨1, 0⟩
doc_comment:
/-- The B-sector idempotent e+ in sector coordinates: (1, 0).
    In split-complex coordinates: e+ = (1+j)/2 (defined over Z[1/2]). -/

name: e_minus_sector
source_excerpt: def e_minus_sector : SectorPair := ⟨0, 1⟩
doc_comment: /-- The C-sector idempotent e- in sector coordinates: (0, 1). -/

name: e_plus_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem e_plus_idem : SectorPair.mul e_plus_sector e_plus_sector = e_plus_sector := by
  simp [e_plus_sector, SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- e+² = e+ (idempotent). -/

name: e_minus_idem
source_excerpt:
theorem e_minus_idem : SectorPair.mul e_minus_sector e_minus_sector = e_minus_sector := by
  simp [e_minus_sector, SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- e-² = e- (idempotent). -/

name: e_orthogonal
source_excerpt:
theorem e_orthogonal :
    SectorPair.mul e_plus_sector e_minus_sector = ⟨0, 0⟩ := by
  simp [e_plus_sector, e_minus_sector, SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- e+ · e- = 0 (orthogonal). -/

name: e_partition
source_excerpt:
theorem e_partition :
    SectorPair.add e_plus_sector e_minus_sector = ⟨1, 1⟩ := by
  simp [e_plus_sector, e_minus_sector, SectorPair.add]
doc_comment: /-- e+ + e- = 1 (partition of unity). -/

name: GaussInt
source_excerpt:
structure GaussInt where
  re : Int
  im : Int
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
doc_comment:
/-- An "elliptic" number: a + bi where i² = -1.
    We represent as integer pairs (Gaussian integers). -/

name: GaussInt.mul
doc_comment:
/-- Gaussian integer multiplication: (a+bi)(c+di) = (ac-bd) + (ad+bc)i.
    Uses i² = -1. -/

name: GaussInt.ext
source_excerpt:
theorem GaussInt.ext {a b : GaussInt} (hre : a.re = b.re) (him : a.im = b.im) : a = b := by
  cases a; cases b; simp_all

name: int_no_zero_div
source_excerpt:
private theorem int_no_zero_div {a b : Int} (h : a * b = 0) : a = 0 ∨ b = 0 := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos a.natAbs with ha | ha
  · left; exact Int.natAbs_eq_zero.mp ha
  · right
    have h_abs : a.natAbs * b.natAbs = 0 := by
      rw [← Int.natAbs_mul]; exact Int.natAbs_eq_zero.mpr h
    have hb : b.natAbs = 0 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b.natAbs with hb | hb
      · exact hb
      · exfalso; have := Nat.mul_pos ha hb; omega
    exact Int.natAbs_eq_zero.mp hb
doc_comment: /-- Helper: Int is an integral domain (proved via natAbs). -/

name: no_elliptic_idempotent
source_excerpt:
theorem no_elliptic_idempotent (z : GaussInt)
    (h : GaussInt.mul z z = z) :
    z = ⟨0, 0⟩ ∨ z = ⟨1, 0⟩ := by
  -- Extract component equations
  have hR : z.re * z.re - z.im * z.im = z.re := by
    have := congrArg GaussInt.re h; simp [GaussInt.mul] at this; exact this
  have hI : z.im * z.re + z.im * z.re = z.im := by
    have := congrArg GaussInt.im h; simp [GaussInt.mul] at this
    rw [Int.mul_comm z.re z.im] at this; exact this
  -- Factor IM equation: z.im * (z.re + z.re - 1) = 0
  have him_factor : z.im * (z.re + z.re - 1) = 0 := by linear_combination hI
  -- Int integral domain: z.im = 0 or z.re + z.re = 1 (impossible)
  rcases int_no_zero_div him_factor with hb | hab
  · -- z.im = 0: then z.re² = z.re
    rw [hb] at hR; simp at hR
    -- hR: z.re * z.re = z.re
    have hre_factor : z.re * (z.re - 1) = 0 := by linear_combination hR
    rcases int_no_zero_div hre_factor with ha | ha
    · left; exact GaussInt.ext ha hb
    · right
      have hre1 : z.re = 1 := by omega
      exact GaussInt.ext hre1 hb
  · -- z.re + z.re = 1: impossible in ℤ (parity)
    exfalso; omega
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T10] No nontrivial idempotent in the Gaussian integers:
    if (a+bi)² = (a+bi) over Z, then (a,b) = (0,0) or (a,b) = (1,0).

    Proof: From (a+bi)² = a+bi:
    - Real part: a² - b² = a
    - Imaginary part: 2ab = b
    From 2ab = b: either b = 0 or 2a = 1 (impossible in Z).
    If b = 0: a² = a, so a(a-1) = 0, hence a = 0 or a = 1. -/

name: split_complex_forced
source_excerpt:
theorem split_complex_forced :
    -- Split-complex has nontrivial idempotent
    (∃ e : SectorPair, SectorPair.mul e e = e ∧ e ≠ ⟨0, 0⟩ ∧ e ≠ ⟨1, 1⟩) ∧
    -- Elliptic has NO nontrivial idempotent
    (∀ z : GaussInt, GaussInt.mul z z = z → z = ⟨0, 0⟩ ∨ z = ⟨1, 0⟩) := by
  constructor
  · -- Witness: e_plus_sector = (1, 0)
    exact ⟨e_plus_sector, e_plus_idem, by simp [e_plus_sector], by simp [e_plus_sector]⟩
  · exact no_elliptic_idempotent
doc_comment:
/-- [I.T10] Split-complex forced: the split-complex algebra (j² = +1) admits
    nontrivial idempotents (e+, e-), while the elliptic algebra (i² = -1) does not.
    Therefore, encoding a bipolar partition requires j² = +1. -/

name: polarity_inv
source_excerpt: def polarity_inv (z : SplitComplex) : SplitComplex := ⟨z.re, -z.im⟩
doc_comment: /-- The polarity involution σ: j ↦ -j, i.e., (a, b) ↦ (a, -b). -/

name: polarity_inv_squared
source_excerpt:
theorem polarity_inv_squared (z : SplitComplex) :
    polarity_inv (polarity_inv z) = z := by
  simp [polarity_inv]

name: polarity_inv_fixes_real
source_excerpt:
theorem polarity_inv_fixes_real (a : Int) :
    polarity_inv ⟨a, 0⟩ = ⟨a, 0⟩ := by
  simp [polarity_inv]
doc_comment: /-- σ fixes the real part. -/

name: polarity_inv_j
source_excerpt:
theorem polarity_inv_j :
    polarity_inv SplitComplex.j = SplitComplex.neg SplitComplex.j := by
  simp [polarity_inv, SplitComplex.j, SplitComplex.neg]

name: polarity_inv_swaps_sectors
source_excerpt:
theorem polarity_inv_swaps_sectors (z : SplitComplex) :
    to_sectors (polarity_inv z) =
    ⟨(to_sectors z).c_sector, (to_sectors z).b_sector⟩ := by
  simp [polarity_inv, to_sectors]
  omega
doc_comment: /-- σ swaps sectors: σ maps (u, v) to (v, u) in sector coordinates. -/

name: chi_split
source_excerpt:
def chi_split (p N : TauIdx) : SectorPair :=
  if polarity_chi p N == -1 then e_plus_sector      -- B-dominant → B-sector
  else if polarity_chi p N == 1 then e_minus_sector  -- C-dominant → C-sector
  else ⟨0, 0⟩                                        -- non-prime
doc_comment:
/-- [chunk_0228] Split-complex lift of the polarity character.
    Maps the Int-valued polarity_chi to sector idempotents:
    - B-dominant (chi = -1) → e_plus_sector = (1, 0)
    - C-dominant (chi = +1) → e_minus_sector = (0, 1)
    - non-prime (chi = 0)   → (0, 0)
    Ground truth: chunk_0228_M002194 — χ̃(p) ∈ {e⁻, e⁺}. -/

name: chi_split_idempotent
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_split_idempotent (p N : TauIdx) :
    SectorPair.mul (chi_split p N) (chi_split p N) = chi_split p N := by
  unfold chi_split
  split
  · exact e_plus_idem
  · split
    · exact e_minus_idem
    · simp [SectorPair.mul]
doc_comment: /-- chi_split is idempotent-valued: the output squares to itself. -/

name: chi_split_of_b
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_split_of_b (p N : TauIdx) (h : polarity_chi p N = -1) :
    chi_split p N = e_plus_sector := by
  simp [chi_split, h]
doc_comment: /-- Bridge theorem: polarity_chi = -1 implies chi_split = e_plus_sector. -/

name: chi_split_of_c
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_split_of_c (p N : TauIdx) (h : polarity_chi p N = 1) :
    chi_split p N = e_minus_sector := by
  simp [chi_split, h]
doc_comment: /-- Bridge theorem: polarity_chi = +1 implies chi_split = e_minus_sector. -/

name: chi_split_orthogonal
source_excerpt:
theorem chi_split_orthogonal (p q N : TauIdx)
    (hp : polarity_chi p N = -1) (hq : polarity_chi q N = 1) :
    SectorPair.mul (chi_split p N) (chi_split q N) = ⟨0, 0⟩ := by
  rw [chi_split_of_b p N hp, chi_split_of_c q N hq]
  exact e_orthogonal
doc_comment:
/-- The two character representations are orthogonal:
    chi_split for B-dominant and C-dominant primes give orthogonal sectors. -/

name: coprime_product
source_excerpt:
theorem coprime_product {a b c : Nat}
    (hac : Nat.Coprime a c) (hbc : Nat.Coprime b c) :
    Nat.Coprime (a * b) c := by
  by_contra hne
  -- gcd(a*b, c) ≥ 2
  have hne0 : Nat.gcd (a * b) c ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    apply hne
    -- gcd = 0 → c = 0
    have hc0 : c = 0 := by
      rcases Nat.gcd_dvd_right (a * b) c with ⟨k, hk⟩
      rw [h0, Nat.zero_mul] at hk; exact hk
    subst hc0
    -- hac : Coprime a 0, hbc : Coprime b 0 — unwrap to gcd form
    have ha : Nat.gcd a 0 = 1 := hac
    have hb : Nat.gcd b 0 = 1 := hbc
    rw [Nat.gcd_zero_right] at ha hb
    show Nat.gcd (a * b) 0 = 1
    rw [Nat.gcd_zero_right, ha, hb]
  have hge2 : Nat.gcd (a * b) c ≥ 2 := by omega
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpdvd⟩ := exists_prime_divisor _ hge2
  have hpab : p ∣ a * b := dvd_trans hpdvd (Nat.gcd_dvd_left _ _)
  have hpc : p ∣ c := dvd_trans hpdvd (Nat.gcd_dvd_right _ _)
  rcases euclid_lemma hp hpab with hpa | hpb
  · -- p | a and p | c → p | gcd(a,c) = 1, but p ≥ 2
    have h1 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) (Nat.dvd_gcd hpa hpc)
    rw [hac] at h1; have := hp.1; simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
  · have h1 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) (Nat.dvd_gcd hpb hpc)
    rw [hbc] at h1; have := hp.1; simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
doc_comment:
/-- coprime(a,c) ∧ coprime(b,c) → coprime(a*b,c).
    Proof by prime factor contradiction using euclid_lemma. -/

name: coprime_product_right
source_excerpt:
theorem coprime_product_right {a b c : Nat}
    (hca : Nat.Coprime c a) (hcb : Nat.Coprime c b) :
    Nat.Coprime c (a * b) :=
  (coprime_product hca.symm hcb.symm).symm
doc_comment: /-- Symmetric form: coprime(c,a) ∧ coprime(c,b) → coprime(c,a*b). -/

name: coprime_primorial_of_coprime_primes
source_excerpt:
private theorem coprime_primorial_of_coprime_primes {m : TauIdx} :
    ∀ {k : TauIdx}, (∀ j, j < k → Nat.Coprime (nth_prime m) (nth_prime (j + 1))) →
    Nat.Coprime (nth_prime m) (primorial k) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    show Nat.gcd (nth_prime m) 1 = 1
    exact Nat.gcd_one_right _
  | succ n ih =>
    intro h
    simp only [primorial]
    apply coprime_product_right
    · exact h n (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega)
    · exact ih (fun j hj => h j (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))
doc_comment: /-- Any prime that is pairwise coprime to all primes in M_k is coprime to M_k. -/

name: prime_coprime_primorial
source_excerpt:
theorem prime_coprime_primorial {k : TauIdx} (hyp : CRTHyp (k + 1)) :
    Nat.Coprime (nth_prime (k + 1)) (primorial k) :=
  coprime_primorial_of_coprime_primes fun j hj =>
    hyp.pairwise_coprime k j
      (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
      (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
      (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
doc_comment: /-- The (k+1)-th prime is coprime to the k-th primorial. -/

name: cofactor_exact
source_excerpt:
theorem cofactor_exact {k i : TauIdx} (hi : i + 1 ≤ k) :
    primorial k / nth_prime (i + 1) * nth_prime (i + 1) = primorial k :=
  Nat.div_mul_cancel (nth_prime_dvd_primorial hi)
doc_comment: /-- Exact division: cofactor * p_{i+1} = M_k. -/

name: cofactor_coprime
source_excerpt:
theorem cofactor_coprime : ∀ {k i : TauIdx}, i < k → CRTHyp k →
    Nat.Coprime (primorial k / nth_prime (i + 1)) (nth_prime (i + 1)) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro i hi; exact absurd hi (Nat.not_succ_le_zero i)
  | succ n ih =>
    intro i hi hyp
    simp only [primorial]
    rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp hi) with heq | hlt
    · -- i = n: cofactor = (p_{n+1} * M_n) / p_{n+1} = M_n
      rw [heq, Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by
        have := nth_prime_pos (show n + 1 ≥ 1 by omega)
        simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)]
      exact (prime_coprime_primorial hyp).symm
    · -- i < n: cofactor = p_{n+1} * (M_n / p_{i+1})
      have hi_n : i + 1 ≤ n := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
      rw [Nat.mul_div_assoc _ (nth_prime_dvd_primorial hi_n)]
      apply coprime_product
      · -- Coprime p_{n+1} p_{i+1}
        exact hyp.pairwise_coprime n i
          (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
          (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
          (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
      · -- Coprime (M_n/p_{i+1}) p_{i+1}: IH
        exact ih (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
          ⟨fun j hj => hyp.all_prime j (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega),
           fun j l hj hl hjl => hyp.pairwise_coprime j l
             (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega) (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega) hjl⟩
doc_comment: /-- Key induction: the primorial cofactor M_k/p_{i+1} is coprime to p_{i+1}. -/

name: other_prime_dvd_cofactor
source_excerpt:
theorem other_prime_dvd_cofactor {k i j : TauIdx}
    (hi : i < k) (hj : j < k) (hne : i ≠ j) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    nth_prime (j + 1) ∣ primorial k / nth_prime (i + 1) := by
  have hjdvd := nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show j + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
  rw [← cofactor_exact (show i + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)] at hjdvd
  have hp_j := hyp.all_prime j hj
  rcases euclid_lemma hp_j hjdvd with h | h
  · exact h
  · -- p_{j+1} | p_{i+1}: contradiction
    exfalso
    have hcop := hyp.pairwise_coprime j i hj hi (Ne.symm hne)
    -- p_{j+1} | p_{i+1} and gcd(p_{j+1}, p_{i+1}) = 1, but p_{j+1} ≥ 2
    have hle := Nat.le_of_dvd
      (by have := (hyp.all_prime i hi).1; simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
      (Nat.dvd_gcd ⟨1, (Nat.mul_one _).symm⟩ h)
    rw [hcop] at hle
    have := hp_j.1; simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
doc_comment: /-- p_{j+1} divides the cofactor M_k/p_{i+1} when j ≠ i (both < k). -/

name: mul_mod_eq_zero_of_dvd
source_excerpt:
private theorem mul_mod_eq_zero_of_dvd {a b c : Nat} (h : a ∣ b) :
    (b * c) % a = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_mod_right]
doc_comment: /-- Helper: if a ∣ b then (b * c) % a = 0. -/

name: crt_basis_diagonal
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_basis_diagonal {k i : TauIdx} (hi : i < k) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    crt_basis k i % nth_prime (i + 1) = 1 := by
  simp only [crt_basis]
  -- (cofactor * mod_inv cofactor pi) % M_k % pi
  -- Step 1: % M_k % pi = % pi (since pi | M_k)
  rw [mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _
    (nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show i + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))]
  -- Step 2: mod_inv_correct gives (cofactor * mod_inv cofactor pi) % pi = 1
  exact mod_inv_correct _ _
    (cofactor_coprime hi hyp)
    (by have := (hyp.all_prime i hi).1; simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
doc_comment: /-- e_i ≡ 1 (mod p_{i+1}): diagonal case of CRT basis orthogonality. -/

name: crt_basis_off_diagonal
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_basis_off_diagonal {k i j : TauIdx}
    (hi : i < k) (hj : j < k) (hne : i ≠ j) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    crt_basis k i % nth_prime (j + 1) = 0 := by
  simp only [crt_basis]
  -- Step 1: % M_k % pj = % pj
  rw [mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _
    (nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show j + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))]
  -- Step 2: pj | cofactor, so (cofactor * anything) % pj = 0
  exact mul_mod_eq_zero_of_dvd (other_prime_dvd_cofactor hi hj hne hyp)
doc_comment: /-- e_i ≡ 0 (mod p_{j+1}) for j ≠ i: off-diagonal case. -/

source_excerpt:
example : crt_basis 5 0 % nth_prime 1 = 1 :=
  crt_basis_diagonal (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) crt_hyp_5

example : crt_basis 5 2 % nth_prime 3 = 1 :=
  crt_basis_diagonal (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) crt_hyp_5

example : crt_basis 5 4 % nth_prime 5 = 1 :=
  crt_basis_diagonal (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) crt_hyp_5

example : crt_basis 5 0 % nth_prime 2 = 0 :=
  crt_basis_off_diagonal (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega)
    (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) crt_hyp_5
doc_comment: -- Off-diagonal: formal

source_excerpt:
example : crt_basis 5 3 % nth_prime 1 = 0 :=
  crt_basis_off_diagonal (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega)
    (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega) crt_hyp_5

name: dvd_of_mod_eq_zero
source_excerpt:
private theorem dvd_of_mod_eq_zero {a m : Nat} (h : a % m = 0) : m ∣ a := by
  have := Nat.div_add_mod a m; rw [h, Nat.add_zero] at this
  exact ⟨a / m, this.symm⟩
doc_comment: /-- If a % m = 0 then m ∣ a. -/

name: mod_eq_zero_of_dvd'
source_excerpt:
private theorem mod_eq_zero_of_dvd' {a m : Nat} (h : m ∣ a) : a % m = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h; exact Nat.mul_mod_right m k
doc_comment: /-- If m ∣ a then a % m = 0. -/

name: coprime_mul_dvd
source_excerpt:
theorem coprime_mul_dvd {p q n : Nat} (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q)
    (hp : p ∣ n) (hq : q ∣ n) : p * q ∣ n := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hp
  have : q ∣ k := hcop.symm.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left hq
  obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := this
  exact ⟨j, by rw [Nat.mul_assoc]⟩
doc_comment: /-- Coprime divisibility product: gcd(p,q)=1, p∣n, q∣n → p*q∣n. -/

name: mod_sub_eq_zero
source_excerpt:
private theorem mod_sub_eq_zero {a b m : Nat} (hab : a ≥ b) (h : a % m = b % m) :
    (a - b) % m = 0 := by
  by_cases hm : m = 0
  · subst hm; simp at h; omega
  · have hm_pos : m > 0 := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hm
    have key : (b + (a - b)) % m = b % m := by rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' hab, h]
    rw [Nat.add_mod] at key
    have hr := Nat.mod_lt b hm_pos
    have hd := Nat.mod_lt (a - b) hm_pos
    -- key : (b%m + (a-b)%m) % m = b%m, with b%m < m and (a-b)%m < m
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (b % m + (a - b) % m) m with h1 | h1
    · rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h1] at key; omega
    · have h2 : b % m + (a - b) % m < m + m := by omega
      rw [Nat.mod_eq_sub_mod h1, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)] at key; omega
doc_comment: /-- a ≥ b and a%m = b%m implies (a-b)%m = 0. -/

name: mod_eq_of_sub_eq_zero
source_excerpt:
private theorem mod_eq_of_sub_eq_zero {a b m : Nat} (hab : a ≥ b)
    (h : (a - b) % m = 0) : a % m = b % m := by
  by_cases hm : m = 0
  · subst hm; simp at h; omega
  · -- (a-b)%m = 0 → a-b = m*q → a = m*q + b → a%m = b%m
    have hk := Nat.div_add_mod (a - b) m
    rw [h, Nat.add_zero] at hk
    -- hk : m * ((a-b)/m) = a - b
    conv_lhs => rw [show a = m * ((a - b) / m) + b from by omega]
    rw [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod_right, Nat.zero_add,
      mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _ ⟨1, (Nat.mul_one _).symm⟩]
doc_comment: /-- (a-b)%m = 0 and a ≥ b implies a%m = b%m. -/

name: mod_eq_of_coprime_mod_eq
source_excerpt:
private theorem mod_eq_of_coprime_mod_eq {a b p q : Nat}
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q)
    (hp : a % p = b % p) (hq : a % q = b % q) :
    a % (p * q) = b % (p * q) := by
  rcases Nat.le_total a b with hab | hba
  · exact (mod_eq_of_sub_eq_zero hab
      (mod_eq_zero_of_dvd' (coprime_mul_dvd hcop
        (dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (mod_sub_eq_zero hab hp.symm))
        (dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (mod_sub_eq_zero hab hq.symm))))).symm
  · exact mod_eq_of_sub_eq_zero hba
      (mod_eq_zero_of_dvd' (coprime_mul_dvd hcop
        (dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (mod_sub_eq_zero hba hp))
        (dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (mod_sub_eq_zero hba hq))))
doc_comment: /-- Two-modulus CRT uniqueness step. -/

name: crt_unique_mod
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_unique_mod : ∀ {k : TauIdx}, CRTHyp k →
    ∀ {a b : TauIdx},
    (∀ l, l < k → a % nth_prime (l + 1) = b % nth_prime (l + 1)) →
    a % primorial k = b % primorial k := by
  intro k; induction k with
  | zero => intro _ _ _ _; simp only [primorial, Nat.mod_one]
  | succ n ih =>
    intro hyp a b h
    simp only [primorial]
    apply mod_eq_of_coprime_mod_eq (prime_coprime_primorial hyp)
    · exact h n (by simp only [TauIdx]; omega)
    · exact ih
        ⟨fun j hj => hyp.all_prime j (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega),
         fun j l hj hl hjl => hyp.pairwise_coprime j l
           (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)
           (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega) hjl⟩
        (fun l hl => h l (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))
doc_comment:
/-- CRT uniqueness: pointwise agreement at each prime implies agreement
    modulo the primorial. -/

source_excerpt:
example : ∀ a b, (∀ l, l < 5 → a % nth_prime (l + 1) = b % nth_prime (l + 1)) →
    a % primorial 5 = b % primorial 5 :=
  fun _ _ h => crt_unique_mod crt_hyp_5 h
doc_comment: -- Formal smoke test: CRT uniqueness at depth 5

name: crt_decompose_getD
source_excerpt:
private theorem crt_decompose_getD {x k l : TauIdx} (hl : l < k) :
    (crt_decompose x k).getD l 0 = x % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
  simp only [crt_decompose, List.getD, List.getElem?_map,
    List.getElem?_range hl, Option.map, Option.getD_some]
doc_comment: /-- Helper: crt_decompose x k has l-th element = x % p_{l+1} when l < k. -/

name: crt_reconstruct_go_lt
source_excerpt:
private theorem crt_reconstruct_go_lt (residues : List TauIdx) (k : TauIdx)
    (hk : primorial k > 0) :
    ∀ (i fuel : Nat) (acc : TauIdx), acc < primorial k →
    crt_reconstruct_go residues k i fuel acc < primorial k := by
  intro i fuel
  induction fuel generalizing i with
  | zero => intro acc hacc; unfold crt_reconstruct_go; simp; exact hacc
  | succ n ih =>
    intro acc hacc
    unfold crt_reconstruct_go
    simp only [Nat.succ_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    split
    · exact hacc
    · exact ih (i + 1) _ (Nat.mod_lt _ hk)
doc_comment: /-- crt_reconstruct_go result < primorial k when acc < primorial k. -/

name: crt_reconstruct_lt
source_excerpt:
private theorem crt_reconstruct_lt {k : TauIdx} (residues : List TauIdx)
    (hk : primorial k > 0) :
    crt_reconstruct residues k < primorial k := by
  simp only [crt_reconstruct]
  exact crt_reconstruct_go_lt residues k hk 0 k 0 hk
doc_comment: /-- crt_reconstruct result < primorial k. -/

name: add_mul_basis_off_diag
source_excerpt:
private theorem add_mul_basis_off_diag {acc r k i l : TauIdx}
    (hi : i < k) (hl : l < k) (hne : i ≠ l) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    (acc + r * crt_basis k i) % nth_prime (l + 1) = acc % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
  have h0 : crt_basis k i % nth_prime (l + 1) = 0 := crt_basis_off_diagonal hi hl hne hyp
  have h1 : (r * crt_basis k i) % nth_prime (l + 1) = 0 := by
    rw [Nat.mul_mod, h0, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.zero_mod]
  rw [Nat.add_mod, h1, Nat.add_zero,
    mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _ ⟨1, (Nat.mul_one _).symm⟩]
doc_comment: /-- Off-diagonal: adding r * e_i doesn't change result mod p_{l+1}. -/

name: add_mul_basis_diag
source_excerpt:
private theorem add_mul_basis_diag {acc r k i : TauIdx}
    (hi : i < k) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    (acc + r * crt_basis k i) % nth_prime (i + 1) = (acc + r) % nth_prime (i + 1) := by
  have h1 : crt_basis k i % nth_prime (i + 1) = 1 := crt_basis_diagonal hi hyp
  rw [Nat.add_mod acc (r * _), Nat.mul_mod, h1, Nat.mul_one,
    mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _ ⟨1, (Nat.mul_one _).symm⟩, ← Nat.add_mod]
doc_comment: /-- Diagonal: adding r * e_i changes result mod p_{i+1} by r. -/

name: add_mod_primorial
source_excerpt:
private theorem add_mod_primorial {a b k l : TauIdx}
    (hl : l < k) :
    (a % primorial k + b) % nth_prime (l + 1) = (a + b) % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
  rw [Nat.add_mod, mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _
    (nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show l + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega)),
    ← Nat.add_mod]
doc_comment: /-- Reducing mod M_k is invisible mod p_{l+1}. -/

name: crt_reconstruct_go_mod_prime
source_excerpt:
private theorem crt_reconstruct_go_mod_prime
    {k l : TauIdx} (residues : List TauIdx) (hl : l < k) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    ∀ (i fuel : Nat) (acc : TauIdx), i ≤ k → fuel ≥ k - i →
    crt_reconstruct_go residues k i fuel acc % nth_prime (l + 1) =
    (acc + if l ≥ i then residues.getD l 0 else 0) % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
  intro i fuel
  induction fuel generalizing i with
  | zero =>
    intro acc hi hfuel
    have hik : i = k := by omega
    unfold crt_reconstruct_go; simp
    rw [hik]
    have hlk : ¬(l ≥ k) := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
    simp [hlk]
  | succ n ih =>
    intro acc hi hfuel
    unfold crt_reconstruct_go
    simp only [Nat.succ_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    split
    · -- i ≥ k: returns acc
      rename_i hige
      have hlti : ¬(l ≥ i) := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
      simp [hlti]
    · -- i < k: take one step
      rename_i hige
      have hilt : i < k := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
      -- Simplify fuel: n + 1 - 1 = n (clear afterward to not confuse omega)
      have hfuel_simp : n + 1 - 1 = n := by omega
      rw [hfuel_simp]; clear hfuel_simp
      -- Apply IH at i+1
      rw [ih (i + 1) _ (by omega) (by omega)]
      -- Clear hfuel (Nat subtraction confuses omega)
      clear hfuel
      -- Goal: (acc' + if l ≥ i+1 ...) % p = (acc + if l ≥ i ...) % p
      -- where acc' = (acc + r_i * e_i) % M_k
      by_cases hli : l = i
      · -- Diagonal: l = i (subst eliminates i, keeps l)
        subst hli
        rw [if_neg (show ¬(l ≥ l + 1) from by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega), Nat.add_zero,
          if_pos (Nat.le_refl l)]
        -- Goal: ((acc + rl * el) % Mk) % p = (acc + rl) % p
        rw [mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _
          (nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show l + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))]
        exact add_mul_basis_diag hilt hyp
      · by_cases hlti : l < i
        · -- l < i: both ifs are false
          rw [if_neg (show ¬(l ≥ i + 1) from by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega),
            if_neg (show ¬(l ≥ i) from by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega),
            Nat.add_zero, Nat.add_zero]
          rw [mod_mod_of_dvd _ _ _
            (nth_prime_dvd_primorial (show l + 1 ≤ k by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega))]
          exact add_mul_basis_off_diag hilt hl
            (by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega) hyp
        · -- l > i: both ifs are true, same residue
          have hlgei1 : l ≥ i + 1 := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
          have hlgei : l ≥ i := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
          have hne_il : i ≠ l := by simp only [TauIdx] at *; omega
          rw [if_pos hlgei1, if_pos hlgei]
          -- Goal: ((acc + ri*ei) % Mk + rl) % p = (acc + rl) % p
          rw [add_mod_primorial hl]
          -- Rearrange: acc + ri*ei + rl = (acc + rl) + ri*ei
          rw [Nat.add_assoc,
            Nat.add_comm (residues.getD i 0 * crt_basis k i) (residues.getD l 0),
            ← Nat.add_assoc]
          exact add_mul_basis_off_diag hilt hl hne_il hyp
doc_comment:
/-- Accumulator invariant: crt_reconstruct_go modulo p_{l+1} picks up exactly
    the l-th residue (all other contributions vanish by basis orthogonality). -/

name: crt_roundtrip_formal
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_roundtrip_formal {x k : TauIdx} (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose x k) k = x % primorial k := by
  -- Strategy: show both sides agree mod each prime, then apply CRT uniqueness.
  have h_agree : ∀ l, l < k →
      crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose x k) k % nth_prime (l + 1) =
      x % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
    intro l hl
    simp only [crt_reconstruct]
    rw [crt_reconstruct_go_mod_prime _ hl hyp 0 k 0 (Nat.zero_le k) (by omega)]
    simp only [Nat.zero_le, ↓reduceIte, Nat.zero_add]
    -- Goal: (crt_decompose x k).getD l 0 % p_{l+1} = x % p_{l+1}
    rw [crt_decompose_getD hl]
    -- Goal: x % p_{l+1} % p_{l+1} = x % p_{l+1}
    exact mod_mod_of_dvd x _ _ ⟨1, (Nat.mul_one _).symm⟩
  -- CRT uniqueness gives agreement mod M_k
  have h_mod := crt_unique_mod hyp h_agree
  -- h_mod : crt_reconstruct ... % M_k = x % M_k
  -- LHS is already < M_k, so % M_k is a no-op
  rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (crt_reconstruct_lt _ (primorial_pos k))] at h_mod
  exact h_mod
doc_comment: /-- CRT round-trip: reconstruct ∘ decompose = id (mod M_k). -/

source_excerpt:
example : crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose 42 5) 5 = 42 % primorial 5 :=
  crt_roundtrip_formal crt_hyp_5
doc_comment: -- Formal smoke tests

source_excerpt:
example : crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose 100 5) 5 = 100 % primorial 5 :=
  crt_roundtrip_formal crt_hyp_5

example : crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose 0 5) 5 = 0 % primorial 5 :=

name: crt_reconstruct_mod_prime
source_excerpt:
theorem crt_reconstruct_mod_prime {k l : TauIdx} (residues : List TauIdx)
    (hl : l < k) (hyp : CRTHyp k) :
    crt_reconstruct residues k % nth_prime (l + 1) =
    residues.getD l 0 % nth_prime (l + 1) := by
  simp only [crt_reconstruct]
  rw [crt_reconstruct_go_mod_prime _ hl hyp 0 k 0 (Nat.zero_le k) (by omega)]
  simp only [Nat.zero_le, ↓reduceIte, Nat.zero_add]

end Tau.Polarity
doc_comment:
/-- CRT projection: crt_reconstruct residues k mod p_{l+1} = residues[l] mod p_{l+1}.
    This is the key interface theorem for downstream formal proofs
    (Teichmüller retraction, orthogonality, etc.). -/

name: mod_inv_go
doc_comment:
/-- Find modular inverse of a mod m by brute-force search.
    Returns x such that (a * x) % m = 1, or 0 if not found. -/

name: mod_inv
source_excerpt: def mod_inv (a m : Nat) : Nat := mod_inv_go a m 1 m
doc_comment: /-- Modular inverse: a⁻¹ mod m. Correct for coprime a, m with m > 1. -/

name: mod_inv_go_correct
source_excerpt:
theorem mod_inv_go_correct (a m x fuel : Nat)
    (h_exists : ∃ y, x ≤ y ∧ y < x + fuel ∧ (a * y) % m = 1) :
    (a * mod_inv_go a m x fuel) % m = 1 := by
  induction fuel generalizing x with
  | zero =>
    obtain ⟨y, _, hy_lt, _⟩ := h_exists; omega
  | succ n ih =>
    unfold mod_inv_go
    simp only [Nat.succ_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    split
    · rename_i heq; exact beq_iff_eq.mp heq
    · rename_i hne
      apply ih
      obtain ⟨y, hxy, hy_lt, hy_mod⟩ := h_exists
      refine ⟨y, ?_, by omega, hy_mod⟩
      rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hxy with rfl | hlt
      · exfalso; exact (beq_iff_eq.not.mp hne) hy_mod
      · omega
doc_comment: /-- mod_inv_go finds a valid inverse when one exists in range. -/

name: mod_inv_correct
source_excerpt:
theorem mod_inv_correct (a m : Nat) (hcop : Nat.Coprime a m) (hm : m > 1) :
    (a * mod_inv a m) % m = 1 := by
  unfold mod_inv
  apply mod_inv_go_correct
  obtain ⟨x, hx_lt, hx_mod⟩ := mod_inv_exists a m hcop hm
  have hx1 : x ≥ 1 := by
    rcases x with _ | x
    · -- x = 0: (a * 0) % m = 0 % m = 0 ≠ 1
      simp at hx_mod
    · exact Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le x)
  exact ⟨x, hx1, by omega, hx_mod⟩
doc_comment: /-- mod_inv is correct for coprime inputs with m > 1. -/

name: crt_decompose
source_excerpt:
def crt_decompose (x k : TauIdx) : List TauIdx :=
  (List.range k).map (fun i => x % nth_prime (i + 1))
doc_comment:
/-- CRT forward map: x ↦ (x mod p₁, ..., x mod p_k).
    Returns the list of residues modulo each prime. -/

name: crt_basis
doc_comment:
/-- CRT basis element eᵢ: the unique element of Z/M_kZ with
    eᵢ ≡ 1 (mod pᵢ) and eᵢ ≡ 0 (mod pⱼ) for j ≠ i.
    i is 0-indexed: crt_basis k 0 corresponds to p₁. -/

name: crt_reconstruct_go
source_excerpt:
def crt_reconstruct_go (residues : List TauIdx) (k : TauIdx) (i fuel : Nat)
    (acc : TauIdx) : TauIdx :=
  if fuel = 0 then acc
  else if i ≥ k then acc
  else
    let ri := residues.getD i 0
    let ei := crt_basis k i
    crt_reconstruct_go residues k (i + 1) (fuel - 1) ((acc + ri * ei) % primorial k)
termination_by fuel
doc_comment: /-- CRT reconstruction accumulator: Σ rᵢ · eᵢ mod M_k. -/

name: crt_reconstruct
source_excerpt:
def crt_reconstruct (residues : List TauIdx) (k : TauIdx) : TauIdx :=
  crt_reconstruct_go residues k 0 k 0
doc_comment: /-- CRT inverse map: (r₁,...,r_k) ↦ Σ rᵢ · eᵢ mod M_k. -/

name: crt_basis_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_basis_check (k i j : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  crt_basis k i % nth_prime (j + 1) == (if i == j then 1 else 0)
doc_comment: /-- CRT basis orthogonality: eᵢ mod pⱼ = δᵢⱼ. -/

name: crt_roundtrip_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_roundtrip_check (x k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  crt_reconstruct (crt_decompose x k) k == x % primorial k
doc_comment: /-- CRT round-trip: decompose ∘ reconstruct = id (mod M_k). -/

name: crt_coherence_check
doc_comment:
/-- CRT coherence: reducing CRT output from depth l to depth k
    gives the same as CRT at depth k with first k residues. -/

name: crt_exhaustive_check_go
doc_comment: /-- CRT full-range check: round-trip holds for all x in [0, M_k). -/

name: crt_exhaustive_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_exhaustive_check (k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  crt_exhaustive_check_go k 0 (primorial k)

name: crt_idempotent_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_idempotent_check (k i : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  let mk := primorial k
  let ei := crt_basis k i
  (ei * ei) % mk == ei
doc_comment: /-- eᵢ · eᵢ ≡ eᵢ (mod M_k): each basis element is idempotent. -/

name: crt_orthogonal_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_orthogonal_check (k i j : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  i == j || (crt_basis k i * crt_basis k j) % primorial k == 0
doc_comment: /-- eᵢ · eⱼ ≡ 0 (mod M_k) for i ≠ j: distinct basis elements are orthogonal. -/

name: crt_partition_go
doc_comment: /-- Σ eᵢ ≡ 1 (mod M_k): basis elements sum to unity. -/

name: crt_partition_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_partition_check (k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  crt_partition_go k 0 k 0 == 1 % primorial k

name: crt_add_hom_check
source_excerpt:
def crt_add_hom_check (a b k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  let sum_decomp := crt_decompose (a + b) k
  let a_decomp := crt_decompose a k
  let b_decomp := crt_decompose b k
  (List.range k).all (fun i =>
    sum_decomp.getD i 0 == (a_decomp.getD i 0 + b_decomp.getD i 0) % nth_prime (i + 1))
doc_comment: /-- CRT is a ring homomorphism: decompose(a+b) = decompose(a) + decompose(b) mod primes. -/

name: crt_mul_hom_check

def crt_mul_hom_check (a b k : TauIdx) : Bool :=
  let prod_decomp := crt_decompose (a * b) k

  let b_decomp := crt_decompose b k
  (List.range k).all (fun i =>
    prod_decomp.getD i 0 == (a_decomp.getD i 0 * b_decomp.getD i 0) % nth_prime (i + 1))
doc_comment: /-- CRT is a ring homomorphism: decompose(a*b) = decompose(a) * decompose(b) mod primes. -/

name: ext_gcd
doc_comment:
/-- Extended GCD: returns (gcd, s, t) with gcd = Nat.gcd a b
    and ↑a * s + ↑b * t = ↑gcd (Int coefficients). -/

name: ext_gcd_fst
source_excerpt:
theorem ext_gcd_fst (a b : Nat) : (ext_gcd a b).1 = Nat.gcd a b := by
  induction b using Nat.strongRecOn generalizing a with
  | _ b ih =>
  unfold ext_gcd
  split
  · -- b = 0
    rename_i hb; rw [hb, Nat.gcd_zero_right]
  · -- b > 0
    rename_i hb
    simp only []
    have hlt : a % b < b := Nat.mod_lt a (by omega)
    rw [ih (a % b) hlt b]
    -- Goal: Nat.gcd b (a % b) = Nat.gcd a b
    rw [Nat.gcd_comm a b, Nat.gcd_rec b a, Nat.gcd_comm]
doc_comment: /-- ext_gcd computes the GCD. -/

name: ext_gcd_bezout
source_excerpt:
theorem ext_gcd_bezout (a b : Nat) :
    (↑a : Int) * (ext_gcd a b).2.1 + (↑b : Int) * (ext_gcd a b).2.2 =
    ↑(ext_gcd a b).1 := by
  induction b using Nat.strongRecOn generalizing a with
  | _ b ih =>
  unfold ext_gcd
  split
  · -- b = 0: (a, 1, 0). ↑a * 1 + ↑0 * 0 = ↑a ✓
    simp
  · -- b > 0
    rename_i hb
    simp only []
    have hlt : a % b < b := Nat.mod_lt a (by omega)
    have ih' := ih (a % b) hlt b
    -- ih': ↑b * (ext_gcd b (a%b)).2.1 + ↑(a%b) * (ext_gcd b (a%b)).2.2 = ↑(ext_gcd b (a%b)).1
    -- Goal: ↑a * (ext_gcd b (a%b)).2.2 + ↑b * ((ext_gcd b (a%b)).2.1 - ↑(a/b) * (ext_gcd b (a%b)).2.2) = ↑(ext_gcd b (a%b)).1
    set g := (ext_gcd b (a % b)).1
    set x := (ext_gcd b (a % b)).2.1
    set y := (ext_gcd b (a % b)).2.2
    -- Key: a = b * (a/b) + a%b (lifted to Int)
    have hdiv : (↑a : Int) = ↑b * ↑(a / b) + ↑(a % b) := by
      have := Nat.div_add_mod a b; omega
    linear_combination ih' + y * hdiv
doc_comment: /-- Bézout identity: ↑a * s + ↑b * t = ↑(ext_gcd a b).1. -/

name: ext_gcd_spec
source_excerpt:
theorem ext_gcd_spec (a b : Nat) :
    (↑a : Int) * (ext_gcd a b).2.1 + (↑b : Int) * (ext_gcd a b).2.2 =
    ↑(Nat.gcd a b) := by
  rw [← ext_gcd_fst a b]; exact ext_gcd_bezout a b
doc_comment: /-- Combined: ext_gcd gives Bézout coefficients for gcd. -/

name: mod_inv_exists
source_excerpt:
theorem mod_inv_exists (a m : Nat) (hcop : Nat.Coprime a m) (hm : m > 1) :
    ∃ x : Nat, x < m ∧ (a * x) % m = 1 := by
  -- Get Bézout: ↑a * s + ↑m * t = ↑(gcd a m) = 1
  have hbez := ext_gcd_spec a m
  rw [hcop] at hbez
  -- hbez : ↑a * s + ↑m * t = 1
  set s := (ext_gcd a m).2.1
  set t := (ext_gcd a m).2.2
  -- (↑a * s) mod ↑m = 1
  have hm0 : (↑m : Int) ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hm_pos : (↑m : Int) > 0 := by omega
  have has_mod : ((↑a : Int) * s) % (↑m : Int) = 1 := by
    -- (↑a * s + ↑m * t) % ↑m = (↑a * s) % ↑m
    have h1 := Int.add_mul_emod_self_left ((↑a : Int) * s) (↑m : Int) t
    -- h1 : (↑a * s + ↑m * t) % ↑m = (↑a * s) % ↑m
    rw [hbez] at h1
    -- h1 : (1 : Int) % ↑m = (↑a * s) % ↑m
    rw [Int.emod_eq_of_lt (by omega) (by omega)] at h1
    -- h1 : 1 = (↑a * s) % ↑m
    exact h1.symm
  -- Positive representative: x = ((s % m) + m) % m
  let x_int := (s % (↑m : Int) + ↑m) % (↑m : Int)
  have hx_nonneg : x_int ≥ 0 := Int.emod_nonneg _ hm0
  have hx_lt : x_int < (↑m : Int) := Int.emod_lt_of_pos _ hm_pos
  -- x_int = s % ↑m (and hence x_int ≡ s mod m)
  have hx_eq : x_int = s % (↑m : Int) := by
    show (s % (↑m : Int) + ↑m) % (↑m : Int) = s % (↑m : Int)
    have h1 := Int.add_mul_emod_self_left (s % (↑m : Int)) (↑m : Int) 1
    simp only [Int.mul_one] at h1
    rw [h1]; exact Int.emod_emod_of_dvd s ⟨1, by ring⟩
  have hx_mod : ((↑a : Int) * x_int) % (↑m : Int) = 1 := by
    rw [hx_eq, Int.mul_emod (↑a : Int) (s % (↑m : Int)) (↑m : Int),
        Int.emod_emod_of_dvd s ⟨1, by ring⟩, ← Int.mul_emod, has_mod]
  -- Convert to Nat
  use x_int.toNat
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · exact (Int.toNat_lt hx_nonneg).mpr hx_lt
  · have : (↑(a * x_int.toNat) : Int) % (↑m : Int) = 1 := by
      rw [Nat.cast_mul, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hx_nonneg]; exact hx_mod
    exact_mod_cast this
doc_comment: /-- If gcd(a, m) = 1 and m > 1, there exists x < m with (a*x) % m = 1. -/

    chi legendreBClass 3  = Pol 3  ∧

    chi legendreBClass 7  = Pol 7  ∧

    chi legendreBClass 13 = Pol 13 ∧
    chi legendreBClass 17 = Pol 17 ∧
    chi legendreBClass 19 = Pol 19 ∧
    chi legendreBClass 23 = Pol 23 :=
  ⟨chi_legendre_eq_Pol_at_2,

   chi_legendre_eq_Pol_at_5,

name: sectorSigma
source_excerpt:
def sectorSigma (s : SectorPair) : SectorPair :=
  ⟨s.c_sector, s.b_sector⟩

@[simp] theorem sectorSigma_e_plus :
    sectorSigma e_plus = e_minus := rfl

@[simp] theorem sectorSigma_e_minus :
    sectorSigma e_minus = e_plus := rfl

/-
σ-fixedness for SectorPairs note: a SectorPair is σ-fixed iff its
components are equal.  At concrete instances this reduces to
`rfl`-style proofs.  The universal proof would require structure-level
extensionality reasoning that's clunky in this concrete TauLib setting;
we capture σ-fixedness at the four canonical atoms via the theorems
below (sectorSigma_fixed_at_zero / sectorSigma_fixed_at_one) which
suffice for the paper §10 four-atom dictionary structure.
-/

/-- The σ-fixed atoms among the four canonical idempotents are
    exactly `0 = ⟨0, 0⟩` and `1 = ⟨1, 1⟩`. -/
@[simp] theorem sectorSigma_fixed_at_zero :
    sectorSigma (⟨0, 0⟩ : SectorPair) = ⟨0, 0⟩ := rfl

@[simp] theorem sectorSigma_fixed_at_one :
    sectorSigma (⟨1, 1⟩ : SectorPair) = ⟨1, 1⟩ := rfl
doc_comment:
/-- **σ swaps the canonical idempotents at the SectorPair level**.

    Note: `e_plus_sector = ⟨1, 0⟩` and `e_minus_sector = ⟨0, 1⟩`
    in the `SectorPair` representation; the σ-swap exchange
    `e_+ ↔ e_-` corresponds to swapping the b-sector and c-sector
    components. -/

name: four_atom_dictionary

      | Truth4.T => SectorPair.mk 1 1   -- α-total → 1 = e_+ + e_-
      | Truth4.F => SectorPair.mk 0 0   -- α-null → 0 = the zero
      | Truth4.B => e_plus_sector       -- γ → e_+ (B-lobe)
      | Truth4.N => e_minus_sector := by  -- η → e_- (C-lobe)
  cases t <;> rfl

/-- **The four atoms of B_σ(D) realised on Truth4**: each Truth4
    constructor maps to a specific SectorPair element. -/
@[simp] theorem four_atom_T : Truth4.toSectorPair Truth4.T = ⟨1, 1⟩ := rfl
@[simp] theorem four_atom_F : Truth4.toSectorPair Truth4.F = ⟨0, 0⟩ := rfl
@[simp] theorem four_atom_B : Truth4.toSectorPair Truth4.B = e_plus_sector := rfl
@[simp] theorem four_atom_N : Truth4.toSectorPair Truth4.N = e_minus_sector := rfl

/-- **Paper Lemma four-atoms**: the canonical σ-equivariant Boolean

    `{0, e_+, e_-, 1}` at the SectorPair level.
